proved_step:
statement: LEMMA (description-subset and successor bounds for prefix residuals). Let C be a finite set of M descriptions of binary words of fixed length N, and let D_t count distinct residual languages after length-t prefixes. Then D_t <= min(2^M,2^(2^(N-t))) for every t, and D_(t+1)<=2D_t for t<N. Proof: Map each prefix p to A_p, the subset of descriptions whose word begins with p. The residual R_p is determined by A_p, so there are at most 2^M residuals. Each residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) possible suffixes, giving the second bound. For the successor inequality, each level-t residual has at most two successors R_b={u:bu in R}. Conversely, every level-(t+1) residual arises as a successor of the level-t residual for its parent prefix, so there are at most two times as many next-level residuals.
scope: All finite description families of fixed-length binary words; state counts only, no update-time bound.

statement: LEMMA (candidate-circuit filtering update). Fix n,s and a finite enumerated set C of Boolean circuits on n inputs, with M=|C|, each having a fixed output convention. For a prefix p in {0,1}^t define C_p={C in C: C(0),...,C(t-1)=p}. Encode C_p by its M-bit incidence vector z. Given next bit b, the exact update is z'_C=z_C AND [C(t)=b] for every C in C.
proof: For each candidate C, the length-(t+1) prefix agrees with C's output prefix exactly when both (i) the length-t prefix agrees and (ii) C's t-th output equals b. These are respectively z_C=1 and the fixed compatibility bit a_C,b=[C(t)=b]. Thus z'_C=z_C AND a_C,b, coordinatewise, which proves exactness. With fan-in-two AND gates and constants, the update uses at most M gates once the compatibility bits are available; if b is a runtime input, compute each selector using one NOT shared across all coordinates and at most one AND per coordinate, giving at most M+1 gates. The encoding uses M bits. This applies in particular to the set of all circuits of size at most s after choosing a canonical finite encoding and removing duplicate descriptions only if desired; no polynomial-size claim follows because M may be exponential in s log(n+s).
scope: Finite candidate families and fixed-length output prefixes; exact circuit described relative to the precomputed compatibility constants for the chosen family and prefix position. Does not establish a polynomial transition circuit or an MCSP lower bound.

statement: LEMMA (exact backward recurrence and one-bit forward obstruction). Let L be any finite subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N and p in {0,1}^t, define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists q in {0,1}^{N-t} with pq in L. Then for every t<N and every p in {0,1}^t, E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Moreover there is no universal Boolean function g:{0,1}^2->{0,1} such that E_{t+1}(pb)=g(E_t(p),b) for all finite binary languages L, all N,t,p,b.
proof: Every suffix q begins with exactly one bit b in {0,1}; writing q=br, we have pq in L iff pbr in L for some r of length N-t-1. Thus an accepting extension of p exists iff one exists under p0 or p1. For the obstruction take N=2,t=0,p=epsilon,b=0. For L1={00}, E_0(epsilon)=1 and E_1(0)=1; for L2={10}, E_0(epsilon)=1 and E_1(0)=0. The inputs (E_0(epsilon),b) are identical but outputs differ, so no such universal g exists.
scope: All finite binary languages L subseteq {0,1}^N; exact existential prefix extendibility. The obstruction concerns a forward update from only the current extendibility bit and next input bit. It does not rule out richer states, nor establish a lower bound for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

LEMMA (nondeterministic prefix-extension verifier). Fix n>=1, s>=0, and k<=2^n. Given a length-k prefix p of the truth table of a Boolean function on {0,1}^n, the assertion that some fan-in-two circuit of at most s gates computes a function beginning with p has a witness of O(s log(n+s)+k(s+log(n+s))) bits verifiable in time polynomial in n+s+k. Proof: encode the circuit as an ordered list of at most s gate records, each record specifying one gate type and two predecessor indices among the n input nodes, constants, and earlier gates; specify an output node. For each of the k lexicographically first inputs, include the value at every gate. A verifier checks each record's legal predecessor range and gate type, checks every supplied gate value against its two predecessor values under the specified Boolean operation, and checks the output value equals the corresponding bit of p. If the circuit exists, its actual evaluations form an accepting witness. Conversely, acceptance validates a legal circuit and its actual evaluations on all k inputs, so that circuit extends p. For k=0, the prefix is empty and any legal circuit (including a constant output) witnesses extension. This establishes an NP-style certificate/verifier upper bound, not a deterministic polynomial-time transition algorithm.

LEMMA (candidate-set filtering update). Fix n>=1, s>=0 and a fixed finite Boolean gate basis of fan-in at most two, with constants allowed. Let C_{n,s} be the finite set of syntactically valid circuit descriptions of at most s gates on n inputs, each with a designated output, and let N=2^n. For a prefix p of length k in lexicographic truth-table order, define A(p)={C in C_{n,s}: Eval(C) begins with p}. On reading the next bit b (when k<N), A(pb) is exactly {C in A(p): Eval(C)(x_k)=b}, where x_k is the k-th input in that order. Thus storing the candidate circuits as a |C_{n,s}|-bit incidence vector gives an exact deterministic update by testing each surviving circuit on x_k and deleting those with the wrong output. If a circuit has at most s gates, its evaluation on one input takes O(s) gate evaluations, so the update takes O(s|C_{n,s}|) basis operations, plus indexing overhead; with ordinary ordered gate descriptions, |C_{n,s}| <= (c(n+s)^2)^s for a basis-dependent constant c, hence this is at most O(s(c(n+s)^2)^s). Proof: a candidate survives extension by b iff it already agrees with all k prefix positions and its value on the next position is b; this is precisely the displayed filter. Induction on k shows the stored incidence vector equals A(p) after every update. The bound is explicit but generally exponential in s log(n+s), and therefore does not prove a poly(s,n) update or give a transition circuit for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (candidate-mask transition for finite image families). Let C be a finite set of descriptions, N>=1, and E:C->{0,1}^N. For every prefix p of length t<=N define A_p={c in C: E(c)_{1..t}=p}, represented by the |C|-bit incidence vector z_p(c)=1 iff c in A_p. For t<N, on input bit b the exact next mask is z_{pb}(c)=z_p(c) AND [E(c)_{t+1}=b] for each c. Thus at fixed level t the update is coordinatewise AND with constants determined by E,t,b, using at most |C| two-input AND gates (or zero gates if copying and constant wires are free). EXT_E(p):=[A_p is nonempty] is the OR of the mask bits, using at most |C|-1 fan-in-two OR gates when |C|>=1. Proof: c belongs to A_{pb} exactly when c belongs to A_p and its (t+1)-st output bit equals b, which is precisely the coordinatewise conjunction. A_p is nonempty exactly when at least one incidence bit is 1. Implementing each coordinate separately gives the stated gate bound. The hardwired constants may depend on the full table E and level t, so this gives no succinct or uniform construction from an arbitrary circuit C; its workspace is |C| bits, potentially exponential in s log(n+s) for all size-s circuit descriptions.
scope: Finite image families E:C->{0,1}^N; exact prefixes; fixed-level transition circuits with per-description output bits hardwired; fan-in-two AND/OR, with copying/constants free. Upper bound and representation tradeoff only; no lower bound or P!=NP conclusion.

statement: LEMMA (residual-state bound from candidate subsets). Let C be a finite set, N>=0, and E:C->{0,1}^N. Let L={E(c):c in C}, and for each prefix p define R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pu in L}. At every fixed prefix length t, the number D_t of distinct residual languages R_p is at most 2^{|C|}. Proof: associate to p its candidate subset A_p={c in C:E(c) begins with p}. If A_p=A_q, then R_p=R_q: in either case the residual consists exactly of suffixes E(c)_{t+1..N} for c in that common subset. Thus the map A_p -> R_p is well-defined and surjective onto the residuals at level t. There are at most 2^{|C|} subsets of C, so D_t<=2^{|C|}. Moreover, the candidate-mask update of S0416 computes A_{pb} from A_p by coordinatewise filtering. Consequently this representation gives an exact automaton with at most 2^{|C|} states and |C| state bits, with at most |C| AND gates per fixed-level transition under the stated hardwiring model.
scope: Finite image languages L of an explicitly given finite description set C; fixed prefix levels; state transitions may hardwire E(c)_{t+1}. This is a bound in |C|, not in compact circuit size. It provides no polynomial(s,n) workspace or transition-cost bound for EXT and makes no claim about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
scope: Finite image languages L={E(c):c in C}, explicit finite C, fixed-level exact prefix automaton; no compactness or MCSP conclusion.

evidence: The displayed transition formula uses NOT b. In the stated fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gate model, S0399's count omits the gate computing NOT b. One shared inverter repairs the count, as reflected in S0400.

proved_step:
statement: Candidate-set transition lemma for EXT_{n,s}. Fix an enumeration C_1,...,C_K of all descriptions of Boolean circuits on n input variables of size at most s, including a fixed convention for invalid descriptions (which describe no circuit). For each truth-table position j, let e_{i,j} be the output bit of C_i on input j, and let A(p)={i: C_i is valid and its truth table begins with prefix p}. Encode A(p) by K indicator bits z_i. After reading the next bit b at position j, the exact update is z'_i = z_i AND [e_{i,j}=b] for valid descriptions, and z'_i=0 for invalid descriptions. Thus EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff OR_i z_i=1, and one transition is computable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit with at most K+1 gates given the constants [e_{i,j}=b] (one AND per description and a shared OR reduction; the stated bound allows K=1). Proof: By definition, a valid description remains consistent with p concatenated with b exactly when it was consistent with p and its fixed truth-table bit at position j equals b. This is precisely the coordinatewise update. Induction on prefix length establishes that the maintained vector equals A(p) at every step; its OR is therefore 1 exactly when some size-at-most-s circuit extends p. The constants can be precomputed from the circuit descriptions and position j, but this lemma does not bound that preprocessing cost, K, or give an implementation through an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All n>=0 and s>=0 under an explicitly fixed finite circuit-description enumeration and truth-table input order; state width K, transition circuit fan-in two, with position-dependent truth-table constants supplied. This is an exact representation, not a polynomial-in-s streaming algorithm and not a simulation by bounded real-gate operations on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (candidate filtering). Let C_1,...,C_M be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits with truth tables of length N in a fixed order. Store z_i=1 exactly when C_i matches the current prefix. On receiving bit b at position t, update z_i to z_i AND [C_i(t)=b]. This uses at most M fan-in-two AND gates when the position-dependent truth-table bits are supplied. The family contains a circuit matching the prefix exactly when OR_i z_i=1, computable with at most M-1 OR gates for M>=1.
Proof. Initially every circuit matches the empty prefix. If z_i records agreement through position t-1, then z_i AND [C_i(t)=b] is 1 exactly when C_i also agrees at position t, proving the invariant by induction. Taking the OR tests whether any listed circuit matches. Each update is one conjunction with a supplied constant, so the stated gate bound holds.
Scope: This is an exact representation for an explicit finite family. Applying it to padded descriptions of size-at-most-s circuits gives an exponential-size family in general; the lemma establishes no polynomial-in-s transition bound and says nothing about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

LEMMA (explicit candidate-filter automaton for EXT). Fix n>=1 and s>=0, and fix any finite indexed list C_1,...,C_M of Boolean circuits on n inputs that contains a representative of every Boolean function computable by a fan-in-two circuit of size at most s. Let a_0,...,a_{2^n-1} be the fixed truth-table input order. For each prefix p of length t, define z_j(p)=1 iff C_j(a_i)=p_i for every i<t. Then z(p) is an exact streaming state for EXT_{n,s}: EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff OR_j z_j(p)=1. On the next bit b at position t, update z'_j=z_j AND [C_j(a_t)=b]. With the position-dependent constants [C_j(a_t)=b] supplied, this transition uses at most M fan-in-two AND gates (each coordinate is either z_j or 0). A padded topological description of a size-s circuit has O(s log(n+s+2)+log(n+s+2)) bits, so taking one list entry per description gives M <= 2^{O(s log(n+s+2))}. Proof: Initially every candidate agrees with the empty prefix. If z_j(p)=1, filtering by the next truth-table value retains C_j exactly when it agrees with the extended prefix; induction gives the invariant. The list covers every function in the size-s class, so the candidate set is nonempty exactly when p is an EXT prefix. For the description bound, topologically order at most s gates and pad to s slots; encode each gate type, its at most two predecessors among inputs/constants/earlier slots, and the output. Each slot requires O(log(n+s+2)) bits, giving the stated length and count. This exact construction is a baseline only: it proves no lower bound against compressed states and gives no connection to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

evidence: The construction explicitly evaluates each candidate circuit at the current address and charges every gate, including the shared address-bit negation and the final AND with z_j. Induction establishes exact prefix agreement. This refines the prior free-position-constant transition bound; it does not establish a compressed-state transition.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (uniform candidate-filter transition). Let n>=1, s>=0 and C_1,...,C_M be fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits with constants on n inputs, each of size at most s. For each truth-table prefix p of length t, set z_j(p)=1 iff C_j(a_i)=p_i for all i<t. With current state z, the n-bit address a_t, and next bit b as inputs, the exact next state is computable in at most M(s+5)+1 fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates. Proof: Compute y_j=C_j(a_t) with a copy of C_j, costing at most s gates. Compute e_j=(y_j AND b) OR ((NOT y_j) AND (NOT b)); share NOT b across candidates and use four further gates per candidate. Set z'_j=z_j AND e_j, adding one gate per candidate. The total is at most Ms+5M+1. Initially all candidates agree with the empty prefix. The update retains candidate j exactly when it agreed with the preceding prefix and C_j(a_t)=b, so induction proves the invariant at every prefix. If the list contains a representative for every size-at-most-s circuit function, OR_j z_j(p)=1 exactly when p is an EXT prefix. Scope: the explicit candidate-list representation only; M can be exponential, and this gives no compression into H_C or bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (EXT residual transition circuit). For any finite binary language L, let D_t and D_{t+1} be the numbers of distinct residual languages after prefixes of lengths t and t+1. With one-hot encodings of the D_t residuals, the transition on the next input bit is computable on valid encodings by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit with at most 2D_t+3D_{t+1}+1 gates.
proof: For each destination residual Q and bit b, let P_b(Q) be the level-t residuals whose b-extension has residual Q. Output y_Q = ((¬b) AND OR_{R in P_0(Q)} x_R) OR (b AND OR_{R in P_1(Q)} x_R), with an empty OR equal to 0. On a valid one-hot input exactly the active residual's successor contributes, so the outputs encode precisely the next residual. Across both bits there are 2D_t predecessor-successor incidences; the OR trees use at most their total input count, hence at most 2D_t gates. Each destination uses at most two ANDs and one OR, costing 3D_{t+1}; one shared NOT computes ¬b. The stated bound follows.
scope: All finite binary languages, adjacent fixed prefix levels, valid one-hot state encodings, fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gate count. It gives no bound on D_t in terms of n and s, and no representation for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (bounded-residual layered circuit). Fix c>=0. For every finite binary language L subseteq {0,1}^N whose number D_t of distinct residual languages after length-t prefixes satisfies D_t <= (N+s)^c for every 0<=t<=N, L has an exact layered one-hot streaming circuit with at most 5N(N+s)^c+N fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates.
proof: At level t encode the active residual by its D_t-bit one-hot vector. For each bit b and destination residual Q at level t+1, OR the source bits for residuals whose b-successor is Q; empty groups give 0. The groups partition the D_t sources for each b, so all predecessor OR trees cost at most 2D_t gates. Select the two predecessor signals for each Q using b, with two AND gates and one OR gate, for 3D_{t+1} gates, and share one NOT gate. This computes the unique successor exactly on every valid one-hot state. Summing over t=0,...,N-1 gives at most 2 sum D_t + 3 sum D_{t+1} + N <= 5N(N+s)^c+N. The final residual is accepting exactly when it contains the empty suffix, so its one-hot coordinate gives the decision output.
scope: All finite binary languages with the stated uniform polynomial bound on every residual count; one-hot representation and fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits. No claim about Search-MCSP residual counts, arbitrary representations, or P versus NP.

statement: THEOREM (exact extremal residual count for finite binary languages). Let N>=0 and 0<=t<=N. For L subseteq {0,1}^N, let R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for p in {0,1}^t, and let D_t(L)=|{R_p:p in {0,1}^t}|. Then max_{L subseteq {0,1}^N} D_t(L)=min(2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes and exactly 2^(2^(N-t)) subsets of the suffix universe, so D_t(L) is at most their minimum. For attainment, put a=2^t and b=2^(2^(N-t)). If a<=b, choose an injection phi from the a prefixes into the b suffix subsets and set L={pz:z in phi(p)}; then every residual equals phi(p), so D_t=a. If a>b, select b-1 prefixes (possible since a>b), biject them with the nonempty subsets of the suffix universe, and define L from those prefix-subset pairs; every other prefix has empty residual, while the selected prefixes realize all b-1 nonempty subsets, so D_t=b. (For b=1, the second case cannot occur unless a>1; selecting zero prefixes yields the sole empty residual and D_t=1.) Thus the upper bound is attained in all cases.
scope: Exact finite extremal theorem over all languages on fixed-length binary strings; no claim about the particular language EXT_{n,s}, its transition cost, or arbitrary MCSP encodings.

statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-consistency update for EXT). Fix n≥1, N=2^n, an ordering z_1,…,z_N of {0,1}^n, and a finite enumerated family C={C_1,…,C_K} of Boolean circuits on n inputs, with K≥1. For t∈{0,…,N}, let q_t∈{0,1}^K have coordinate i equal to 1 iff C_i(z_j)=p_j for every j≤t, where p=p_1…p_t. On input bit b at position t+1, update q'_{i}=q_i∧[C_i(z_{t+1})=b]. This update uses at most K+1 fan-in-two AND/NOT gates: the constants a_i=C_i(z_{t+1}) are fixed for each position and q'_i=q_i∧b if a_i=1, while q'_i=q_i∧¬b if a_i=0, sharing ¬b. The final decoder accepts iff OR_i q_{N,i}=1. For C the family of all size-≤s circuits, this decides EXT_{n,s}; standard padded descriptions give K≤2^{O(s log(n+s))}.
proof: At t=0 every circuit agrees with the empty prefix, so q_0=1^K. Assume q_t records exactly the circuits agreeing with p_1…p_t. Circuit C_i agrees with the extended prefix p_1…p_t b exactly when it agrees with the old prefix and its fixed output C_i(z_{t+1}) equals b. Thus the displayed update establishes the invariant at t+1. Induction proves it for all t. At t=N, some coordinate is 1 exactly when some circuit in C has truth table p, proving the decoder. For each coordinate the update uses one AND; when its fixed output is 0, it also uses the shared NOT b. Hence at most K+1 gates. The padded-description count supplies the stated bound when C contains all size-≤s circuits. This is an explicit exponential-in-description-length construction, not a poly(s) transition bound. Scope: fixed finite family, fixed input ordering, and position-dependent transition circuits; no minimality or lower-bound assertion.

statement: LEMMA (fixed-instance H_C information is insufficient to determine EXT across candidate families). Let U be a finite set of truth tables, let C∈U be fixed, and let F_1,F_2⊆U both contain C. Define H_C(y)=1 iff y=C, and EXT_F(p)=1 iff some y∈F has prefix p. There exist U,C,F_1,F_2 and a prefix p for which H_C is identical in the two settings but EXT_{F_1}(p)≠EXT_{F_2}(p). Hence the truth table of one fixed-instance verifier H_C, without information specifying the admissible family F, does not determine EXT_F.
proof: Take U={00,01,10,11}, C=00, F_1={00}, F_2={00,01}, and p=01. Both settings have the same function H_C(y)=[y=00]. But no member of F_1 has prefix 01, whereas 01∈F_2, so EXT_{F_1}(01)=0 and EXT_{F_2}(01)=1. Thus the fixed verifier's truth data alone cannot determine the EXT answer uniformly over candidate families. This says nothing about representations that also encode F, and it is not a lower bound against arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (candidate-suffix characterization of EXT residuals). Let F be a nonempty finite set of binary strings of length N, and for each t let P_t={p∈{0,1}^t: p is a prefix of some y∈F}. For p∈P_t define R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pu∈F}. Then the distinct residuals after t bits are exactly the distinct sets R_t(p), and their number D_t is at most min(|P_t|, 2^{N-t}, 2^{|F|}). For b∈{0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb)={u∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu∈R_t(p)} whenever pb∈P_{t+1}. Thus the exact residual transition is left quotient by the next bit on the surviving suffix set.
proof: For a prefix p of length t, a continuation u of length N−t completes p to a member of F exactly when pu∈F; hence the residual continuation set is R_t(p), proving the characterization. There are at most |P_t| such sets because there are |P_t| prefixes. Each is a subset of the 2^{N−t} possible suffixes, giving at most 2^{2^{N−t}}; for the stronger stated bound 2^{N−t} is not generally valid, so replace it by 2^{2^{N−t}}. Also each R_t(p) is a subset of the suffixes of members of F, a universe of size at most |F|, so there are at most 2^{|F|} possibilities. Finally, u∈R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu∈F iff bu∈R_t(p), proving the transition identity. Scope: finite fixed-length binary languages; no claim that these sets have a succinct encoding or that the transition can be implemented by bounded operations on H_C.

statement: REPAIR LEMMA (candidate-suffix characterization with valid residual count). Let F be a nonempty finite set of binary strings of length N. For each t in {0,...,N}, let P_t be the set of length-t prefixes of members of F. For p in P_t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. The residual language after prefix p is exactly R_t(p), so the number D_t of distinct residuals is at most min(|P_t|, 2^{2^{N-t}}). For b in {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb)={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu in R_t(p)} whenever pb is a prefix of a member of F.
proof: A suffix u of length N-t completes p to a member of F if and only if pu is in F. Thus the residual continuation language after p is exactly R_t(p). There is one such set for each p in P_t, so D_t≤|P_t|. Each R_t(p) is a subset of the universe {0,1}^{N-t}, which has 2^{N-t} elements. That universe has 2^{2^{N-t}} subsets, so D_t≤2^{2^{N-t}}. Finally, for every u of length N-t-1, u belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) exactly when pbu belongs to F, which holds exactly when bu belongs to R_t(p). This proves the transition identity. Scope: finite fixed-length binary languages; this gives no succinct encoding or gate-cost bound for the transition through H_C.

statement: Lemma (unique computation transcript for H_C). Let C be any Boolean circuit with a fixed topological ordering of q gates and Boolean inputs x. Define H_C(x,y)=T_out AND AND_{i=1}^q (y_i <-> T_i(x,y_{<i})), where T_i is gate i's Boolean function applied to its input wires and earlier gate outputs, and T_out is the designated output wire. For each fixed x there is exactly one y in {0,1}^q satisfying the q equivalences; consequently sum_y H_C(x,y)=C(x), interpreting Boolean values as 0 or 1.
proof: Fix x and construct y in gate order, setting each y_i to gate i's value on x and the already assigned predecessor outputs. This satisfies every equivalence. For uniqueness, induction on i shows that any satisfying y must have the same y_i: its predecessors are fixed inputs or agree with the constructed values by induction, so gate i's function determines y_i. Thus exactly one y satisfies the equivalences. On that y, T_out equals C(x). Hence H_C is 1 for exactly one y if C(x)=1, and is 0 for every y if C(x)=0. Summing over y gives C(x).
scope: All deterministic Boolean circuits with a fixed topological gate order and the stated H_C encoding. This does not give a bounded-gate translation from EXT residual transitions to H_C.

statement: Lemma (truth-table transition bound for binary state encodings). Let X be a finite set of D>=1 states, let Y be a finite set of E>=1 states, and let delta_b:X->Y be deterministic for b in {0,1}. Encode X by distinct m=ceil(log2 D) bit strings and Y by distinct r=ceil(log2 E) bit strings, with arbitrary unused strings allowed. Then on valid encodings (x,b), the map (x,b)->code(delta_b(x)) has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most r(2^m+1)(m+1) gates.
Proof: For each output coordinate j, form a DNF with one term for each of the D valid input codes x together with each b in {0,1} for which output coordinate j equals 1. The input has m+1 bits. Each term is a conjunction of at most m+1 literals, costing at most m AND gates with fan-in two. There are at most 2D terms, whose OR costs at most 2D-1 gates (or 0 if there are none); input negations are shared and cost at most m+1 gates. Thus one output bit costs at most 2Dm+(2D-1)+(m+1) <= (2^m+1)(m+1) gates because D<=2^m. Repeat independently for r coordinates, giving the claimed bound. Unused encodings may be assigned arbitrary outputs and are irrelevant to the stated valid-input guarantee.
Scope: This is a generic finite transition-function upper bound for arbitrary stationary injective encodings and fan-in-two Boolean gates. It does not exploit MCSP structure, does not bound circuit-description update time uniformly in (n,s), and supplies no lower bound.

statement: For any fixed n-input Boolean circuit C with s fan-in-two gates, a state (i,a) tracks whether the first k streamed truth-table bits match C: on next bit b, compute c=C(i), set a'=a AND (b iff c), and increment i modulo 2^n. This transition uses O(s+n) gates. Initially (i,a)=(0,1); induction on k proves that i is the next assignment and a records agreement on every bit read. The circuit C is hardwired. This does not bound the cost of merging candidates in EXT.

LEMMA. For b>=1, every map T:{0,1}^{b+1}->{0,1}^b has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size at most b((b+1)2^(b+1)-1)+(b+1), with constants allowed. Proof. For each output coordinate j, let t_j be the number of inputs where it is 1. If t_j=0, use constant 0. Otherwise form its DNF: each of t_j minterms on b+1 literals uses b AND gates, and their OR uses t_j-1 gates, totaling (b+1)t_j-1 <= (b+1)2^(b+1)-1. Sum over b outputs and share at most b+1 NOT gates for input literals. Each minterm matches exactly its defining input, so all outputs are correct. This exponential bound does not imply polynomial update cost for EXT or H_C.

LEMMA. Let a deterministic binary automaton have q>=1 states and transition delta:Q x {0,1}->Q. With q-bit one-hot state encoding, its exact next-state map has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most 4q+1 gates. Proof. Compute not b once. For each source i compute z_i0=x_i AND not b and z_i1=x_i AND b, costing 2q gates. For each destination j, output the OR of all routed signals z_ia with delta(i,a)=j. Across destinations there are 2q signals, and their OR trees cost at most 2q gates total; empty or singleton lists cost zero. Total at most 4q+1. For a valid one-hot input exactly one routed signal is active and it reaches the unique correct destination. This bounds update cost by automaton width q, but does not bound q for EXT.

LEMMA (binary-coded transition upper bound). Let a deterministic automaton have D>=2 states and a binary alphabet. Encode its states by distinct q-bit strings, where q=ceil(log2 D). Its transition function has an exact fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit on the q state bits and one input bit, correct on every valid state code, with at most D(q-1)+q+2D+2Dq gates. Proof: Share the q input-bit negations. For each of the D valid state codes, its equality indicator is a conjunction of q literals and costs q-1 AND gates, so all indicators cost D(q-1). For each state i, form z_{i,0}=eq_i AND NOT b and z_{i,1}=eq_i AND b, costing 2D gates. For each of the q output bits, OR the selector terms whose corresponding successor-code bit is 1. At most 2D terms occur, so this costs at most 2D gates per output bit; an empty disjunction is constant 0. On a valid code for state i, exactly the selector for its actual input symbol is active, yielding the correct successor code. Scope: finite deterministic binary automata; correctness is required only on valid state codes.

LEMMA (candidate-set residual update for EXT). Fix n,s and a finite explicitly enumerated circuit-description set C containing one description per circuit of size at most s. For a truth-table prefix p, define A_p={C in C: Eval(C) begins with p}. At the next position i and bit b, A_{pb}={C in A_p: Eval(C)(i)=b}. Therefore A_p is an exact residual-state representation: it is nonempty iff p has a completion in Im(Eval), and the update is coordinatewise filtering by the next output bit. Proof: membership in A_{pb} is equivalent to membership in A_p and agreement of Eval(C) with b at position i, which is exactly the displayed set intersection. Scope: finite circuit-description sets and EXT prefix states; no compactness or gate-cost bound is asserted.

statement: LEMMA (EXT transition information). Let C be a fixed Boolean circuit on n input bits, let E_C be its truth table in a fixed order, and define EXT_C(p)=1 exactly when p is a prefix of E_C. At a prefix p of length t, the next-bit EXT transition values are determined by the pair (EXT_C(p0), EXT_C(p1)); specifically, if p is a prefix of E_C then exactly one of these values is 1 when t<2^n, and the value for b is 1 iff E_C[t]=b. Proof: By the definition of prefix, p0 is a prefix of E_C iff p is a prefix and the next symbol E_C[t] equals 0; likewise p1 is a prefix iff p is a prefix and E_C[t] equals 1. Since E_C[t] is a Boolean value, exactly one case holds. If p is not a prefix, neither extension is a prefix. This identifies the information needed for the transition at a reachable state as the next truth-table bit E_C[t], together with reachability; it does not provide a bounded-cost circuit representation of that information from H_C. Scope: fixed C, its exact truth table, and all prefix lengths t<2^n.

statement: LEMMA (deterministic transcript projection recurrence). Let T_1,...,T_m be Boolean functions where T_i takes x and y_1,...,y_{i-1} and returns one bit, and let A(x,y) be any Boolean acceptance predicate. Define H(x,y)=A(x,y) AND AND_{i=1}^m [y_i=T_i(x,y_{<i})]. For 0<=i<=m and a prefix u in {0,1}^i, define E_i(x,u)=1 iff there exists y_{i+1},...,y_m such that H(x,u,y_{i+1},...,y_m)=1. Then E_i(x,u)=E_{i+1}(x,u,T_{i+1}(x,u)) for i<m. Thus existentially projecting H onto transcript prefixes yields a deterministic next-bit recurrence, but its circuit cost includes evaluating T_{i+1} and E_{i+1}; it gives no bounded-operation representation or bound for an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
proof: Fix x,u. Every transcript satisfying H must have next bit T_{i+1}(x,u). Any completion witnessing E_i therefore gives a completion witnessing E_{i+1} at that forced longer prefix. Conversely, a completion witnessing E_{i+1} at the forced prefix, preceded by that bit, satisfies all transcript constraints and A, so witnesses E_i. The two predicates are equal. This is only a projection identity; it does not show that E_i is efficiently representable.
scope: All finite Boolean x domains, all m>=1, arbitrary Boolean transition functions T_i and acceptance predicate A. No bound on representation or evaluation cost of T_i or E_i.

statement: LEMMA (deterministic transcript projection recurrence). Let X be any Boolean domain, m>=1, T_i:X×{0,1}^{i-1}->{0,1} for 1<=i<=m, and A:X×{0,1}^m->{0,1}. Define H(x,y)=A(x,y) AND ∧_{i=1}^m [y_i=T_i(x,y_1,...,y_{i-1})]. For 0<=i<=m and u∈{0,1}^i, define E_i(x,u)=1 iff there exists z∈{0,1}^{m-i} with H(x,u,z)=1. Then for every i<m, E_i(x,u)=E_{i+1}(x,u,T_{i+1}(x,u)). Proof: any satisfying completion after u must use the forced next bit T_{i+1}(x,u), so its suffix witnesses the right side. Conversely, a suffix witnessing the right side, prefixed by that forced bit, satisfies every transcript constraint and A, hence witnesses the left side. This is an exact recurrence only; it gives no circuit-size or evaluation-time bound for T_{i+1} or E_{i+1}.
scope: All Boolean domains X, all integers m>=1, all deterministic Boolean transition functions T_i and acceptance predicates A.

statement: LEMMA (exact binary extension decomposition for EXT). Fix n,s and let F_{n,s} be the set of truth tables of Boolean circuits on n input bits of size at most s, with a fixed basis and size convention. For 0<=k<2^n, let L_k be the length-k prefixes of members of F_{n,s}. For every p in {0,1}^k, p is in L_k iff p0 or p1 is in L_{k+1}. Equivalently, EXT_k(p)=EXT_{k+1}(p0) OR EXT_{k+1}(p1). Proof: If p is a prefix of a truth table f in F_{n,s}, its next bit f(k) is either 0 or 1, so p f(k) belongs to L_{k+1}. Conversely, if p b is a prefix of some f in F_{n,s}, then its length-k prefix p is also a prefix of f. This is exact for any fixed family of complete truth tables. It yields no bound on the number of distinct prefixes, transition representation cost, or evaluation cost.
scope: All fixed circuit families F_{n,s}, all 0<=k<2^n, with truth-table prefixes in the standard fixed input ordering.

statement: LEMMA (explicit one-hot residual update bound). Let L be a finite binary language, and let R_t be its set of distinct residual languages after prefixes of length t, with D_t=|R_t| and D_{t+1}=|R_{t+1}|. Encode the current residual by one Boolean coordinate x_R per R in R_t, with exactly one coordinate equal to 1. For Q in R_{t+1} and b in {0,1}, let P_b(Q) be the set of level-t residuals whose b-successor is Q, and define z_{Q,b}=OR_{R in P_b(Q)} x_R, with an empty OR equal to 0. On input bit b, output y_Q=((NOT b) AND z_{Q,0}) OR (b AND z_{Q,1}). This computes exactly the next one-hot residual vector. The update has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit with at most 2D_t+3D_{t+1}+1 gates: for each bit value, the predecessor sets partition the D_t sources, so the OR trees use at most 2D_t gates total; each destination uses two AND gates and one OR gate; and NOT b is shared. Correctness follows because the unique active source contributes to exactly its b-successor, so exactly that destination coordinate is 1. This is a conditional bound and makes no assertion that D_t is small.
scope: Every finite binary language L and every t for which both residual levels are defined, under the one-hot state encoding; fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates.

gap: For EXT_{n,s}, bound the residual counts D_t and the cost of encoding residual states and constructing successor maps tightly enough to obtain polynomial transition cost in n and s. The one-hot update bound is linear in D_t+D_{t+1}; no such bound for the MCSP family, or bounded-cost connection to arbitrary H_C, has been established here.

proved_step:
statement: LEMMA (raw-prefix implementation of EXT). Fix N=2^n and any family F of N-bit truth tables. A deterministic streaming machine can recognize whether a completed word belongs to F by storing the raw prefix p in an N-bit register, initially all zero, and a length counter. On each incoming bit b, append b to the occupied prefix and leave the remaining register cells unchanged. This update is realizable by a fixed Boolean circuit with O(N) fan-in-two gates (for each possible counter value, select the cell to write; equivalently use a one-hot position register and O(N) controlled writes), using O(N) state bits. At end of input, acceptance is exactly the predicate [p in F]. For F=Im(Eval_{n,s}), this is the exact EXT_{n,s} predicate. Proof: induction on the number k of bits read shows that the first k register cells equal the input prefix and the others retain their initial padding; hence after N bits the register equals the input word, and the final test accepts iff that word is in F. The construction bounds the storage and transition cost but supplies no circuit bound for the final membership predicate; therefore it does not yield a small MCSP decision circuit or an EXT-to-H_C reduction.
scope: All finite families F subseteq {0,1}^N; N>=1; fixed-length streaming input, fan-in-two Boolean circuits for state transitions.

evidence: The construction is correct: for each destination residual Q at level t+1 and bit b, define P_b(Q) as the set of level-t residuals whose b-successor is Q. The next-state bit y_Q = ((NOT b) AND OR_{R in P_0(Q)} x_R) OR (b AND OR_{R in P_1(Q)} x_R) correctly computes the one-hot encoding of the successor residual on any valid one-hot input (exactly one x_R = 1). Gate count: each nonempty predecessor OR with k inputs uses k-1 fan-in-2 OR gates; sum over all nonempty P_b(Q) of (|P_b(Q)|-1) = 2D_t - (#nonempty P_b(Q)) ≤ 2D_t. Each of D_{t+1} destinations uses two fan-in-2 AND gates and one fan-in-2 OR gate (3D_{t+1}), plus one shared NOT gate for NOT b. Total ≤ 2D_t + 3D_{t+1} + 1 fan-in-2 AND/OR/NOT gates. No counterexample found; the argument is exact and complete for the stated scope (any finite binary language, one-hot encoding, fan-in-2 gates).

The construction is standard and correct: for each of the t satisfying assignments, create a minterm (conjunction of m literals). Each minterm requires m-1 fan-in-2 AND gates to combine m literals. The t minterms are combined with t-1 fan-in-2 OR gates. Total gates = t(m-1) + (t-1) = tm - t + t - 1 = tm - 1. With free input negations (the m negated/positive literals per minterm are not charged), this matches the claim. If NOT gates are charged, at most m input negations (one per variable) suffice, shared across all minterms, giving tm - 1 + m gates. No counterexample exists; the argument is exact for the stated scope.

The argument is correct: if two distinct residuals R1, R2 at prefix length t shared the same streaming state, then for any suffix w in their symmetric difference (which exists because R1 != R2), the completed inputs p1 w and p2 w would reach the same final state and thus receive the same decision, contradicting that exactly one is in the language. Hence distinct residuals require distinct states, so state count >= D_t and state bits >= ceil(log2 D_t). The claim explicitly notes this does not imply a transition-circuit gate lower bound, which is accurate (state equivalence is necessary but not sufficient for transition-circuit complexity). No counterexample; the argument is exact and complete for the stated scope.

The lemma is correct. A fan-in-two circuit with at most s gates over {AND, OR, NOT, constants} on n inputs can be described by: (1) gate count g ≤ s in ⌈log₂(s+1)⌉ bits, (2) for each of s slots: gate type (4 possibilities = 2 bits) + two predecessors each from n inputs + 2 constants + ≤s earlier gates = n+s+2 choices, so 2⌈log₂(n+s+2)⌉ bits per slot, (3) output label from n+s+2 choices = ⌈log₂(n+s+2)⌉ bits. Total: ⌈log₂(s+1)⌉ + s(2 + 2⌈log₂(n+s+2)⌉) + ⌈log₂(n+s+2)⌉ = O(s log(n+s)). Number of such strings ≤ 2^{O(s log(n+s))}. Decoding reconstructs the circuit exactly. The scope is correctly limited to description counting only, not state or transition complexity of EXT. No counterexample exists.

Exactness holds by induction on prefix length. At t=0 all flags are 1. The update z_C <- z_C AND [C(t+1)=b] retains flag iff circuit C agrees with the extended prefix. The compatibility bit [C(t+1)=b] is b if C(t+1)=1 else NOT b, i.e. a constant gate depending on C and b; implemented with one fan-in-two AND per circuit and a shared NOT for b. OR over all flags is 1 iff at least one circuit matches the prefix, which is definition of EXT_{n,s0}. Gate count per bit is O(|C_{n,s0}|). By S0408, |C_{n,s0}| <= 2^{O(s0 log(n+s0))}, which is polynomial in n for fixed s0. Scope correctly limited to constant s0; no uniform polynomial claim for growing s is made.

The lemma is a basic combinatorial fact about prefix residuals of finite description sets. Proof verified: (1) Each prefix p maps to A_p ⊆ C (descriptions with word starting with p); the residual R_p = {q : pq described by some d ∈ A_p} is uniquely determined by A_p, giving ≤ 2^M distinct residuals. (2) Each R_p ⊆ {0,1}^{N-t}, so ≤ 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residuals. (3) R_p = R_{p0} ∪ R_{p1} (disjoint on first bit), so each level-t residual yields at most 2 level-(t+1) residuals, and every level-(t+1) residual is R_{pb} for some p,b, giving D_{t+1} ≤ 2D_t. No counterexample exists; the bounds are tight (achieved when all 2^M description subsets yield distinct residuals and all suffix subsets appear).

The lemma describes an exact filtering update for a fixed finite set of candidate circuits. Proof verified: For each candidate circuit C, the length-(t+1) prefix agrees with C's output prefix iff (i) the length-t prefix agrees (z_C=1) and (ii) C's t-th output equals b (a_{C,b}=[C(t)=b]). Thus z'_C = z_C AND a_{C,b} coordinatewise. This is exact by construction. The gate count analysis (≤ M+1 gates with precomputed compatibility bits) is correct for the described circuit model. The lemma explicitly does not claim polynomial-size transitions (M may be exponential in s log(n+s)), so no unwarranted complexity conclusion is drawn. No counterexample exists; the update rule is mathematically exact for the given finite enumeration.

The lemma has two parts. (1) Backward recurrence: E_t(p) = 1 iff ∃q: pq ∈ L. Every q starts with 0 or 1, so pq ∈ L iff p0r ∈ L or p1r ∈ L for some r. Thus E_t(p) = E_{t+1}(p0) ∨ E_{t+1}(p1). This is exact and holds for all finite L. (2) Forward obstruction: For N=2, t=0, p=ε, b=0, take L1={00} and L2={10}. For L1: E_0(ε)=1, E_1(0)=1. For L2: E_0(ε)=1, E_1(0)=0. The inputs (E_0(ε),b)=(1,0) are identical but outputs differ, so no universal g exists. The counterexample is minimal and valid. The lemma correctly notes this does not rule out richer states. No gap or counterexample.

Computational verification (cm-6f85817dc76f465e) of witness/verifier logic for multiple test cases: simple AND circuit, NOT circuit, invalid witness detection (tampered gate values, wrong output gate), witness size analysis matching claimed O(s log(n+s) + k(s+log(n+s))) bound, and larger parameter test (n=4, s=10, k=8). All tests passed - the witness encoding, verification checks, and size bounds are sound. The lemma correctly establishes an NP-style certificate/verifier upper bound for prefix extension.

Computational verification (cm-3a1b1c8a5e7d4f2a) of the filtering property A(pb) = {C in A(p) : Eval(C)(x_k) = b} for all n in {1,2,3}, s in {0,1,2,3} (where computationally feasible), and all prefixes up to length min(3, 2^n). All tests passed - the filtering update is exact. Size bound |C_{n,s}| <= (c(n+s)^2)^s verified with c=5 for the {AND,OR,NOT,CONST0,CONST1} basis: holds for all tested (n,s) pairs, ratio ranges from 1.0x to 1311x. The lemma correctly establishes the exact deterministic filtering update and its exponential cost.

Computational verification (cm-8e4b2a1d9f7c4e3a) of the coordinatewise AND transition z_{pb}(c) = z_p(c) AND [E(c)_{t+1}=b] and the OR reduction for EXT_E(p) across all prefixes for random E:C->{0,1}^N with C_size in {2,3,5} and N in {2,4,8}. All assertions hold exactly. The lemma correctly establishes the fixed-level transition circuit with hardwired constants and its gate bounds. The explicit caveat about hardwiring depending on full E and level t is correctly stated - this is an upper bound/representation tradeoff, not a uniform construction.

Computational verification (cm-8e4b2a1d9f7c4e3a and new test): for 100 random trials with |C| in [1,8], N in [1,6], at all prefix lengths t, the number of distinct residual languages D_t never exceeded 2^{|C|}. The mapping A_p -> R_p is well-defined and surjective. The automaton construction with |C| state bits and coordinatewise AND transitions correctly implements the exact prefix automaton. Scope confirmed: bound is in |C|, not compact circuit size; no polynomial(s,n) workspace or transition-cost bound for EXT.

proved_step: REPAIR LEMMA (explicit candidate filtering with separated costs). Let C_1,...,C_K be a finite indexed family of Boolean circuits, and suppose the position-dependent bits e_{i,j}=C_i(a_j) are supplied as constants. For a prefix p, let z_i(p)=1 exactly when C_i agrees with p on every position already read. On reading bit b at position j, update each coordinate by z'_i=z_i AND [e_{i,j}=b]. This transition uses at most K fan-in-two AND gates. The predicate that at least one listed circuit matches the prefix is OR_{i=1}^K z_i and uses max(K-1,0) fan-in-two OR gates. Thus transition plus acceptance uses at most K+max(K-1,0) gates if both are counted. Proof: Initially all coordinates are 1, which records agreement with the empty prefix. Assume the coordinates record agreement through the positions before j. A listed circuit agrees through position j exactly when it previously agreed and its supplied bit e_{i,j} equals b; the update therefore preserves the invariant. Induction gives the invariant for every prefix. Its disjunction is true exactly when some listed circuit matches. Each update coordinate requires at most one AND gate; a binary OR tree on K inputs uses K-1 gates when K>=1 and zero gates when K=0. The two computations have separate costs, so no claim of a K+1 combined bound is needed. Scope: explicit finite families with supplied position-dependent constants; this does not bound preprocessing, give a polynomial-in-s implementation for EXT, or simulate arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: Residual derivative identity. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p a length-t prefix. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb)={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu in R_t(p)}. Therefore EXT_F(pb)=1 iff this derivative set is nonempty, where EXT_F(p) means R_t(p) is nonempty. Proof: for every u of length N-t-1, u∈R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu∈F iff bu∈R_t(p), by associativity of concatenation and the definition of R_t. Equality follows by extensionality; nonemptiness gives the stated equivalence.
scope: All finite Boolean-string families F⊆{0,1}^N and valid t,p,b. This is a semantic transition identity only; it gives no efficient representation or update-time bound when F=Im(Eval).
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing—yes, the identity is representation-free and oracle-independent; natural—no circuit lower bound or largeness/easiness property; algebrizing—no algebraic argument; localizing—no locality claim. Circumvention tests: none claimed; this is a set identity, not a P-vs-NP route.

statement: Explicit-family trie lemma. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N with M=|F|. Let P(F) contain the empty string and every prefix of every member of F. There is a deterministic streaming automaton with one state for each p∈P(F), plus a dead state ⊥. From p on bit b it moves to pb if pb∈P(F), and otherwise to ⊥; ⊥ loops to itself. It accepts exactly the viable prefixes. The automaton has at most 2+MN states. Given F explicitly, a trie constructs it in O(MN) time and space, and a transition is one child-pointer lookup. Proof: Initially the state is the empty prefix, which is viable since F is nonempty. Inductively, if the state is p, after reading b the new prefix is pb; it is viable exactly when pb∈P(F), which is precisely the transition rule. If the state is ⊥, no extension can become viable. Hence the state after any input prefix p is p if p∈P(F), and ⊥ otherwise; acceptance therefore agrees with EXT_F. Each of the M strings contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, so |P(F)|≤1+MN; adding ⊥ gives at most 2+MN states. Inserting each explicitly listed string and its prefixes builds the trie in O(MN) time and space, and each transition follows one child pointer.
scope: All nonempty explicitly listed F⊆{0,1}^N. This is a RAM/trie lookup bound with O(log(MN+2)) state bits and O(MN) preprocessing/storage; it gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound when F=Im(Eval_{n,s}) is only implicit.
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing—yes, the construction is oracle-independent; natural—no lower-bound property; algebrizing—no algebraic method; localizing—no locality claim. No P-vs-NP circumvention is claimed.

statement: Levelwise residual-state characterization. Fix a finite family F⊆{0,1}^N. For 0≤t≤N and each length-t prefix p, define R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}: p·u∈F}. Let r_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p) as p ranges over {0,1}^t. A deterministic layered streaming automaton that, at level t, must determine for every continuation u whether p·u∈F needs at least r_t distinguishable states at that level; storing R_t(p) uses exactly r_t states and supports the exact transition R_{t+1}(p·b)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: b·u∈R_t(p)}. Proof: If R_t(p)≠R_t(q), choose u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of p·u and q·u is in F. Any deterministic automaton in the same level with the same state after p and q would give identical acceptance on continuation u, a contradiction. Thus all r_t residuals require distinct states. Conversely, use the distinct residual sets as level-t states. On bit b transition to the set {u: b·u∈R}; by the definition of residuals this is R_{t+1}(p·b) whenever R=R_t(p). At level N, accept iff the residual contains the empty string. This recognizes F exactly.
scope: Finite F⊆{0,1}^N, fixed bit order, deterministic layered automata whose required output is membership of the completed string in F. The result characterizes state count at each level; it gives no efficient encoding, transition computation, or polynomial update bound for F=Im(Eval_{n,s}).
barriers: Diagnostic: relativizing—yes, combinatorial and oracle-independent; natural—no lower-bound property; algebrizing—no algebraic method; localizing—no locality claim. No P-vs-NP progress claimed.

statement: Layered projection construction. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size T. For each prefix length t and prefix p in {0,1}^t, define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t} with H(pz)=1. For each such p, a fan-in-two circuit computing E_t(p) can be constructed by placing one copy of H for each of the 2^(N-t) suffixes and ORing their outputs, with size at most 2^(N-t)(T+1)-1. Consequently, for every t<N the two child extension values E_{t+1}(p0), E_{t+1}(p1) are obtained by the same construction with 2^(N-t-1) copies each; together, the two child circuits have size at most 2^(N-t)(T+1)-2. Proof: E_t(p)=OR_{z in {0,1}^{N-t}} H(pz), by definition. Each term is implemented by a copy of H with its first t input wires fixed to p and remaining wires fixed to z; this does not increase the gate count. A binary OR tree on q=2^(N-t) outputs uses q-1 gates, so size is at most qT+(q-1)=q(T+1)-1. Applying this with q/2 completions to each child gives two costs 2[(q/2)T+(q/2-1)]=q(T+1)-2. The construction is uniform given H, p, and the truth-table input order, but exponential in the unobserved suffix length in general.

statement: Residual-state counting and transition lemma: for finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and each level t, define R_p={z: pz in F} for length-t prefixes p. There are at most min(2^t,|F|) distinct nonempty residuals and at most one empty residual; for t<N, R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}. The layered residual automaton recognizes F exactly.
proof: There are 2^t prefixes. Every prefix with nonempty residual extends to an element of F, and distinct prefixes have distinct extensions, so there are at most |F| such prefixes. The count of distinct nonempty residuals is bounded by the count of those prefixes. All empty residuals equal the empty set. For the transition, z in R_{pb} iff pbz in F iff bz in R_p. Finally, R_x is nonempty exactly when x in F.
scope: Finite binary languages, fixed length N and coordinate order; exact layered state characterization only.

statement: Residual equivalence exactly characterizes mergeable prefixes in deterministic layered streaming for any finite fixed-length language F: at level t, p and q may share a state only if R_p=R_q; equal residuals admit identical continuation acceptance and define a well-defined residual transition.
proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose a suffix z in their symmetric difference; precisely one of pz,qz is in F, contradicting deterministic identical continuation behavior from a common state. If R_p=R_q, every suffix has the same acceptance outcome from p and q. The residual transition is well-defined since R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}; equal parent residuals yield equal child residuals. The residual-class machine accepts exactly F at the terminal level.
scope: Finite F subset {0,1}^N, fixed input order; exact deterministic layered streaming only, no efficiency claim.

statement: Exact residual-width lemma. Let F be any finite subset of {0,1}^N and, for each t, let d_t be the number of distinct residuals R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} over prefixes p of length t. Every deterministic layered streaming recognizer for F has at least d_t states at level t; a recognizer with exactly d_t states at each level exists.
proof: For the lower bound, suppose prefixes p and q with different residuals reach the same state. Choose z in the symmetric difference of R_p and R_q. Exactly one of pz and qz belongs to F, but deterministic processing from the common state on the same suffix z must give the same result, a contradiction. Thus each distinct residual requires a distinct state. For the upper bound, use the residuals themselves as states. On input bit b, map R_p to its left quotient {z: bz is in R_p}; this equals R_{pb}, so the transition is well-defined even when multiple prefixes have the same residual. At level N, accept exactly the nonempty residual. This recognizes F and has d_t states at level t.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N, fixed input order, deterministic layered streaming; no uniform construction or transition-cost claim.
known_closest: Myhill–Nerode residual equivalence for deterministic automata, specialized to fixed-length layered machines.
novelty: Gives the exact minimum width at every layer, rather than only a necessary state-merging condition.
obstacle: For EXT_{n,s}, this does not bound d_t or show that residual transitions can be implemented with bounded real-gate cost from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
attack: Use a distinguishing suffix for unequal residuals to prove the width lower bound, then construct the matching residual-state machine using left quotients.

statement: Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite family of Boolean strings of length N. At depth t, for each prefix p define R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: p concatenated with u lies in F}. The number of distinct R_p at depth t is at most min(2^t,2^M), hence the total number of depth-labelled residual states is at most sum_{t=0}^N min(2^t,2^M). Proof: there are 2^t prefixes, and every residual set is determined by the subset of the M indexed strings extending p, of which there are at most 2^M. For a next bit b, the exact residual transition retains precisely those suffixes beginning in b and deletes their first bit, so it is well-defined on residual sets. This state-count bound does not bound the real-gate cost of computing the transition or its construction cost.
scope: All finite indexed families F of M Boolean strings of common length N, with depth-labelled residuals.

LEMMA (explicit-family candidate filtering). Let F be a finite set of M distinct strings in {0,1}^N, with coordinates ordered 0,...,N-1. For each prefix p of length t define z_f(p)=1 iff f agrees with p on coordinates 0,...,t-1. Then z(p) exactly represents the strings in F extending p; on reading bit b at coordinate t, set z'_f=z_f AND [f_t=b] for every f in F. With the coordinate tests supplied, this transition has at most M fan-in-two AND gates. The prefix is extendible to a member of F iff OR_{f in F} z_f=1, using at most M-1 fan-in-two OR gates when M>=1. Proof: At t=0 all strings agree with the empty prefix. Assuming the invariant at t, a string agrees with the prefix extended by b exactly when it agreed through t-1 and its t-th bit equals b, which is the stated coordinate update. Induction proves the invariant at every prefix length; the OR is true exactly when the represented set is nonempty. Scope: explicit finite F with supplied position-dependent coordinate tests. This gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound for circuit truth tables and no implementation through an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

statement: Affine-prefix extension lemma. For n>=0, let F_n be the Boolean affine functions f(x)=c+sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i over GF(2), and fix any ordering x^(0),...,x^(2^n-1) of {0,1}^n. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, EXT^aff_n(p)=1 iff the GF(2) linear system c+sum_i a_i x_i^(j)=p_j for 0<=j<t is consistent. After each new truth-table bit p_t at position x^(t), appending the corresponding equation and maintaining a row-echelon basis gives an exact streaming algorithm with at most n+1 coefficient variables and O((n+1)^2) bit operations per update; initialization is the empty system. Proof: Each affine function corresponds exactly to one coefficient vector (c,a_1,...,a_n) in GF(2)^(n+1). The prefix is extendible by an affine function exactly when one such vector satisfies all t displayed equations, which is exactly consistency. Inductively, the maintained row-echelon basis represents precisely the solution set of the equations seen so far. Appending the next equation and eliminating its pivot preserves that represented solution set; a contradiction row arises exactly when no coefficient vector extends the prefix. Thus the algorithm decides prefix extendibility exactly. A basis has at most n+1 rows of length n+2, and insertion/elimination costs O((n+1)^2) bit operations. This proves an efficient transition bound for the affine subclass only; it makes no claim about EXT for arbitrary size-s circuits or simulation through arbitrary H_C.

statement: Residual-language identity for EXT: Fix n,s and a finite set F of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with truth-table positions ordered 0,...,N-1 where N=2^n. For a prefix p of length t, define Ext_F(p) as the set of strings q in {0,1}^{N-t} for which the concatenation pq is the truth table of some f in F. For each f in F, let r_{f,t} be the suffix (f(t),...,f(N-1)), and let A_F(p)={f in F: f agrees with p on positions 0,...,t-1}. Then Ext_F(p)={r_{f,t}: f in A_F(p)}. Consequently, for any two prefixes p,p' of the same length t, A_F(p)=A_F(p') implies Ext_F(p)=Ext_F(p'); moreover Ext_F(p) is nonempty iff A_F(p) is nonempty.
proof: Fix q of length N-t. By definition, q belongs to Ext_F(p) iff pq is the truth table of some f in F. This is equivalent to there being f in F whose first t truth-table bits equal p and whose remaining N-t bits equal q. The first condition is exactly f in A_F(p), and the second is exactly r_{f,t}=q. This proves both set inclusions and hence the identity. If A_F(p)=A_F(p'), the displayed descriptions give equal extension sets. Finally, the set of suffixes displayed is nonempty exactly when A_F(p) is nonempty.
scope: All finite n>=0, all finite F of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, all t in {0,...,2^n}, and the fixed truth-table order. This is a semantic residual identity; it gives no bound on the number of distinct residuals, their encoding cost, or their transition cost in an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

statement: Residual-state lower bound. Let F be any finite family of length-N binary strings, and for each t let R_t(p)={q in {0,1}^{N-t}: pq is in F} for p in {0,1}^t. Every deterministic streaming machine that decides whether the full input lies in F must have at least |{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}| distinct states after t input bits. Proof: if R_t(p) and R_t(p') differ, choose q in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pq,p'q belongs to F. If the machine were in the same state after p and p', determinism gives identical future behavior on common suffix q and hence the same final answer, a contradiction. Thus each distinct residual requires a distinct state; the state-bit lower bound is ceil(log2 of the maximum such count over t).
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and deterministic exact streaming deciders; this is a state-count bound only, not a transition-cost claim.

statement: Residual-width upper bound for finite languages. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For each t, the number of distinct nonempty residual sets R_t(p)={q in {0,1}^{N-t}: pq in F}, over p in {0,1}^t, is at most min(2^t, |F|). If the empty residual is included, the total number of residuals is at most min(2^t, |F|)+1. Proof: There are only 2^t prefixes. Each word in F has a unique length-t prefix, so the nonempty residuals partition F into nonempty parts; their number is therefore at most |F|. There is at most one empty residual. Taking both bounds gives the claim.
scope: All finite nonempty F subseteq {0,1}^N and each t in 0..N. This bounds canonical automaton state width only; it gives no transition-cost bound for EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: EXT residual-width bound by represented truth tables. Fix n,s and N=2^n, and let F be the set of distinct length-N truth tables computed by Boolean circuits of size at most s. For every prefix length t, the canonical residual automaton for EXT_{n,s} has at most |F|+1 states at depth t, including the empty residual. Proof: for each prefix p, its residual R_t(p) is exactly the set of suffixes q such that pq belongs to F. Thus every nonempty residual is a nonempty subset of F consisting of words with the same length-t prefix. Distinct nonempty residuals are disjoint, because a full word has a unique length-t prefix. Choosing one word from each nonempty residual gives an injection into F, so there are at most |F| nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual. This is a state-count bound and gives no transition-cost bound or simulation by arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
scope: All n,s and t=0,...,2^n; F is the set of distinct truth tables of size-at-most-s circuits under the fixed input order. State count only.

statement: Continuation-witness characterization of deterministic exact states. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, fix a cut t, and let P_t(F) be the prefixes of length t that extend to an element of F. Define p ~_F p' iff for every suffix q in {0,1}^{N-t}, pq belongs to F exactly when p'q belongs to F. Every deterministic one-pass exact streaming machine recognizing F has at least |P_t(F)/~_F| states after t bits; moreover a machine with exactly that many reachable states at depth t exists when each depth is represented by its equivalence classes. Proof: If two prefixes lead to the same machine state, then for every suffix q the deterministic continuation from that state on q is identical, so acceptance of pq and p'q agrees; thus they are equivalent. Hence different equivalence classes require different states. Conversely, use the equivalence class of the consumed prefix as state. On bit b, map [p] at depth t to [pb] at depth t+1. This is well-defined: if p~p', then for every suffix r, membership of pbr in F equals membership of p'br in F, by applying the equivalence to suffix br. At depth N accept exactly classes whose represented prefix is in F. This constructs the layered canonical automaton.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and all cuts 0<=t<=N; deterministic exact one-pass automata with depth-aware states/transitions. The result characterizes required states but gives no bound on real-gate transition cost for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary H_C.

gap: S0471 characterizes the number of exact states at a cut but does not bound the real-gate cost of transitions or express them using an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C. Its closes=G0003 annotation overstates what the lemma proves; the transition-cost bridge remains open.
evidence: S0471 proves only the deterministic continuation-equivalence state characterization; it supplies no transition implementation or gate-cost bound.

proved_step:
statement: Residual-state construction for a finite binary language. Let F⊆{0,1}^N. For each t and each length-t prefix p, set R_t(p)={r∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pr∈F}. Any deterministic exact one-pass machine recognizing F must reach different states after p and q whenever R_t(p)≠R_t(q). Conversely, a layered deterministic exact machine can use the residual sets R_t(p) as its states at depth t, including the empty residual; its transition on b maps R_t(p) to R_{t+1}(pb), and its terminal states accept exactly residual {ε}. Proof: If two prefixes reach the same state, every common continuation produces the same acceptance result, so their residual sets agree. For the construction, the residual after reading b is exactly {r:br∈R_t(p)}, which depends only on R_t(p) and b; hence the transition is well-defined. At depth N, the residual is {ε} exactly for prefixes in F and is empty otherwise, giving exact acceptance. This repairs S0471's converse by including nonextendable prefixes through the empty residual state.
scope: All finite F⊆{0,1}^N and deterministic exact one-pass automata with depth-aware state sets. This gives an exact state characterization/construction; it does not bound real-gate transition cost or implement transitions using arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

statement: Explicit completion expansion for EXT from a decision circuit. Let N=2^n, let L⊆{0,1}^N be the truth tables accepted by a Boolean circuit H of size h, and define EXT_L(p)=1 iff some q∈{0,1}^{N−|p|} has pq∈L. For each prefix length t, there is a Boolean circuit E_t with t input bits computing EXT_L on length-t prefixes, of size at most 2^{N−t}(h+1)−1 using fan-in-two gates, assuming H has h gates and fixed input order. Proof: For every suffix q of length N−t, make a copy H_q of H whose first t inputs are the variable prefix p and whose remaining inputs are the constants q. OR the 2^{N−t} output bits with a fan-in-two tree. The output is 1 exactly when at least one completion pq is accepted. The construction uses 2^{N−t}h gates for copies and 2^{N−t}−1 OR gates. At t=N it is H itself; at t=0 it is the constant indicating whether L is nonempty. Applied to L={truth tables with circuit complexity at most s}, this gives an exact EXT computation from any MCSP decision circuit H_C, but the bound can be exponential in N−t and therefore does not establish poly(s) transition cost.
scope: All N>=0, all Boolean languages L⊆{0,1}^N with a size-h decision circuit, and every cut 0<=t<=N. Fan-in-two circuit size counts gates; constants and input wiring are free. This is an explicit upper bound for computing the EXT predicate at one cut, not a lower bound or a streaming update implementation.

statement: LOGARITHMIC-TAIL COMPLETION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, where constants and wiring are free. For a cut t=N-k, define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists q in {0,1}^k with H(pq)=1. Then E_t is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^k(h+1)-1 gates. Consequently, if k<=c log_2(h+2) for a fixed constant c, E_t has size O((h+2)^(c+1)); in particular, for h=poly(s) it has size poly(s) whenever the unprocessed suffix length is O(log s). Proof: For each of the 2^k strings q, take a disjoint copy H_q of H with its first N-k inputs wired to p and its last k inputs fixed to q. OR the 2^k outputs using a binary OR tree, which uses 2^k-1 gates. H_q(p)=H(pq), so the OR computes E_t. The total gate count is 2^k h+(2^k-1)=2^k(h+1)-1. If k<=c log_2(h+2), then 2^k<=(h+2)^c, yielding size <=(h+2)^c(h+1)=O((h+2)^(c+1)). If h is polynomially bounded in s and k=O(log s), this is polynomial in s. This only constructs the completion predicate at cuts with logarithmic remaining suffix; it gives no poly(s) bound for early cuts, no update implementation for the full EXT automaton, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP circuits beyond their decision-circuit size h.
scope: All N>=0, all Boolean circuits H on N inputs, all cuts t with k=N-t, fan-in-two gate count with constants/wiring free. The polynomial consequence assumes the stated asymptotic bounds; no MCSP lower bound is claimed.

statement: Let L be any language of fixed-length words {0,1}^N recognized exactly by a deterministic left-to-right streaming machine. For each depth t and prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_L(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in L}. Any such machine has at least |{R_L(p):p in {0,1}^t}| distinct states after t symbols. Conversely, the layered machine whose depth-t states are the distinct sets R_L(p), with transition R_L(p) --b--> R_L(pb), recognizes L exactly. Therefore the minimum possible number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct accepting-continuation residuals at that depth. Proof: If two prefixes p,q reach the same deterministic state, then every continuation u induces the same accept/reject outcome from that state, so R_L(p)=R_L(q); contrapositively distinct residuals require distinct states. For the converse define the transition by appending b to any representative prefix; this is well-defined because equal residuals at depth t imply that for each b the residuals after pb agree, as membership of every remaining v is equivalent to bv belonging to the original residual. At depth N accept exactly when the empty continuation belongs to the residual. Induction on t proves the invariant that the state after p is R_L(p), hence exact recognition. This characterizes the information an exact fixed-length streaming algorithm must preserve; it provides no transition circuit bound in terms of an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All N>=0 and all Boolean languages L subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic streaming machines reading one bit per transition, with a fixed known depth. State lower bound is per layer; no uniformity, transition gate complexity, or MCSP simulation claim is included.

evidence: Direct proof by unpacking the definition of R_t(p); no finite computation is needed. This supplies the exact residual transition operation but does not claim a gate-cost bound or close the arbitrary-H_C transition-simulation obligation.
proved_step: statement: Residual-section lemma for EXT. Let N>=1, let F be any set of N-bit strings, and for each prefix p of length t<=N define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For t<N and b in {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently R_t(p) is the disjoint union of 0R_{t+1}(p0) and 1R_{t+1}(p1), where bA={bv:v in A}. Proof: For any v of length N-t-1, v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbv belongs to F, iff bv belongs to R_t(p). Every length-(N-t) string has a unique first bit b and remaining suffix v, so it belongs to exactly one of the two displayed sections; membership in that section is equivalent to pv with that first bit lying in F by the defining equivalence. Thus the pair of child residuals is exactly the information needed to reconstruct the parent residual, and each child is obtained by a fixed section operation. Scope: exact residual languages for any fixed-length target F, including EXT with F=Im(Eval); this proves the abstract transition identity only and gives no bound on representing or computing the sections in real gates from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

evidence: Direct distinguishability proof: unequal residual sets have a suffix on which membership differs; identical machine states force identical future behavior on that suffix, contradicting exact recognition. This general proof requires no finite enumeration.

statement: Layerwise residual lower bound for exact streaming recognition. Let N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and 0<=t<=N. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and let r_t be the number of distinct residual sets. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in F exactly must reach at least r_t distinct states after t bits, hence needs at least ceil(log2 r_t) state bits (zero if r_t=1). Proof: If p and q have different residuals but lead to the same state, choose u in their symmetric difference. Starting from that shared state, the machine's deterministic run on u gives the same answer for pu and qu. Exactly one lies in F, a contradiction. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states; a B-bit state has at most 2^B possibilities, so 2^B>=r_t. This applies to EXT_{n,s} for F equal to the set of size-at-most-s circuit truth tables in the fixed order, but does not bound transition gate cost or give a simulation from arbitrary H_C.
scope: All finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N and all layers t, for deterministic exact one-pass recognition; applies to EXT prefix membership under its fixed truth-table ordering.

evidence: Direct construction and proof: successor residuals are determined solely by the current residual and next bit, because R(pb)={u: bu in R(p)}. Acceptance at the final layer is membership of the empty suffix. No computation is needed for this general finite-language lemma.
