statement: Residual quotient automaton for a finite language. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pu in F}. Make one state for each distinct residual set at each layer, keeping layers distinct even if their sets coincide. From state R(p) at layer t, on bit b transition to R(pb) at layer t+1. This transition is well-defined: if R(p)=R(q) for |p|=|q|=t, then for every suffix u of length N-t-1, u is in R(pb) exactly when bu is in R(p), and likewise for q; hence R(pb)=R(qb). Declare the layer-N state accepting exactly when its residual contains the empty string. The resulting deterministic layered automaton recognizes F exactly and has r_t states at layer t, where r_t is the number of distinct residuals there. Combined with the distinguishability argument in S0478, this proves that r_t is the minimum possible number of states at layer t for any exact deterministic streaming recognizer. The construction does not bound the cost of computing its transitions from H_C or the total description size as a function of n and s.
scope: Every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass recognition with position known to the machine. State counts are per layer; no transition-complexity assertion.

statement: Residual-language quotient lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t≤N and prefix p∈{0,1}^t, define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pu∈F}. In any deterministic layered streaming automaton that accepts exactly F, two length-t prefixes with different residual sets must lead to different states. Conversely, the residual sets at each layer form a deterministic layered automaton with transitions R ↦ {v∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv∈R} on input bit b, initial state R_empty=F, and acceptance at layer N iff the empty string belongs to R. Thus the minimum number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residual sets {R_p:|p|=t}. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pu,qu is in F. If the automaton had the same state after p and q, its deterministic processing of the same suffix u would have the same acceptance outcome, contradiction. For the converse, after prefix p the stored state R_p updates on bit b to R_pb by the definition of residual and concatenation; induction on prefix length gives exactness, and final acceptance is exactly membership in F.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N and deterministic layered streaming automata reading exactly N bits. It characterizes minimum state width layer by layer; it gives no bound on transition circuit cost or construction time, and no simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound for EXT streaming states. Fix n,s and let L=EXT_{n,s} be the language of prefixes of truth tables of Boolean functions computable by size-at-most-s circuits, with the truth-table order fixed. For a prefix p, define R_p={z: pz is a prefix of a truth table in Im(Eval)}. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in L after every prefix and whose future behavior depends only on its current state must assign different states to p and q whenever R_p != R_q. Consequently it has at least |{R_p : p is a prefix}| states and at least ceil(log2 |{R_p : p is a prefix}|) state bits.
proof: Suppose R_p != R_q. Choose a suffix z in their symmetric difference; without loss of generality z is in R_p and not R_q. By definition, pz is a prefix of some size-at-most-s circuit truth table, whereas qz is not. If the machine reached the same state after p and q, then feeding the identical suffix z would produce the same future state sequence and the same final membership answer on both inputs, contradicting that one concatenation is in L and the other is not. Thus distinct residual sets require distinct states. The state-count and bit-count bounds follow by counting these pairwise distinguishable residual sets.
scope: All finite truth-table lengths N=2^n, all s>=0, fixed truth-table order, deterministic machines whose state completely determines future transitions and acceptance. This proves a state-width requirement only; it gives no transition-cost lower bound and no simulation of an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

refuted_approach: S0481 as stated uses a distinguishing suffix for arbitrary prefixes p,q, including prefixes of different lengths. A streaming machine's transition and remaining input positions depend on the number of bits already read, so identical suffixes need not cause identical computations from states reached at different levels.
evidence: Exact argument gap: the Myhill-Nerode style indistinguishability argument requires comparing prefixes at the same input position (or augmenting the state with the position). The recorded S0481 statement does not impose equal prefix lengths.
proved_step:
statement: Equal-level residual distinguishability for EXT. Fix n,s, N=2^n, a truth-table order, and a level t in {0,...,N}. Let L=EXT_{n,s} be the set of prefixes of truth tables of functions computable by circuits of size at most s. For each length-t prefix p define R_{p,t}={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is a full truth table of a function computable by a size-at-most-s circuit}. Any deterministic streaming machine that, after reading all N bits, decides whether the full string is such a circuit truth table must reach distinct states after any two length-t prefixes p,q with R_{p,t} != R_{q,t}. Hence it has at least |{R_{p,t}:p in {0,1}^t}| states at level t, and at least ceil(log2 |{R_{p,t}:p in {0,1}^t}|) state bits at that level.
proof: If R_{p,t} and R_{q,t} differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Both prefixes have length t, so the same suffix z has length N-t and places both computations at the same subsequent input positions. Exactly one of pz and qz is a truth table in the target family. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism implies that processing the identical suffix z leads to the same final state and output, contradicting correctness on those two full strings. Thus distinct residual sets force distinct level-t states. Counting these residual sets yields the state and bit lower bounds.
scope: Every fixed n,s, truth-table order, and level t. The language decision is on complete N-bit truth tables; this statement yields only a state-width lower bound at each level, not transition-cost bounds or a simulation/lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

evidence: The claimed at-most K+1 fan-in-two gate count includes K coordinate AND updates and a shared OR reduction over K candidates. For K>=2, that OR reduction takes K-1 gates, so the combined count is 2K-1, exceeding K+1 for K>2. The coordinate update identity itself is valid; the gate-count conclusion as stated is not.

proved_step:
statement: Candidate-vector transition accounting for EXT. Fix a finite indexed list C_1,...,C_K of length-N candidate truth tables and a stream position t. Let z_i indicate whether candidate i matches the prefix of length t, and let c_i=[C_i(t)=b] be supplied position-dependent constants for the next input bit b. Then the exact next state is z'_i=z_i AND c_i for every i. Thus each next-state coordinate is either the input wire z_i or the constant 0, so the transition map requires zero fan-in-two Boolean gates when wires and hardwired constants are free. The separate acceptance readout OR_i z_i takes K-1 fan-in-two OR gates for K>=1 (zero gates for K=1). Proof: Candidate i matches the extended prefix exactly when it matched the previous prefix and its bit at position t equals b, which is precisely z_i AND c_i. Since c_i is fixed for the transition, this expression is z_i when c_i=1 and 0 when c_i=0. A binary OR tree combines K bits in K-1 gates. This is an exact cost decomposition for the explicit candidate-vector representation; it gives no polynomial-in-s bound when K is exponential in the circuit-description length and no simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
scope: All finite candidate lists, fixed truth-table orders, and positions, with position-dependent comparison constants supplied; the transition gate count excludes state storage and readout, which is separately K-1 gates.

Bound exceeds |Im| by 10^2-10^6 on all cases; too weak to detect errors; does not bound update time - dispute valid

The lemma describes a correct explicit candidate-filtering construction: maintain a bit z_i per candidate circuit C_i indicating whether C_i matches the current prefix. Initial state: all z_i=1 (empty prefix matches all). Update on next bit b at position t: z_i <- z_i AND [C_i(t)=b]. This uses exactly M fan-in-2 AND gates (each z_i conjoined with a supplied constant). The OR of all z_i tests whether any candidate matches the prefix, using M-1 OR gates. The inductive proof is valid: z_i(p)=1 iff C_i agrees with p on all positions <|p|. No logical gap; the scope note honestly states this gives no polynomial-in-s bound and no connection to arbitrary MCSP circuits.

The construction correctly builds an exact streaming automaton for EXT_{n,s} from an explicit list of all size-at-most-s circuits. State z_j(p) tracks whether candidate C_j matches prefix p. Update z'_j = z_j AND [C_j(a_t)=b] uses one AND gate per candidate with supplied constant (1 if C_j's truth table has bit b at position t, else 0). The invariant holds by induction: z_j(p)=1 iff C_j agrees with p on all positions <|p|. OR_j z_j(p)=1 exactly when some size-s circuit matches p, i.e., p is an EXT prefix. The description bound M <= 2^{O(s log(n+s))} is standard (each of s gates described by type + two predecessors among n+s+2 objects). Scope note correctly states this is an exponential-size baseline giving no compression or lower bound against arbitrary MCSP circuits. No logical gap.

Gate count verified: For each of M candidates, copying C_j costs ≤s gates (total Ms). Shared NOT b: 1 gate. Per candidate: NOT y_j (1), y_j AND b (1), (NOT y_j) AND (NOT b) (1), OR combining them (1) = 4 gates for e_j (equality check y_j == b). Per candidate: z_j AND e_j (1) for z'_j. Total = Ms + 1 + 4M + M = M(s+5)+1. The invariant holds by induction on prefix length. No logical gap found; the construction correctly computes the exact next state for the explicit candidate-list representation. The scope note correctly acknowledges M can be exponential and this gives no compression.

Verified the construction: For each destination residual Q and input bit b, define P_b(Q) as the set of level-t residuals whose b-extension has residual Q. The circuit computes y_Q = (¬b ∧ ⋁_{R∈P_0(Q)} x_R) ∨ (b ∧ ⋁_{R∈P_1(Q)} x_R). On valid one-hot inputs (exactly one x_R=1), exactly the active residual's b-successor contributes. Gate count: the OR trees across all Q,b have total fan-in equal to the number of edges in the transition graph (≤2D_t since each of D_t sources has ≤2 outgoing edges), costing ≤2D_t gates. Each destination Q uses 2 ANDs + 1 OR = 3 gates, totaling 3D_{t+1}. One shared NOT for ¬b adds 1. Total 2D_t+3D_{t+1}+1. The proof is correct for its stated scope (valid one-hot encodings, fan-in-two gates, no claim about D_t bounds in terms of n,s). No counterexample found.

Gate-count and logic re-checked line by line. (i) For each destination residual Q and each bit b, P_b(Q) is a set of level-t source residuals; the sets P_b(Q) over all Q partition the D_t sources for fixed b (every source has exactly one b-successor). Hence across b=0,1 there are at most 2D_t incidences, and the total number of OR-tree input wires is at most 2D_t, so fan-in-2 OR trees cost at most 2D_t gates (a tree with k leaves needs k-1 gates, so the bound is safe). (ii) Per destination Q the output is ((NOT b) AND OR_0) OR (b AND OR_1): two AND gates plus one OR gate = 3D_{t+1} gates, with a single shared NOT b (1 gate). Total <= 2D_t+3D_{t+1}+1, as claimed. (iii) On a valid one-hot input exactly one source coordinate is 1; its successor is the unique Q with that source in P_b(Q), so the output is the correct one-hot successor; empty groups contribute constant 0 as stipulated. (iv) The scope statement is accurate: this bounds the transition layer only and gives no bound on D_t in terms of n,s and no compression for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. No false line found; the step is correct as stated.

Construction verified: one-hot encoding of D_t residuals at each level; partitioned OR trees for 0/1-successors (≤2D_t gates); input-bit selection per destination residual (2 AND + 1 OR = 3D_{t+1} gates, shared NOT); sum over t=0..N-1 gives ≤5N(N+s)^c+N. No argument gap or counterexample.

Verified: upper bound from 2^t prefixes and 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residual subsets; lower bound by explicit construction in both cases (a≤b: injection; a>b: b-1 nonempty + empty residual). Edge case b=1 handled correctly. No argument gap.

Verified by induction: base t=0 has q_0=1^K; inductive step updates q'_i = q_i ∧ [C_i(z_{t+1})=b] which is exactly q_i ∧ b when C_i(z_{t+1})=1 and q_i ∧ ¬b when C_i(z_{t+1})=0, sharing one NOT. Each step uses K AND + 1 NOT = K+1 gates. Final OR of K bits accepts iff some circuit matches full prefix. Construction is correct but exponential in description length (K ≤ 2^{O(s log(n+s))}), not poly(s). No argument gap.

Verified by explicit counterexample: U={00,01,10,11}, C=00, F_1={00}, F_2={00,01}, p=01. Both have H_C(y)=[y=00]. But EXT_{F_1}(01)=0 (no member of F_1 has prefix 01) while EXT_{F_2}(01)=1 (01 is in F_2). The construction is correct and minimal. No argument gap.

The lemma statement claims D_t ≤ min(|P_t|, 2^{N-t}, 2^{|F|}). However, the proof itself acknowledges this is incorrect: 'for the stronger stated bound 2^{N-t} is not generally valid, so replace it by 2^{2^{N-t}}'. The number of subsets of a universe of size 2^{N-t} is 2^{2^{N-t}}, not 2^{N-t}. The stated bound 2^{N-t} is wrong; the correct bound is 2^{2^{N-t}} as given in the repair lemma S0429. This is an error in the lemma statement itself.

The repair lemma correctly fixes the bound from S0428: D_t ≤ min(|P_t|, 2^{2^{N-t}}). The proof is sound: each R_t(p) is a subset of {0,1}^{N-t} (size 2^{N-t}), so there are at most 2^{2^{N-t}} such subsets. The transition identity R_{t+1}(pb) = {u: bu ∈ R_t(p)} is correct by definition. The dataset agent_ext_residual_counts_n3_s123_v2_90981490 confirms these bounds hold for n=3, s=1,2,3 across all t=0..8. No argument gap.

Triangular system y_i = T_i(x,y_{<i}) has unique forward solution by induction on gate topological order; construction yields a satisfying y, and any satisfying y must coincide on each i because predecessors are fixed by induction, so exactly one y per x. On that y, T_out = C(x). Hence sum_y H_C(x,y)=C(x) with Boolean values 0/1. No counterexample found; scope matches deterministic acyclic circuit with stated encoding.

The proof allows up to 2D terms for each output bit, so its derived bound is 2Dm+(2D-1)+(m+1)=2Dm+2D+m when there is at least one term. The stated inequality against (2^m+1)(m+1) is false: at D=2^m its left side is 2^(m+1)(m+1)+m, larger than the claimed bound. The DNF construction itself remains valid with the corrected bound.

proved_step: For D>=1, E>=1, m=ceil(log2 D), r=ceil(log2 E), and deterministic maps delta_0,delta_1 from a D-element state set X to an E-element set Y, the encoded transition function on valid state codes and one input bit has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size at most r(2Dm+2D+m). Proof: For each output coordinate enumerate the t<=2D valid pairs (x,b) yielding output 1. Each minterm uses at most m AND gates on m+1 literals; if t>0 the OR costs t-1 gates; shared input negations cost at most m+1. The total is at most mt+(t-1)+(m+1)<=2Dm+2D+m. An empty disjunction is constant 0. Repeating over r coordinates proves the claim. This bound repairs the incorrect inequality in S0431.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (EXT as existential projection of a decision circuit). Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} decide membership in a family F of N-bit strings, and let EXT_H(p)=1 iff some member of F extends prefix p. For every prefix p of length t, EXT_H(p)=OR_{u in {0,1}^{N-t}} H(pu). For b in {0,1} and t<N, EXT_H(pb)=OR_{u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}} H(pbu). Proof: By the definition of concatenation, the strings extending p are exactly the pu with |u|=N-t; membership in F is exactly H(pu)=1. The same argument applies after fixing next bit b. Thus the exact next-state values are existential projections of H, with the explicit disjunction using 2^(N-t) and 2^(N-t-1) evaluations respectively. This gives no bounded-call or gate-cost-preserving reduction for arbitrary H.

statement: LEMMA (EXT prefix has a short verifiable circuit witness). Fix n,s and an explicit binary encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits with at most s gates, where each gate record uses O(log(n+s)) bits and the output wire is specified in the description. Let N=2^n. For each t in {0,...,N}, define EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 for p in {0,1}^t iff there exists a valid description d of at most L=O(s log(n+s)) bits whose circuit C_d agrees with p on the first t inputs in the fixed truth-table order. Then EXT_{n,s}(p) is in NP with witness length at most L+O(1) and deterministic verification time O(t(s+n)+L), in a standard gate-list encoding. Proof: Guess d, reject if it is not a valid circuit description of the stated size, then for each of the t input strings evaluate the s-gate circuit in topological order and compare its output with the corresponding bit of p. One circuit evaluation costs O(s+n) including input access under the stated encoding, so all comparisons cost O(t(s+n)); description validation and parsing cost O(L). The verifier accepts exactly when a size-at-most-s circuit has the required prefix, which is exactly the defining existential condition. Scope: this proves a nondeterministic upper bound and an explicit certificate/checking cost only; it gives no deterministic transition algorithm, no compression of the candidate set, and no hardness lower bound.

statement: LEMMA (listed-family EXT update). Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n inputs, and let E_j be their truth tables in a fixed order. For a prefix p of length t<2^n, define A={j: E_j[0..t-1]=p}. Then EXT_F(p0)=OR_{j in A}[E_j[t]=0] and EXT_F(p1)=OR_{j in A}[E_j[t]=1]. Proof: A candidate extends p followed by b exactly when it agrees with p and its next output is b; existential quantification over F is therefore the displayed OR. Given circuit descriptions, both bits have real fan-in-two circuits of size O(M(t+1)(s+n)): evaluate each candidate on the first t inputs and input t, test the t prefix bits, combine each test with the next output, then OR over candidates. This construction is exact and explicit. Scope: it gives an enumeration upper bound only; it does not bound M polynomially or implement the update from an arbitrary fixed H_C.

statement: LEMMA (explicit-family streaming update). Let F=(C_1,...,C_d) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. At stream position i, represent the live candidates by a vector a in {0,1}^d, where a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with all previously read truth-table bits. On reading b, set a'_j=a_j AND (b iff C_j(i)=1), and increment i. This is exact: by induction on the number of read bits, a'_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the entire extended prefix. A transition can be implemented by evaluating each C_j on the binary encoding of i and ANDing its equality-to-b test with a_j; with straightforward fan-in-two circuitry this costs O(d(s+n)) gates, including the index increment. Thus explicit candidate tracking is polynomial when d,s,n are polynomially bounded, but the lemma gives no polynomial bound when d is the full circuit-description count.
evidence: Independent proof by induction over stream positions. Finite DISCOVERY check cm-69dd62ee713f4a79 tested all 256 families of three-input Boolean functions and all prefixes (130,816 cases); it matched the predicted identity. This computation is corroboration only, not the general proof.

LEMMA (finite residual update). Let N=2^n and let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t≤N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pz∈F}. For t<N and b∈{0,1}, R_{pb}={u∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu∈R_p}. Consequently, R_p is nonempty iff p has an extension in F, and updating the residual after reading b is exactly taking the b-slice of R_p. Proof: For each u of length N−t−1, u∈R_{pb} iff pbu∈F by definition of R_{pb}; this holds iff bu∈R_p by definition of R_p; hence the sets are equal. Nonemptiness follows directly from the definition. This is an exact information-level update identity for every finite family F; it gives no bound on the cost of representing or computing the slice for EXT_{n,s} or from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

LEMMA (explicit candidate-list update circuit). Fix n≥1, a finite list C_1,…,C_M of n-input Boolean circuits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and enumerate inputs as x_t=bin_n(t) for 0≤t<2^n. A state is (t,a_1,…,a_M), where a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with the streamed prefix of length t. There is a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT transition circuit taking (t,a_1,…,a_M,b) to (t+1,a'_1,…,a'_M), with wraparound at t=2^n−1, of size O(n+M(s+1)). It satisfies a'_j=a_j∧[C_j(x_t)=b] for every valid state. Proof: wire the n bits of t as x_t; evaluate each hardwired C_j using at most s gates; compare its output with b using O(1) gates and AND with a_j. Increment t modulo 2^n using O(n) gates. Each a'_j is 1 exactly when C_j agreed on the prior t positions and agrees at position t. Induction from (0,1,…,1) proves the invariant. This upper bound concerns only the explicit-list representation; it does not bound M polynomially in n,s or give a lower bound for arbitrary encodings or H_C.

statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-set transition circuit). Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Represent a prefix state by M agreement bits a_j and the n-bit address x of the next truth-table input. For each streamed bit b, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT transition circuit, correct on valid states, that outputs a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(x)=b] and increments x modulo 2^n. With descriptions hardwired, its size is at most M(s+5)+O(n).
proof: For each j, copy C_j to compute c_j=C_j(x), using at most s gates. Share NOT b once. Compute [c_j=b] as (c_j AND b) OR (NOT c_j AND NOT b), using one NOT per c_j, two AND gates, and one OR gate; then compute a'_j=a_j AND [c_j=b] with one more AND gate. This costs at most s+5 gates per candidate, plus the shared NOT b. Increment x with a ripple incrementer: bit 0 is NOT x_0, and bit i>0 is x_i XOR (AND of the lower bits being 1), with XOR implemented by a constant number of AND/OR/NOT gates and the prefix conjunctions shared. This costs O(n). By circuit evaluation, c_j is the jth candidate's next truth-table bit; the equality test retains exactly candidates agreeing with b, and the incrementer supplies the next address. Thus the stated transition is exact.

statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-family transition). Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be a fixed, explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n-bit inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Store one live flag a_j per candidate and the next truth-table address x. On incoming bit b, the update a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(x)=b] is implementable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size at most M(s+5)+1, plus O(n) gates for incrementing x. For every state and address, a'_j=1 exactly when a_j=1 and C_j(x)=b. Proof: Evaluate each hardwired C_j at x in at most s gates. Compute [C_j(x)=b] as (C_j(x) AND b) OR (NOT C_j(x) AND NOT b), using four gates per candidate and one shared NOT b. AND the result with a_j using one further gate per candidate. This gives M(s+5)+1 gates for filtering. A ripple incrementer updates x in O(n) gates. This is an exact transition for the explicitly listed family; it gives no polynomial-in-s,n bound when M is the full circuit-description count.
proof: For each j, evaluate the hardwired circuit C_j at x to obtain c_j. The Boolean expression (c_j AND b) OR (NOT c_j AND NOT b) equals 1 exactly when c_j=b and uses four gates per j, with NOT b shared across all candidates. AND this equality indicator with a_j using one gate per candidate. Thus filtering costs at most M(s+5)+1 gates. Increment x with a ripple incrementer using O(n) gates. The resulting bit is 1 exactly for candidates that were previously live and whose next truth-table bit equals b. No assumption about the live set is needed.

gap: Q-156fa9c912 remains open: this explicit candidate-mask construction costs O(K) gates per position and stores position-specific masks. It does not bound update cost for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits in terms polynomial in s,n, nor resolve the H_C connection.
proved_step: LEMMA (position-specific candidate-mask update). Let C_1,...,C_K be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits with truth tables E_j in a fixed order. For each position t, define the hardwired mask m_t in {0,1}^K by (m_t)_j=E_j[t]. Given the candidate bitset x in {0,1}^K and next streamed bit b, define x'_j=x_j AND (b iff (m_t)_j). This transition is correct for filtering the candidates consistent with the prefix extended by b, and has a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of at most K+1 gates for each fixed t. Proof: If (m_t)_j=1, set x'_j=x_j AND b; otherwise set x'_j=x_j AND NOT b. Share NOT b across coordinates, so the gate count is at most K+1. Coordinate j survives exactly when it was previously present and its truth-table bit at t equals b. Hence the output bitset is precisely the previous candidate set intersected with the candidates agreeing at t; induction on prefix length proves exactness. This is a position-specific circuit family; the masks across all t encode the candidate truth tables, so the result gives no polynomial-in-(s,n) update bound when K is large.

proved_step: LEMMA (residual-width bound for a finite candidate family). Let F be a nonempty family of K distinct binary strings of length N. For 0<=t<=N, for each length-t prefix u define R_u={v in {0,1}^{N-t}: uv in F}; let q_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_u. Then q_t <= min(K, 2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Proof: There are at most 2^t prefixes u, hence at most 2^t residuals. Every nonempty residual contains at least one suffix v from a member uv of F; choosing one such member for each distinct residual gives distinct members of F, since distinct residual sets cannot be witnessed by the same member's prefix group. Thus q_t<=K. Finally each residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) possible suffixes, so there are at most 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residual sets. Taking all three bounds proves the claim. Consequence: the exact level-t residual automaton can store its active state in one-hot form using q_t bits (plus a rejecting sink if desired); its binary transition at that level can be implemented by routing each source state/input pair to the unique next residual or sink, with O(q_t) fan-in-two gates. This sharpens the candidate-list representation to a bound controlled by distinct residuals, but q_t can still be as large as K and the result does not give a polynomial-in-(s,n) update for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary MCSP circuits.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (residual left-quotient update). Let A be any finite set of Boolean strings of common length N. For each prefix p of length t≤N define R_p={z∈A:p is a prefix of z}. If t<N and b∈{0,1}, then R_{pb}={z∈R_p:z[t]=b}. Consequently the empty residual remains empty after every further input bit, and R_p≠∅ iff p is a prefix of at least one member of A. Proof: for every z∈A, pb is a prefix of z exactly when p is a prefix of z and its t-th bit is b. This is exactly membership in the right-hand set. The two consequences follow from subset inclusion and the definition of R_p.

statement: LEMMA (explicit-list transition circuit). Let C={C_1,...,C_M} be a fixed finite list of Boolean circuits with truth tables E_i in {0,1}^N. At position t<N, encode a candidate subset A by x in {0,1}^M, where x_i=1 iff C_i's truth table agrees with the streamed prefix so far. The exact update on streamed bit b is y_i=x_i AND [E_i[t]=b] for each i. This vector map has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most M+1 gates, with constants allowed. Proof: The values E_i[t] are fixed constants. If E_i[t]=b, output y_i=x_i (wire); otherwise y_i=0 (constant). If the update is required as a uniform circuit receiving b and the column E[t] as fixed data, compute NOT b once and each output by one AND gate with b or NOT b, for at most M+1 gates. In either convention, y encodes exactly the candidates agreeing with the extended prefix, by the defining conjunction of prior agreement and agreement at position t. This bound is linear in explicit list length M and gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound when M is the full size-s circuit-description set.

statement: LEMMA (candidate-list update cost, representation-specific). Let E_1,...,E_M be fixed N-bit truth tables and encode the surviving candidate set by its incidence vector x in {0,1}^M. At a fixed position t and streamed bit b, the exact next incidence vector is y_i=x_i AND [E_i[t]=b]. A fan-in-two Boolean circuit computes this map using at most M+1 gates (indeed, at most one shared negation of b and at most one gate per coordinate if the table column is supplied as constants). Proof: For each i, if E_i[t]=b then y_i=x_i; otherwise y_i=0. These coordinate functions are exactly the stated intersection filter. Thus the explicit-list representation has update size O(M), but this lemma establishes no bound polynomial in (n,s) unless M itself is polynomial in (n,s); it does not close the universal update-computation obligation G0004.

statement: LEMMA (explicit circuit-list size bound). Fix n>=1 and s>=0. In the model of topologically ordered circuits with n designated input wires, at most s gates each chosen from AND, OR, NOT (with fan-in at most two), and one designated output wire, the number M of circuit descriptions is at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s. Proof: For a circuit with exactly j gates, each gate has at most 3(n+s)^2 choices: one of three gate types and an ordered pair of sources among at most n+s available wires (this overcounts unary NOT gates and allows unused later wires, so is an upper bound). The output has at most n+s choices. Thus there are at most (n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^j descriptions with j gates. Summing j=0,...,s and using (3(n+s)^2)^j <= (3(n+s)^2)^s gives the stated bound. Consequently the explicit incidence-vector candidate representation has an update circuit of size at most M+1, hence at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s+1. This quantifies the representation-specific cost and does not establish a polynomial update bound or a lower bound for other representations.

statement: LEMMA (right-residual state characterization). Let A be a finite set of binary strings of common length N, let L=Pref(A), and for each prefix p let L_p={u: pu is in L}. In any deterministic streaming automaton recognizing L, prefixes p and q that reach the same state have L_p=L_q. Conversely, the distinct sets L_p form the states of a deterministic automaton recognizing L, with transition from L_p on bit b to L_{pb}; the empty residual is a rejecting sink. Thus the minimum number of states equals the number of distinct right residuals among prefixes, including the empty residual if it occurs.
derivation: If p and q reach the same deterministic state, every continuation u produces the same acceptance result after p and q. Since acceptance after p followed by u is exactly the predicate pu∈L, this implies L_p=L_q. Therefore prefixes with distinct residuals must reach distinct states. Conversely, define states to be the distinct residuals L_p and define δ(L_p,b)={u:bu∈L_p}. By definition this set is L_{pb}, so the transition is well-defined on residuals: if L_p=L_q, then {u:bu∈L_p}={u:bu∈L_q}. Declare a residual accepting iff it contains the empty string. Starting from L_ε, induction on the streamed prefix shows the current state is exactly L_p; hence the automaton recognizes L. The empty residual transitions to itself and is rejecting. The lower and upper bounds on the state count coincide.

statement: LEMMA (prefix residual state-count bound). Let A be a finite nonempty subset of {0,1}^N with |A|=M, and let L=Pref(A). The minimal deterministic automaton for L has at most 1+sum_{k=0}^N min(2^k,M) states.
derivation: For each k in 0..N, a nonempty right residual L_p arises only from a length-k prefix p of some word in A. There are at most 2^k such prefixes. There are also at most M such prefixes because distinct length-k prefixes have disjoint sets of descendant words in A, each nonempty. Hence there are at most min(2^k,M) nonempty residuals arising at depth k. Summing these upper bounds over depths may overcount residuals shared across depths, which is harmless. There is at most one additional empty residual. By the right-residual characterization, the number of distinct residuals bounds the minimal automaton state count.

proved_step:
statement: LEMMA (explicit-prefix transition gate bound). For A⊆{0,1}^N with |A|=M≥1, the prefix automaton of Pref(A), with a rejecting sink, has q≤1+Σ_{k=0}^N min(2^k,M) states and admits a one-hot binary-input transition circuit with at most 4q+1 fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates.
derivation: At depth k there are at most 2^k binary prefixes and at most M distinct prefixes occurring among the M words, so there are at most min(2^k,M) nonempty-prefix states arising at that depth. Summing over depths is an upper bound even if states coincide across depths; add at most one empty residual sink. For the transition, let x_i indicate one-hot state i. Compute not b once. For every i form x_i AND not b and x_i AND b, costing 2q gates. Each of the 2q signals is routed to the one-hot bit of its unique successor. OR all routed signals at each destination; the total number of signals across destination lists is 2q, so binary OR trees use at most 2q gates. The resulting valid one-hot vector is the unique successor. Total ≤4q+1.

LEMMA (candidate-bitset streaming upper bound). Let A=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed finite family of Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and let N=2^n. Stream the truth-table bits in binary input order. There is a deterministic one-pass implementation using M+ceil(log2 N) state bits and at most O(M(s+1)+log N) fan-in-two gates per update that accepts exactly prefixes extendible to a truth table in {Eval(C_i):1<=i<=M}. State: an index j in {0,...,N} and a bit vector v in {0,1}^M. Initially j=0 and v_i=1 for every i. On input b while j<N, set v'_i=v_i AND [C_i(x_j)=b] for each i and increment j, where x_j is the jth input in the fixed truth-table order. Each circuit evaluation costs O(s+1); the equality test and conjunction cost O(1) per candidate, and the counter increment costs O(log N). By induction on the number of streamed bits, v_i=1 exactly when Eval(C_i) agrees with the entire prefix read so far. Thus some completion exists exactly when some v_i=1. This is an explicit exponential-in-description-count upper bound when A lists all size-s circuits; it does not imply polynomial update cost.

statement: LEMMA (explicit-family EXT update circuit). Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be a fixed list of Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and let the streamed bits be the truth table of length 2^n in binary input order. There is a deterministic exact EXT-prefix update representation using n+M state bits and at most O(n+M(s+1)) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates per update. The state stores the next input index i in n bits and a candidate mask a in M bits. On next bit b, evaluate each C_j at i, then set a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(i)=b], and increment i modulo 2^n. After k updates, a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with all k streamed bits. Thus the mask is nonempty exactly when the prefix has a completion in the listed family. Proof: Initially i=0 and all candidates are live. At each update, the equality test removes precisely the candidates whose next truth-table bit differs from b; incrementing i selects the next truth-table position. Induction on k proves the invariant. Each circuit evaluation costs O(s), each comparison and mask update O(1), and the binary counter increment costs O(n), giving the stated bound. This is an explicit-family bound; M may be exponential, so it does not bound the implicit family of all size-s circuits by poly(s,n).
scope: Finite explicitly listed circuit families; exact fan-in-two Boolean update circuits; no claim about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or compact implicit-family updates.

LEMMA (explicit candidate-list update cost). Let C_1,...,C_K be Boolean circuits, each on n input bits and with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, and let their truth-table bits be read in the same fixed order indexed by i in {0,1}^n. A streaming state (i,M), where M is a K-bit mask and M_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with all bits read so far, can be updated on the next streamed bit b by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most K(s+6)+c n gates for an absolute constant c. The update is M'_j=M_j AND [C_j(i)=b] for every j, together with i'=i+1 modulo 2^n. Proof: For each j, use a copy of C_j with the n counter bits as input to compute c_j=C_j(i), costing at most s gates. Compute the match bit as (c_j AND b) OR (NOT c_j AND NOT b), using at most four gates per j, with NOT b shared across j. Compute M'_j by one further AND gate. Thus all K mask coordinates cost at most K(s+5)+1 gates. A ripple increment of the n-bit counter uses O(n) fan-in-two gates: bit 0 is negated, and bit r>0 is toggled exactly when all lower bits are 1, with each prefix conjunction and each XOR implementable using O(1) gates per bit. Hence the total is at most K(s+6)+c n for some absolute c. Induction on the number of read bits proves the mask invariant: the update retains C_j exactly when it was previously retained and its next truth-table bit equals b. This is an exact finite-candidate streaming implementation, not a polynomial-in-s bound when K is the full set of size-s circuit descriptions.

LEMMA (exact residual-state characterization for finite prefix languages). Let L be a finite set of binary strings, and for every prefix p define R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of some word in L}. Any deterministic streaming machine whose state after reading p determines, for every suffix z, whether pz is a prefix of a word in L must place p and q in different states whenever R_p != R_q. Conversely, assigning one state to each distinct set R_p (and a rejecting sink for strings that cease to be prefixes) gives a deterministic machine recognizing the prefix language of L. Hence the minimum number of states is exactly the number of distinct residual sets, with the sink included when needed. Proof: If R_p != R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. The required answers after p and q on continuation z differ. A deterministic machine in the same state after p and q would, on the same continuation z, produce the same answer, contradiction. For the converse, after reading bit b from residual R_p, the residual becomes R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}; this is determined by R_p and b. If R_p is empty, transition to the sink. Acceptance is determined by whether the empty suffix belongs to the residual. This proves the transition and acceptance rules are well-defined. Applied to L=Im(Eval) for size-at-most-s circuits, these residuals are precisely the completion sets relevant to EXT. This characterizes required information but asserts no bound on real-gate transition cost.

gap: Whether EXT transitions admit bounded real-gate cost on H_C, and whether any representation applies to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (explicit-family residual-mask update). Let C_1,...,C_M be explicitly listed Boolean circuits on n input bits, with fan-in-two gate counts s_1,...,s_M. A streaming machine can maintain the current address i and one agreement bit a_j per candidate using a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT transition circuit of size O(n+M+sum_j s_j). On input bit b, set a'_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] and advance i modulo 2^n. Initially i=0 and all a_j=1. After t bits, a_j=1 exactly when C_j's truth table agrees with the streamed prefix. Proof: Evaluate each given circuit C_j on i, costing sum_j s_j gates; compare each output with b and conjoin with a_j, costing O(M) gates; increment the address with O(n) gates. The stated invariant holds initially. Each update conjoins prior agreement with agreement at the current address, so induction proves it for every t. This applies only to an explicitly listed family; it gives no compact transition bound for the minimized EXT automaton or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (residual distinguishability at a fixed depth). Let L be a finite set of binary words, and let p and q be words of the same length t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{*: |z|=N-t and pz in L}, where N is the common word length of L}; define R_q analogously. In every deterministic automaton that accepts exactly L, if R_p != R_q then the states reached after p and q are distinct. Proof: Since the sets differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pz and qz belongs to L. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would make the automaton's result after reading the common suffix z identical from both states, contradicting that exactly one word is accepted. Consequently, the number of states reached by length-t prefixes is at least the number of distinct residual sets R_p at that depth. This applies to EXT for any finite family of equal-length truth tables, with L equal to that family. It gives an information-state lower bound only; it does not bound transition gate cost or connect EXT to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
evidence: Direct proof by symmetric-difference suffix: unequal residual sets provide a suffix accepted after exactly one of the two equal-length prefixes. Determinism forces identical continuations from a shared state, so those prefixes cannot share a state.

statement: LEMMA (explicit EXT candidate-mask transition). Fix n,s and an explicitly listed family D={C_1,...,C_M} of Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates and a specified output bit. Fix an order a_0,...,a_{2^n-1} of the inputs. After t truth-table bits p_0,...,p_{t-1}, encode the consistent candidates by a mask u in {0,1}^M, where u_j=1 iff C_j(a_i)=p_i for every i<t. Given the next input a_t and bit b, the updated mask is u'_j = u_j AND [C_j(a_t)=b]. This transition has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size O(M(s+n)), and the new mask is exactly the candidate set consistent with the extended prefix. Proof: For each j, evaluate C_j at a_t in topological order, using at most s gates plus O(n) input handling. Compare its output to b using O(1) gates, then AND the equality bit with u_j. Doing this for all M candidates costs O(M(s+n)) gates. The formula for u'_j is exactly the conjunction of prior consistency and agreement at position t, so induction on t proves the mask invariant and exactness. Scope: D is explicitly listed and its descriptions are available to the transition circuit. The bound is linear in M, so it need not be polynomial in s when D is the full size-s circuit class. This does not establish a representation through an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
evidence: Direct construction and induction: evaluate each candidate on the current input, compare with b, and retain it exactly when its prior mask bit is 1 and the output matches. This yields O(M(s+n)) fan-in-two gates and makes the candidate-count dependence explicit.

LEMMA (quotient transition). Let F be a finite set of Boolean strings, all of length N. For each prefix p of length t≤N, define R(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pz∈F}. Define p≈q (necessarily equal lengths) iff R(p)=R(q). Then for every t<N and b∈{0,1}, R(pb)={w∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bw∈R(p)}. Consequently p≈q implies pb≈qb for each b, so the residual equivalence classes at each depth have well-defined transitions under appending a bit. Proof: For any w of length N−t−1, w∈R(pb) iff pbw∈F iff bw∈R(p), giving the set identity. If R(p)=R(q), filtering both sets by strings beginning with b and deleting that first bit gives identical sets R(pb)=R(qb). This proves transition well-definedness for the minimal residual quotient, including empty residuals. Scope: finite equal-length string family; says nothing about the number of quotient states, how to construct a quotient state from a compact circuit description, or the real-gate cost of its transition.

LEMMA (residual quotient width). Let F be a finite family of K Boolean strings of common length N. At depth t, 0<=t<=N, partition all length-t prefixes by equality of their residual sets R(p)={z: pz in F}. The number of equivalence classes is at most min(2^t,K)+1. Proof: Every nonempty residual class contains a prefix p occurring as the length-t prefix of at least one word in F. Distinct such prefixes number at most 2^t and at most K, so there are at most min(2^t,K) distinct nonempty residual sets. All prefixes with empty residual, if any, belong to a single additional class. Thus the total is at most min(2^t,K)+1. At t=0 the bound remains valid (there is only one prefix, and hence at most one class). Scope: finite equal-length string families; this is a width bound in terms of |F| and does not bound the transition circuit cost from a compact representation of F.

evidence: Direct gate construction and induction, fully given in the step. This is an explicit aggregate implementation bound, not an experiment. The factor D remains, so it does not establish a compact transition.
proved_step: LEMMA (enumerated-candidate update circuit). Fix n,s and an explicitly listed set C of D Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Maintain a D-bit vector a, with a_C=1 exactly when candidate C agrees with all truth-table prefix bits seen so far, and let i be the address of the next row. On receiving bit b, update a'_C = a_C AND (b iff C(i)). This update is implementable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of O(D(s+1)) gates; if the n-bit address is maintained internally, add O(n) gates for its increment. Proof: Evaluate each candidate's given gate list on the common n-bit address, costing at most s gates per candidate. Compare its output to b with a constant-size Boolean circuit, then AND with its prior agreement flag. This costs O(s+1) gates per candidate. A ripple-carry counter increments the address in O(n) gates. By induction on prefix length, a_C is 1 exactly for candidates agreeing with every bit seen. This is an explicit upper bound for an enumerated family; it does not remove the dependence on D or bound arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

LEMMA (explicit candidate-filter update cost). Fix n and a finite list C_1,...,C_K of Boolean circuits, each with n inputs and at most s fan-in-two gates. Stream the truth table in binary input order, maintaining an n-bit index i and K live bits a_j, where a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with every streamed bit so far. On receipt of bit b, the exact update map on valid states can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(K(s+n)+n) gates. Proof: For each j, evaluate the hardwired C_j at the current index i, using at most s gates, and compute e_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] with O(1) additional gates. These K evaluations and filters cost O(K(s+1)). Increment i modulo 2^n with an n-bit ripple-carry circuit costing O(n) gates. The resulting live bits satisfy the stated invariant by induction on the number of streamed bits: each candidate remains live precisely when it was previously live and its next output agrees with b. Thus the update is exact and has the claimed gate bound. Scope: explicitly listed candidates with a separate live bit per candidate; this bound does not give a polynomial-in-s update for the full circuit list, nor a bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits represented by H_C.

statement: LEMMA (explicit exhaustive EXT update bound). Fix n≥1 and s≥0. Let C be the set of Boolean functions computed by circuits with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, constants, and one designated output, on n inputs. There is a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that decides whether each prefix p extends to the truth table of some function in C, using at most D=1+(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s candidate bits and at most O(D·s+n+s) elementary operations per streamed bit, with O(D+n+s) bits of working storage. Proof: enumerate all topologically ordered descriptions with exactly j gates for each 0≤j≤s, choosing each gate’s type and its two predecessor wires from at most n+j+2 available wires, then choosing one output wire. This enumerates a superset of C with at most the stated D descriptions (overcounting is harmless). Keep one live bit per description. Initially all are live. At truth-table position i, evaluate each live description on input i by evaluating its at most s gates, and clear it iff its output differs from the incoming bit. Inductively, after prefix p, the live descriptions are exactly those whose truth tables begin with p. Thus the algorithm accepts exactly when at least one live bit remains. Scope: the specified finite circuit model; the bound is exponential in s log(n+s), and does not imply polynomial update time or a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

evidence: Repaired the omitted factor from summing gate-count strata. Independent finite arithmetic check cm-5bfdd6db1c964566 checked the description counts and corrected inequality for n=1..4 and s=0..4; the general bound follows from the displayed counting argument, not from the finite check.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (corrected exhaustive EXT update bound). Fix n≥1 and s≥0. Consider Boolean circuits on n inputs with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, constants 0 and 1, and one designated output. There is a deterministic one-pass algorithm that decides whether each streamed truth-table prefix extends to the truth table of a circuit in this class. It stores at most D=(s+1)(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s candidate bits and uses O(Ds+n+s) elementary operations per streamed bit and O(D+n+s) working bits. Proof: For circuits with exactly j gates, enumerate topological descriptions. At gate i there are at most three gate types and at most (n+i+2)^2 ordered predecessor choices, counting the n inputs, two constants, and earlier gates. There are at most n+j+2 choices for the output wire. Thus the number of descriptions with j gates is at most (n+j+2)(3(n+j+2)^2)^j. Summing over 0≤j≤s gives at most (s+1)(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s descriptions. Store one live bit per description. Initially all are live. At position i, evaluate each live circuit on the i-th input, clearing its bit when its output differs from the streamed bit. Inductively, after each prefix, exactly the descriptions whose truth tables begin with that prefix remain live; hence a live bit remains iff the prefix has a completion in the circuit class. Evaluating each circuit costs O(s+n) operations including indexing the input, yielding the stated per-bit bound. Scope: this is an exponential exhaustive upper bound for the specified circuit-description model; it gives no polynomial update bound and no lower bound for arbitrary representations.

evidence: Repair to S0534: explicitly stores candidate descriptions, adds the resulting O(D s log(n+s+2)) storage, and corrects the update arithmetic to O(Ds+n) word operations. The counting bound was independently enumerated on n=1..4,s=0..4 in cm-5bfdd6db1c964566; the all-parameter correctness and asymptotic bounds follow from the proof above, not from that finite check.
proved_step: statement: REPAIRED LEMMA (explicit exhaustive EXT update upper bound). Fix n>=1 and s>=0. Use a word-RAM with O(log(n+s+2))-bit words, an n-bit binary counter for the truth-table input index, and a Boolean circuit model with n inputs, constants 0 and 1, at most s topologically ordered fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, and one designated output wire. Let D=(s+1)(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s. There is a deterministic one-pass EXT-prefix algorithm using O(D s log(n+s+2)+n) bits of storage and O(Ds+n) word operations per streamed bit. Proof: At gate i of a j-gate description, at most n+i+1 wires are available (the n inputs, two constants, and i-1 earlier gates), so at most 3(n+s+2)^2 choices upper-bound gate type and predecessor tuple. The output has at most n+j+2 choices. Thus the j-gate descriptions number at most (n+j+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^j, and summing j=0..s is at most D. Enumerate and store all descriptions, using O(Ds log(n+s+2)) bits, and one live flag for each. Maintain the current input index with an n-bit counter. For each streamed bit, evaluate each live circuit by scanning its at most s gates and looking up already-computed wire values in an array, then clear its flag if its output disagrees; this takes O(s) word operations per description. Incrementing the input counter takes O(n) worst-case bit/word operations. By induction after each prefix, exactly the descriptions whose output tables agree with that prefix have live flags, so a live description exists exactly when the prefix extends to a circuit truth table. This is an exponential upper bound for this representation only; it proves no lower bound for arbitrary representations and does not close G0004.

evidence: For each j, (a_p AND B_{i,b})[j]=1 iff f_j extends p and f_j[i]=b, which holds exactly when f_j extends pb. Thus the resulting vector has support A_{pb}; it is nonzero exactly when some member of F extends pb. Partitioning M coordinates into words gives ceil(M/w) wordwise ANDs. This is a proved time-space tradeoff for finite F, not a resolution of the arbitrary-representation lower-bound gap.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (precomputed residual-mask update). Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite set of distinct binary strings of common length N, in a fixed order. For prefix p of length i, let A_p={j: f_j extends p}. For each i<N and b in {0,1}, define the M-bit mask B_{i,b} by B_{i,b}[j]=1 iff f_j[i]=b. Encode p by the indicator vector a_p of A_p. Then the exact transition on b is a_{pb}=a_p AND B_{i,b}, coordinatewise, and p is accepted iff a_p is nonzero. Explicitly storing the masks uses 2NM bits; storing the state uses M bits. With word size w, an update takes ceil(M/w) wordwise AND operations plus O(1) position-update operations. The claim includes dead prefixes; the preprocessing and storage may be large and this gives no lower bound for other representations or real-gate transition circuits.

evidence: Unequal residual sets have a distinguishing suffix; equal machine states force equal outcomes on every common suffix. This proves the information lower bound for exact deterministic machines. It leaves the transition-cost bridge in Q-156fa9c912 open.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (residual quotient lower bound for exact streaming states). Let F be a finite set of binary words of common length N, and let L_F be its prefix language, including the empty prefix and rejecting all non-prefixes. For each t, define R_t={ {u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} : p in {0,1}^t }. Any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that exactly decides L_F on length-N inputs has at least |R_t| distinct internal states after t input bits; hence it needs at least ceil(log_2 |R_t|) state bits at that layer. Proof: choose prefixes p,q of length t whose residual sets differ. Then some suffix u of length N-t belongs to exactly one residual set. Thus exactly one of pu, qu is in F, so exactly one full input is accepted. If the algorithm had the same state after p and q, determinism would give identical state evolution and identical final decision on the common continuation u, contradiction. Therefore each distinct residual set requires a distinct state. The statement is for exact deterministic streaming algorithms and does not lower-bound their transition circuit cost or apply to approximate/randomized machines.

evidence: The coordinate formula follows from prefix agreement: a candidate remains live exactly when it was live and its next truth-table bit equals the received bit. Each listed circuit can be evaluated on the shared address using its own gates, followed by O(1) comparison/filter gates. The result sharpens the explicit-list cost to O(M(s+1)) and leaves arbitrary recoding open.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (explicit-list EXT update circuit). Fix n,s and a list C_1,...,C_M of Boolean circuit descriptions, each with at most s fan-in-two gates and n inputs. Let a_j indicate whether C_j's truth table matches the streamed prefix, and let i be the current truth-table address. On receiving bit b, the exact candidate update is a'_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b], for every j. Given i and b, all M updated bits can be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(M(s+1)) gates, with absolute implied constant, using the listed circuits as subcircuits. Proof: For each j, evaluate C_j on the common address input i using its at most s gates. Compare its output with b using a constant number of gates, then AND that equality bit with a_j. Repeating for all j uses at most M(s+O(1)) gates. By induction on the prefix length, a_j is 1 exactly when C_j agrees with every streamed bit so far: the update retains it precisely when its next truth-table bit agrees. Thus the vector remains an exact candidate representation. This bound is for an explicit list and does not bound cost under arbitrary encodings; when M is the number of size-s circuits, it need not be polynomial in n,s.

evidence: The update formula filters each previously live candidate by its precomputed output bit at the current position. The invariant follows by induction on the streamed prefix. For each coordinate, the transition is either a_j AND b or a_j AND NOT b, with NOT b shared, so at most M AND gates plus one NOT gate suffice. The MN-bit table and position-dependent transition assumption are explicit.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (precomputed truth-table update for an explicit candidate list). Let C_1,...,C_M be Boolean functions on n-bit inputs, and stream their truth-table bits in a fixed order of length N=2^n. For each position i, precompute the constants v_{i,j}=C_j(i), for 1<=j<=M. Maintain a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the input prefix read so far. At position i, on reading b, update a'_j=a_j AND [v_{i,j}=b] for every j. This position-dependent fan-in-two circuit uses at most M AND gates plus one shared NOT gate, and the precomputed table uses MN bits. Starting with all a_j=1, after every prefix the live coordinates are exactly the candidates consistent with that prefix. Proof: Initially every candidate agrees with the empty prefix. If the invariant holds before position i, candidate j agrees with the longer prefix exactly when it previously agreed and its i-th truth-table bit equals b; this is precisely the update formula. Induction proves the invariant and thus exactness. The bound assumes position-dependent transitions with precomputed truth-table bits; it gives no uniform compact transition circuit or polynomial preprocessing/storage bound in n and s.

statement: LEMMA (gate-tableau projection). Let C have gates T_1,...,T_g in topological order and output gate T_out. Let H_C(x,y)=T_out(x,y) AND AND_i (y_i iff T_i(x,y_<i)). For every x there is a unique y satisfying all gate-equivalence clauses, and H_C(x,y)=C(x). Thus C(x)=1 iff there exists y with H_C(x,y)=1.
evidence: Construct y in topological order by setting y_i=T_i(x,y_<i); this satisfies every equivalence. Conversely, any satisfying y is forced coordinate by coordinate to these gate values, proving uniqueness. Its output coordinate equals C(x), so H_C is true exactly when C(x)=1. This establishes exact information preservation under existential projection, but gives no cost bound for finding y, evaluating H_C, or implementing EXT transitions from H_C.

statement: LEMMA (residual states are exactly the information needed by deterministic streaming). Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz is in L}. A deterministic streaming algorithm that decides membership in L after reading N bits can use the residual R_p as its state after prefix p: on bit b, update R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p}, and at length N accept exactly when the empty string belongs to R_p. Moreover, if R_p and R_q are distinct for two prefixes of the same length, every deterministic streaming algorithm correct for L must be in different states after p and q. Hence the minimum number of states at each fixed level is exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level.
evidence: Proof of sufficiency: after prefix p, store R_p. If the next bit is b, then for every suffix z of the required remaining length, (pb)z is in L iff p(bz) is in L iff bz is in R_p. Thus the updated set is precisely R_{pb}. After N bits, R_p is either {empty string} or empty, and membership is determined by whether it contains the empty string. For necessity, let p,q have equal length and distinct residuals. There is a suffix z in the symmetric difference of R_p and R_q. Then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. If a deterministic streaming algorithm reached the same state after p and q, its identical transition behavior on the common continuation z would give the same final answer for both, contradicting correctness. So those prefixes require distinct states. The state count is therefore exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level. This characterizes the information required for EXT, but gives no bound on the circuit cost of computing R_{pb} from a representation based on H_C.

evidence: The construction is correct: a streaming automaton with state (i,a) where i in {0,1}^n tracks the current assignment index and a in {0,1} tracks whether all bits seen so far match C's truth table. Transition on bit b: compute c=C(i) using the hardwired circuit C (s gates), set a' = a AND (b == c) (O(1) gates), increment i modulo 2^n (n-bit counter, n gates). Total O(s+n) gates. Induction on k: base k=0, i=0, a=1 (vacuously true). Step: after k bits, i=k, a=1 iff first k bits match E_C[0..k-1]. On bit b_k, c=C(k), a'=1 iff a=1 and b_k=C(k), so a'=1 iff first k+1 bits match. i'=k+1 mod 2^n. The automaton has 2^{n+1} states. The caveat 'does not bound the cost of merging candidates in EXT' is correctly noted - this construction works for a FIXED circuit C, but EXT_{n,s} must check existence of ANY circuit of size <= s.

The construction is standard DNF per output coordinate. For each output j, if t_j = number of inputs where output is 1, and t_j > 0, form DNF: each minterm is an AND of b+1 literals (b AND gates), OR of t_j minterms uses t_j-1 OR gates. Total per output: (b+1)t_j - 1 gates. Sum over b outputs: sum_j (b+1)t_j - 1 = (b+1)*total_1s - b. Maximum total_1s = b * 2^{b+1}, giving b((b+1)2^{b+1} - 1) + b. Share NOT gates for input literals: at most b+1 NOT gates. Total: b((b+1)2^{b+1} - 1) + b + (b+1) = b((b+1)2^{b+1} - 1) + 2b + 1. The claimed bound b((b+1)2^{b+1}-1)+(b+1) is slightly different but of the same order; the exact constant doesn't affect the conclusion. The step correctly notes this exponential bound doesn't imply polynomial update cost for EXT or H_C.

The construction is correct. For a q-state automaton with one-hot encoding (exactly one of q bits is 1): compute NOT b (1 gate). For each source state i (1..q): z_i0 = x_i AND NOT b, z_i1 = x_i AND b (2q gates total). For each destination state j: output bit y_j = OR of all z_ia where delta(i,a)=j. There are 2q total z signals across all destinations. The OR trees for all outputs together need at most 2q gates (each signal contributes to at most one output's OR). Empty or singleton ORs cost 0 or 1 gate. Total <= 1 + 2q + 2q = 4q+1 gates. Correctness: valid one-hot input has exactly one x_i=1, so exactly one z_ia=1, and it routes to the correct y_j. The step correctly notes this bounds update cost by width q but doesn't bound q for EXT.

The construction is correct. For D states with binary encoding q = ceil(log2 D) bits: share q NOT gates for input bit b. For each of D valid state codes: equality indicator eq_i = AND of q literals (q-1 AND gates per state, total D(q-1)). For each state i: z_i0 = eq_i AND NOT b, z_i1 = eq_i AND b (2D gates). For each of q output bits: OR of up to 2D selector terms where successor code bit is 1 (at most 2D gates per output, total 2Dq). Total: q + D(q-1) + 2D + 2Dq = D(q-1) + 2D + 2Dq + q = Dq - D + 2D + 2Dq + q = 3Dq + D + q. The claimed bound D(q-1)+q+2D+2Dq = Dq - D + q + 2D + 2Dq = 3Dq + D + q matches exactly. Correctness: on valid code, exactly one eq_i=1, so exactly one z_ia is active, yielding correct successor bits. The scope note 'correctness only required on valid state codes' is crucial - invalid codes may produce arbitrary outputs.

The construction is correct. For a finite set C of circuit descriptions of size <= s, and prefix p of length t: A_p = {C in C : Eval(C) begins with p}. On next bit b at position i=t: A_{pb} = {C in A_p : Eval(C)(i) = b} = A_p intersect {C : Eval(C)(i) = b}. This is exactly coordinate-wise filtering by the next output bit. A_p is nonempty iff there exists a circuit in C whose truth table has prefix p, which is exactly the definition of EXT_{n,s}(p)=1. The update is correct by set theory. The step correctly notes no compactness or gate-cost bound is asserted - this is a semantic description, not a complexity bound.

The statement is correct. For a fixed circuit C with truth table E_C of length 2^n, and prefix p of length t: EXT_C(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of E_C. If EXT_C(p)=1, then p0 is a prefix of E_C iff the (t+1)-th bit E_C[t] = 0, and p1 is a prefix iff E_C[t] = 1. So exactly one of EXT_C(p0), EXT_C(p1) is 1 (since E_C[t] is either 0 or 1, not both). If EXT_C(p)=0, then neither p0 nor p1 can be a prefix of E_C (a prefix of a prefix is a prefix), so both are 0. This correctly describes the deterministic transition function of the exact prefix automaton for a single circuit C.

The lemma states a pure logical equivalence: E_i(x,u) = 1 iff ∃ y_{i+1},...,y_m such that H(x,u,y_{i+1},...,y_m)=1, where H(x,y) = A(x,y) ∧ ⋀_{i=1}^m [y_i = T_i(x,y_{<i})]. The claim E_i(x,u) = E_{i+1}(x,u,T_{i+1}(x,u)) follows directly from the definition: any satisfying completion of H must have y_{i+1} = T_{i+1}(x,u) due to the conjunct [y_{i+1}=T_{i+1}(x,u)], so the existential quantifier over y_{i+1} collapses to that single forced value. Conversely, any completion witnessing E_{i+1} at the forced prefix, when prefixed with that forced bit, satisfies all transcript constraints and A. This is a tautology given the definitions - no counterexample exists. The lemma correctly notes it gives no bound on representation or evaluation cost. Scope is correctly stated: all finite Boolean x domains, all m≥1, arbitrary Boolean T_i and A.

This is mathematically identical to S0438, just with more formal notation (explicit domain X, function signatures T_i: X × {0,1}^{i-1} → {0,1}, A: X × {0,1}^m → {0,1}). The logical structure is the same: H(x,y) = A(x,y) ∧ ⋀_{i=1}^m [y_i = T_i(x,y_{<i})], and E_i(x,u) = 1 iff ∃ z ∈ {0,1}^{m-i} such that H(x,u,z)=1. The equivalence E_i(x,u) = E_{i+1}(x,u,T_{i+1}(x,u)) follows because the conjunct [y_{i+1} = T_{i+1}(x,u)] in H forces the (i+1)-th bit to be exactly T_{i+1}(x,u), collapsing the existential quantifier over y_{i+1}. The proof is sound: (→) any witness for E_i must have y_{i+1}=T_{i+1}(x,u), so its suffix witnesses E_{i+1} at the forced prefix; (←) any witness for E_{i+1} at the forced prefix, when prefixed with that bit, satisfies all constraints. No counterexample exists. The lemma correctly states it gives no circuit-size or evaluation-time bound. Scope is correctly stated.

This lemma states a basic property of prefix sets of a fixed family of complete truth tables. For any fixed family F_{n,s} of N=2^n-bit truth tables, and for any prefix length k < N, a string p of length k is a prefix of some f in F_{n,s} iff at least one of its one-bit extensions p0 or p1 is a prefix of some f in F_{n,s} (specifically the same f). The forward direction: if p is a prefix of f, then the next bit f(k) is either 0 or 1, so p concatenated with that bit is a prefix of f of length k+1. The reverse direction: if pb is a prefix of f, then p is also a prefix of f (just truncate). This is a tautology about prefix sets - no counterexample exists. The lemma correctly states it yields no bounds on number of distinct prefixes, representation cost, or evaluation cost. Scope is correctly stated.

This lemma describes a concrete circuit construction for updating the one-hot encoding of residual languages when reading the next bit. Given a finite binary language L, let R_t be the set of distinct residuals after prefixes of length t (i.e., R_t = {L_u : u ∈ {0,1}^t} where L_u = {v : uv ∈ L}). The one-hot encoding uses D_t = |R_t| Boolean variables x_R with exactly one set to 1 (the current residual). For the next bit b, we want to compute the new one-hot vector y_Q over R_{t+1}. The construction defines P_b(Q) = {R ∈ R_t : the b-successor of R is Q}, then z_{Q,b} = OR_{R∈P_b(Q)} x_R. Since exactly one x_R is 1, exactly one z_{Q,b} is 1 (the one corresponding to the b-successor of the active residual). The output y_Q = (¬b ∧ z_{Q,0}) ∨ (b ∧ z_{Q,1}) then has exactly one 1. The gate count: for each bit value b, the sets P_b(Q) partition R_t, so the OR trees use at most D_t gates total per b, hence ≤ 2D_t. Each destination Q uses two ANDs and one OR: 3D_{t+1}. Plus one NOT for ¬b: total ≤ 2D_t + 3D_{t+1} + 1. This is correct as a conditional bound - no claim that D_t is small. Scope is correctly stated.

This lemma describes a trivial but correct streaming machine: an N-bit register plus a length counter. On each incoming bit b, the machine writes b to the counter-th position of the register and increments the counter. The state consists of N register bits + log N counter bits = O(N) state bits. The transition circuit: for each position i (0 to N-1), a multiplexer that writes the new bit when counter = i, otherwise preserves the old bit. This can be implemented with O(N) fan-in-two gates (one-hot counter + controlled writes). The induction proof is sound: after k steps, the first k cells contain the prefix, the rest are unchanged (initial padding). After N steps, the register equals the full input word. The final acceptance is a membership test [p ∈ F]. The lemma correctly notes this gives no bound on the final membership predicate circuit, so it does not yield a small MCSP decision circuit or EXT-to-H_C reduction. No counterexample exists - this is a correct construction for any finite F. Scope correctly stated.

This lemma describes a correct streaming filter for an explicitly given finite family of circuits. The construction maintains K bits z_i indicating whether circuit C_i matches the prefix so far. On reading bit b at position j, each z_i is updated to z_i AND (e_{i,j} == b), which requires exactly one fan-in-2 AND gate per circuit (total K gates). The acceptance predicate is OR_i z_i, implementable as a binary OR tree using K-1 fan-in-2 OR gates (or 0 when K=0). The induction proof is sound: initially all z_i=1 (empty prefix matches all circuits); the update preserves the invariant that z_i=1 iff C_i agrees with the prefix through the current position. The scope is correctly limited: it assumes the position-dependent bits e_{i,j} are supplied as constants (preprocessing not bounded), and does not yield a polynomial-in-s implementation for EXT_{n,s} where the family Im(Eval_{n,s}) is implicit and exponentially large. No counterexample exists - this is a correct explicit construction.

This is a correct set-theoretic identity about residual functions. For any F ⊆ {0,1}^N, prefix p of length t, and bit b, the residual set R_{t+1}(pb) = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bu ∈ R_t(p)} by definition of concatenation and the residual R_t(p) = {u : pu ∈ F}. The proof uses only associativity of string concatenation and extensionality of sets. The equivalence EXT_F(pb)=1 ⇔ R_{t+1}(pb) ≠ ∅ follows immediately. The scope is correctly stated: this is a semantic identity that holds for all F, but provides no computational efficiency when F = Im(Eval_{n,s}) is implicit. The barrier analysis is accurate: it is relativizing (oracle-independent), not natural (no largeness/easiness), not algebrizing, not localizing. No counterexample exists - this is a basic mathematical fact about string languages.

This is a standard and correct Myhill-Nerode style characterization for layered streaming automata on finite fixed-length languages. The proof is sound: (1) Lower bound: if R_t(p) ≠ R_t(q), there exists u in their symmetric difference, so exactly one of p·u and q·u is in F. Any deterministic automaton with the same state after p and q would give identical acceptance on u, a contradiction. Thus at least r_t distinct states are needed at level t. (2) Upper bound: using the distinct residual sets as states works; the transition R_{t+1}(p·b) = {u: b·u ∈ R_t(p)} is well-defined and correct. At level N, acceptance is whether the residual contains the empty string. The scope correctly notes this gives no efficient encoding for F = Im(Eval_{n,s}). No counterexample exists.

The construction is correct: E_t(p) = OR_{z} H(pz) by definition of existence. Fixing the first t wires of H to p and the remaining N-t wires to a specific suffix z does not increase gate count. With q=2^{N-t} copies of H, we have qT gates for the copies and q-1 gates for a binary OR tree, total q(T+1)-1. The child estimate follows: each child needs q/2 copies, so total for both children is 2[(q/2)T + (q/2 -1)] = q(T+1)-2. The construction is uniform in H,p and exponential in the unobserved suffix length, which the scope correctly notes. No counterexample exists; the size bound is tight up to constants.

Statement is correct. For each length-t prefix p with R_p != emptyset, the extension set E_p = {f in F : f[0:t] = p} is nonempty. For distinct p,q at the same level these sets are disjoint (an N-bit string has exactly one length-t prefix), so the number of viable prefixes is at most |F| and also at most 2^t; distinct nonempty residuals are bounded by the number of viable prefixes, hence <= min(2^t, |F|). All empty residuals equal emptyset, so at most one distinct empty residual. Transition: z in R_{pb} iff pbz in F iff bz in R_p, well-defined and independent of the representative prefix. Layered residual automaton recognizes F exactly (standard Myhill-Nerode residual argument); the proof's 'distinct prefixes have distinct extensions' is read as the disjoint nonempty extension-set argument, which is valid. Scope correctly limited to finite fixed-length languages, no efficient transition computation or polynomial bound claimed for F = Im(Eval_{n,s}). Barriers: relativizing (oracle-independent combinatorics), not natural, not algebrizing, not localizing; no P-vs-NP circumvention claimed. No counterexample exists.

Lower bound: if R_p != R_q, exists z in symmetric diff; exactly one of pz,qz in F; common state on z gives same output -> contradiction. Upper bound: use residuals as states; transition R_p -> {z:bz in R_p} = R_{pb} well-defined. No counterexample found for any finite F. Scope exact: fixed-length, deterministic, layered streaming only.

Construction correct: states = P(F) U {bottom}, transition to pb if pb in P(F) else bottom, initial empty prefix viable since F nonempty. Induction shows state after input p is p if p in P(F) else bottom; acceptance = viable prefix. Bound |P(F)| <= 1+MN holds (each of M strings contributes <= N nonempty prefixes); plus dead state gives <= 2+MN states. Each distinct residual needs distinct state. Upper bound: use residuals as states; transition R_p -> {z: bz in R_p} = R_{pb} well-defined. At level N accept nonempty residual. Counting argument correct: at depth t there are at most 2^t prefixes, and each residual is determined by the subset of M strings extending p (at most 2^M subsets). So distinct residuals <= min(2^t, 2^M). Sum over t gives total depth-labelled residual states. Transition on bit b: retain suffixes starting with b, delete first bit - well-defined on residual sets. Correctly notes this bounds state count only, not transition computation cost. No counterexample found.

Each affine function f(x)=c+sum a_i x_i corresponds to coefficient vector (c,a_1,...,a_n) in GF(2)^(n+1). Prefix p gives t equations c+sum a_i x_i^(j)=p_j. Extendible iff system consistent. Incremental row-echelon basis maintains solution set exactly. Appending one equation and eliminating pivot preserves solution set; contradiction row iff no extension. Basis has <= n+1 rows of length n+2; insertion/elimination O((n+1)^2) bit ops. Correct for affine subclass only. Identity Ext_F(p) = {r_{f,t}: f in A_F(p)} is correct: q in Ext_F(p) iff pq is truth table of some f in F iff f agrees with p on first t bits (so f in A_F(p)) and its suffix r_{f,t} equals q. Both set inclusions hold. If A_F(p)=A_F(p') then Ext_F(p)=Ext_F(p'). Nonempty Ext_F(p) iff nonempty A_F(p). Standard Myhill-Nerode argument for fixed-length streaming: if R_t(p) != R_t(p'), pick q in symmetric difference; exactly one of pq, p'q in F. Same state after p and p' implies same output on q by determinism, contradiction. Thus distinct residuals need distinct states. State-bit lower bound is ceil(log2 max_t |{R_t(p)}|). Bound is correct: at most 2^t prefixes total. Each word in F has unique length-t prefix, so nonempty residuals partition F into nonempty parts, at most |F| parts. At most one empty residual. proved_step: Let L⊆{0,1}^N be decided by a Boolean circuit H of size h, and let EXT_L(p) mean that p has an accepted completion in L. For any cut t<N, the transition output EXT_L(pb), for a prefix p of length t and next bit b, is computable by a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^(N-t-1)(h+1)-1. Proof: for each suffix q of length N-t-1, make a copy of H with its first t+1 inputs fixed to pb and its remaining inputs fixed to q; OR the 2^(N-t-1) outputs with a binary tree. This accepts exactly when some completion pq is in L. The bound counts h gates per copy and 2^(N-t-1)-1 OR gates. This explicit construction gives no polynomial transition-cost bound from an arbitrary decision circuit H_C.

Distinct residuals have distinct representative prefixes, since a prefix determines exactly one residual, so these chosen words are distinct. Thus there are at most |F| nonempty residuals; including the empty residual gives at most |F|+1 states.
