proved_step: BLOCK-TRANSITION EXPANSION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates (constants and input wiring are free). Fix integers t,r with 0<=t<=N and 0<=r<=N-t. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t and block u in {0,1}^r, define E_{t+r}(pu)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-r} such that H(puz)=1. There is a circuit B_{t,r} on (p,u) computing E_{t+r}(pu) with at most 2^{N-t-r}(h+1)-1 fan-in-two gates. Proof: For each suffix z of length N-t-r, make a disjoint copy H_z of H; wire its first t+r input positions to (p,u), and wire its remaining positions to the constant string z. OR all 2^{N-t-r} output bits using a binary tree, which uses 2^{N-t-r}-1 gates. The total is 2^{N-t-r}h+(2^{N-t-r}-1)=2^{N-t-r}(h+1)-1 gates. For every (p,u), this OR is 1 exactly when at least one completion z makes H(puz)=1. Thus if N-t-r<=c log_2(h+2) for fixed c, the size is polynomial in h. This constructs the block-completion predicate only; it does not show that a compact state or transition can be computed from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits at cost poly(s).

evidence: Explicit construction with 2^k copies and a binary OR tree; correctness follows by the definition of existential projection.
proved_step: FIXED-TAIL PROJECTION WITH POLYNOMIAL COST. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have a fan-in-two circuit of h gates, and let 0<=k<=N. Define P_k(x)=OR_{z in {0,1}^k} H(xz), for x in {0,1}^{N-k}. Then P_k has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^k(h+1)-1 gates. If k<=c log_2(h+2) for fixed c>=0, its size is at most (h+2)^c(h+1)-1, hence O((h+2)^(c+1)). Proof: For each of the 2^k strings z, create a disjoint copy H_z of H, wire its final k inputs to z and its first N-k inputs to x. OR the outputs with a fan-in-two tree using 2^k-1 gates. The total is 2^k h+2^k-1. For every x, this OR is 1 exactly when some z satisfies H(xz)=1, so it computes P_k. The logarithmic-tail condition gives 2^k<=(h+2)^c and the stated bound. This is one fixed projection; it implies no polynomial-cost representation for cuts with superlogarithmic remaining suffix.

statement: For any Boolean circuit H:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, any 0<=t<N, and every prefix p in {0,1}^t, define E_t(p)=1 iff some suffix q of length N-t satisfies H(pq)=1. Then E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Proof: Every suffix of length N-t has a unique first bit b in {0,1} and a remaining suffix r of length N-t-1. Thus a completion q with H(pq)=1 exists iff there are b,r with H(pbr)=1, which holds iff E_{t+1}(pb)=1 for at least one b. This identity gives the exact one-bit recurrence for the completion predicate, but does not recover the two child values from E_t(p) or bound the real-gate cost of computing either child from H.
scope: All Boolean circuits H on N input bits, all cuts 0<=t<N, all prefixes p of length t. E_t is existential completion of H. No transition-cost bound or implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits is claimed.

statement: Residual cofactor transition lemma. Let N be a nonnegative integer, F be any subset of {0,1}^N, 0 <= t < N, and p be a length-t prefix. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, define the cofactor D_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. Then R_{t+1}(pb)=D_b(R_t(p)). Consequently, if R_t(p)=R_t(q) for two length-t prefixes p,q, then for each bit b their child residuals are equal; and the pair of child residuals is determined by the full parent residual. Proof: For every v of length N-t-1, v is in R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbv is in F. This is equivalent to bv being in R_t(p), which is equivalent to v being in D_b(R_t(p)). Thus the sets agree. Replacing p by q gives the equal-child consequence when parent residuals coincide. The formula defines each child from the full residual by restriction to strings beginning in b. In contrast, the single bit [R_t(p) is nonempty] need not determine either child bit: for N-t=1, residuals {0} and {1} both have nonempty indicator 1, but their 0-child acceptance indicators differ. This is an exact information-level transition rule; it does not bound the number or real-gate cost of operations needed to compute a cofactor when the representation is an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All finite binary languages F subset {0,1}^N, all 0 <= t < N, and all prefixes p of length t. Residuals are literal suffix sets; cofactor operation is D_b(R)={v:bv in R}. No circuit-size, transition-cost, or P versus NP consequence is claimed.

statement: Residual-circuit restriction lemma. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For every t in {0,...,N} and prefix p in {0,1}^t, define H_p:{0,1}^{N-t}->{0,1} by H_p(q)=H(pq). Then H_p is computed by a circuit with at most h gates, obtained by fixing the first t input wires of H to the bits of p. If t<N and b is a bit, H_{pb}(r)=H_p(br), so the child residual circuit also uses at most h gates. Proof: Substitute constants p at the corresponding input wires of H; this changes no gate and computes q -> H(pq). For the child, substitute b at the first remaining input wire of this restricted circuit; again no gate changes, and its output on r is H_p(br)=H(pbr)=H_{pb}(r). Thus both restrictions preserve the gate bound. The representation (H,p) may still require N+t-independent prefix storage up to N bits and this lemma does not bound transitions of a circuit whose input is an arbitrary MCSP decision-circuit description.
scope: All N>=0, all fan-in-two circuits H on N inputs with h gates, and all prefixes p of length t<=N. Constants and input wiring are free; only circuit gate count is bounded. This gives no compact-state or arbitrary-H_C transition-cost theorem.

statement: One-bit branching-information lemma for EXT. Let F be a finite binary language of words of length N, let t<N, and for every length-t prefix p define e(p)=1 iff R_t(p) is nonempty. Define e_0(p)=1 iff R_{t+1}(p0) is nonempty and e_1(p)=1 iff R_{t+1}(p1) is nonempty. Then e(p)=e_0(p) OR e_1(p). If e(p)=0 the child pair is (0,0); if e(p)=1 the possible child pairs are exactly (1,0),(0,1),(1,1). Proof: Partition the suffixes in R_t(p) by their first bit. The 0-section is nonempty exactly when R_{t+1}(p0) is nonempty, and the 1-section exactly when R_{t+1}(p1) is nonempty. Thus the parent is nonempty iff at least one child is nonempty. An empty parent forces (0,0). Each of the other three pairs is realizable by a language whose words extending p have suffixes respectively {0v}, {1v}, or {0v,1v}, for any v of length N-t-1. Hence the one-bit extension summary loses which child branches survive.
scope: All finite F subset {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. This is an information statement about the Boolean extension predicate, not a gate lower bound or a lower bound on richer representations; no P versus NP consequence is claimed.

statement: Cofactor transition identity for EXT. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1}. For each t and p in {0,1}^t define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists q in {0,1}^{N-t} with H(pq)=1. Then for every t<N and p of length t, E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Proof: The set of length-(N-t) completions of p is the disjoint union of strings 0q and 1q, with q ranging over {0,1}^{N-t-1}. Thus some completion pq is accepted exactly when either some completion p0q is accepted or some completion p1q is accepted. This also covers an empty accepting language, for which both sides are zero. The identity specifies the exact Boolean information propagated by the EXT automaton, but does not bound the real-gate cost of obtaining E_{t+1} from an arbitrary MCSP circuit H_C.

statement: Completion-circuit cofactor recurrence. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, and for each 0<=t<=N define E_t(p)=1 iff some suffix u in {0,1}^{N-t} satisfies H(pu)=1. If E_{t+d} is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of g gates, then E_t is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^d(g+1)-1 gates. Proof: For each of the 2^d suffixes v of length d, fix v in a copy of the E_{t+d} circuit, leaving the first t bits as inputs. The outputs compute E_{t+d}(pv); their OR is E_t(p), since every completion of p has a unique first d bits. A binary OR tree combines the 2^d outputs using 2^d-1 gates. The total is 2^d g+(2^d-1)=2^d(g+1)-1. In particular, d=1 gives 2g+1 gates. Constants and wiring are free. This bounds one Boolean completion predicate at a cut; it does not bound computation of the next residual-state encoding of EXT.
scope: All N>=0, cuts t,d with 0<=t<=t+d<=N, and fan-in-two Boolean circuit size with constants and wiring free.
proof: Fix each length-d suffix v, use one copy of the E_{t+d} circuit with v substituted, and OR the outputs. The copies use 2^d*g gates and the binary OR tree uses 2^d-1. Every completion of p has exactly one such v prefix, so this circuit computes E_t.

statement: Penultimate-cut completion bound. Let N>=1 and let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and wiring free. For p in {0,1}^{N-1}, define E(p)=1 iff H(p0)=1 or H(p1)=1. Then E is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2h+1 gates. Proof: Make two copies of the circuit for H. In the first copy fix its Nth input to 0; in the second fix it to 1. The resulting circuits compute p↦H(p0) and p↦H(p1), each using at most h gates. Feed their outputs to one OR gate. The output is E(p) by its definition, and the total gate count is at most h+h+1. This is the EXT completion predicate at the sole cut with one unprocessed bit; it gives no bound at earlier cuts.
scope: Every integer N>=1, every Boolean H on N bits with a fan-in-two circuit of h gates; constants and wiring are free.

statement: Dense residual streaming cost lemma. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be given by a fan-in-two circuit of h gates. A deterministic left-to-right streaming representation can initialize an N-stage residual table using at most h·2^N gate evaluations, store at most 2^N bits, and update it over the entire input using exactly 2^N−1 bit selections/writes (and no Boolean gates), if a state is represented as an explicit array indexed by suffixes and coordinate selection is the unit-cost update operation. Proof: At depth t store the array A_t[u]=H(pu), for all suffixes u of length N−t, where p is the prefix read so far. Initialize A_0 by evaluating H on each of the 2^N inputs, costing at most h·2^N gates and storing 2^N output bits. Upon reading b, form A_{t+1}[u]=A_t[bu] for each suffix u of length N−t−1. The identity follows directly: A_t[bu]=H(pbu)=A_{t+1}[u]. Thus each update copies one half of the old array and costs 2^(N−t−1) coordinate selections/writes. Summing over t=0,...,N−1 gives Σ_{j=0}^{N−1}2^j=2^N−1. The largest stored array is A_0, of 2^N bits. The update bound is in the stated explicit-array access model; it is not a fan-in-two Boolean circuit bound or a compact/poly(s) representation.
scope: All N≥0 and Boolean H with an h-gate fan-in-two circuit. Resource units are specified explicitly: Boolean gate evaluations for initialization, explicit stored bits, and unit-cost array coordinate selections/writes for updates.

statement: SIMULTANEOUS BLOCK-COFACTOR CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and input wiring free. For integers 0<=t<=N and 0<=b<=N-t, set k=N-t-b. There is a fan-in-two circuit with t input bits p and 2^b outputs indexed by u in {0,1}^b, whose u-output is 1 iff some v in {0,1}^k satisfies H(puv)=1. Its gate count is at most 2^{N-t}h+2^{N-t}-2^b. Proof: for every pair (u,v), make a disjoint copy of H with first t inputs wired to p and remaining inputs fixed to uv, giving 2^{b+k}h=2^{N-t}h gates. For each u, OR its 2^k outputs using a fan-in-two tree of 2^k-1 gates (zero gates if k=0), giving 2^b(2^k-1)=2^{N-t}-2^b further gates. The output for u computes the required existential cofactor; summing gives the bound. Direct enumeration makes the construction uniform. This is a per-cut construction only, not a polynomial early-cut bound or an MCSP lower bound.
scope: All N-bit Boolean circuits H and cuts/blocks 0<=t, 0<=b<=N-t; fan-in-two gate size, constants and wiring free.
evidence: Complete copy-and-OR derivation; no finite computation is used.

BINARY RESIDUAL PARTITION LEMMA. Let N>=1, L be a subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p in {0,1}^t. Define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in L. Then E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Proof: Every completion u has a unique decomposition u=bv, where b is a bit and v is a suffix of length N-t-1. There exists u with pu in L iff there exists b and v with pbv in L. This is equivalent to E_{t+1}(p0)=1 or E_{t+1}(p1)=1, by definition. When t=N-1, v is the empty string, so the boundary case is included. This is only a semantic recurrence and gives no real-gate cost bound from an arbitrary circuit H_C.

statement: Residual membership update lemma. Let L be a language of words of length N, let p have length t<N, and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in L}. For b in {0,1} and u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, the next residual membership bit satisfies 1[u in R_{t+1}(pb)] = 1[bu in R_t(p)]. Thus membership in the next residual is computable with one membership query to the current residual, by prefixing the queried suffix with b. Proof: u belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu belongs to L; this holds iff bu belongs to R_t(p), by the definition of R_t(p). This is an oracle-query identity only; it gives no bound on the real-gate cost of representing or querying R_t(p) from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All fixed-length binary languages L subseteq {0,1}^N, all 0<=t<N, all length-t prefixes p, incoming bits b, and suffixes u of length N-t-1.

statement: Restricted-circuit residual bound. Fix N,h≥0 and a fan-in-two Boolean circuit H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} with h gates; constants and wiring are free. For every t∈{0,…,N} and p∈{0,1}^t, let R_t(p)={q∈{0,1}^{N−t}:H(pq)=1}. Then R_t(p) is computed by a circuit H_p on N−t inputs with at most h gates, obtained by substituting p into H. Under a topological encoding listing each gate type and its two predecessor indices, plus the output source, the number D_t of distinct residuals is at most (c(N+h+2)^2)^(h+1) for an absolute constant c. Each residual has a description of O((h+1)log(N+h+2)) bits. Proof: Substituting p for the first t input wires leaves all h gate operations unchanged, so H_p computes q↦H(pq). For the count, each gate chooses one of finitely many types and two sources among at most N+h+2 possibilities; the output chooses one source from that set. Thus the number of descriptions is at most (c(N+h+2)^2)^(h+1). Each description computes at most one residual, which proves the bound. A description can be stored using O((h+1)log(N+h+2)) bits. This is an information bound only: it gives no polynomial-in-(h,n) bound when N=2^n and no real-gate transition circuit for canonical encodings.

proved_step: statement: Candidate-set transition lemma for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite enumeration C_{n,s} of all Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with a fixed ordering of their 2^n truth-table positions. For a prefix p of length t define V_t(p)={C in C_{n,s}: the first t outputs of C equal p}. Then V_{t+1}(pb)={C in V_t(p): C's output at position t+1 equals b}. Consequently V_t(p) is nonempty iff p is an extendible prefix of a size-at-most-s circuit truth table, and the transition rule recognizes EXT exactly. Proof: By definition, C belongs to V_{t+1}(pb) exactly when its first t outputs equal p and its (t+1)st output equals b. The first condition is C in V_t(p), and the second is the stated filter predicate, proving equality. Nonemptiness is equivalent to existence of a circuit completion, which is the definition of EXT. This is an exact information representation and transition identity; it makes no polynomial bound on representing V_t(p), testing the filter, or implementing transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

evidence: The step correctly states the Myhill-Nerode theorem for fixed-length languages. The forward direction (distinct residuals require distinct states) holds by definition of exact acceptance. The converse construction (residual sets as states with transition R_t(p) --b--> R_{t+1}(pb)) is well-defined because R_{t+1}(pb) = {r : pbr ∈ F} = {r : br ∈ R_t(p)}. At depth N, residuals are {ε} for accepted words and ∅ otherwise. The scope note correctly identifies that this abstract characterization does not bound gate-level transition costs for implementations using MCSP decision circuits. No counterexample exists for the mathematical claim as stated.

The construction is correct: for each of the 2^{N-t} suffixes q, a copy H_q of H with suffix inputs hardwired to q computes H(pq). OR-ing all outputs with a binary tree yields EXT_L(p). Gate count is exactly 2^{N-t}h + (2^{N-t}-1) = 2^{N-t}(h+1)-1. The scope note correctly acknowledges this is exponential in the remaining suffix length and does not yield a streaming update or poly(s) bound for early cuts. No mathematical error in the claim as stated.

The arithmetic is correct: 2^k copies of H (size h each) plus a binary OR tree (2^k-1 gates) gives 2^k(h+1)-1 total. For k ≤ c log₂(h+2), we have 2^k ≤ (h+2)^c, so total size ≤ (h+2)^c(h+1) = O((h+2)^{c+1}). If h = poly(s) and k = O(log s), this is poly(s). The scope note correctly limits the claim to cuts with logarithmic remaining suffix and acknowledges it does not bound early-cut complexity, streaming updates, or arbitrary MCSP circuits. No counterexample to the mathematical statement.

This is the standard Myhill-Nerode theorem for fixed-length languages (the truncation in the transcript doesn't affect the verifiable core). The lower bound holds because any exact deterministic machine must distinguish prefixes with different continuation sets. The upper bound construction uses residuals as states with transition R_L(p) --b--> R_L(pb), which is well-defined since R_L(pb) = {u : pbu ∈ L} = {u : bu ∈ R_L(p)}. The minimum state count at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residuals. The statement is mathematically correct as far as given.

gap: Whether an EXT transition can be implemented with bounded real-gate cost from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C remains open; the lemma narrows the question by showing complete-input membership queries alone can require 2^(N-|p|) queries in the black-box model.
proved_step: statement: Black-box completion-query lower bound. For every k>=0, any deterministic exact algorithm that decides whether an unknown set F subseteq {0,1}^k is nonempty, with access only to membership queries x -> 1[x in F], requires 2^k queries in the worst case. Proof: Run the algorithm against the all-zero oracle (F=empty). If it makes fewer than 2^k queries, choose an unqueried u. The same transcript occurs for F={u}, although the correct outputs differ, contradiction. Querying all strings suffices. Hence for a prefix with k remaining bits, black-box membership access on completed strings alone gives no worst-case exact prefix-extension procedure using fewer than 2^k queries. This is an oracle-model bound only and makes no assertion about real-gate cost when the circuit or structure of F is available.

statement: Explicit circuit construction for prefix extension. Let N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and let H be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size h and depth d deciding membership in F. For a prefix p of length t and k=N-t remaining bits, an exact circuit deciding whether p has an accepted completion is obtained by instantiating H on each of the 2^k strings pu and ORing the outputs in a binary tree. Its size is at most 2^k h+(2^k-1) and its depth is at most d+k. Proof: for each u in {0,1}^k, the corresponding copy outputs 1 exactly when pu is in F. Their disjunction is 1 exactly when some completion belongs to F. There are 2^k copies, costing 2^k h gates, and a binary OR tree on 2^k outputs uses 2^k-1 gates and depth k (with the k=0 case using one copy and no OR gates). This supplies a real-gate upper-bound baseline from an arbitrary complete-input decider; it gives no matching lower bound for structured EXT_{n,s}.

statement: Nondeterministic verifier for prefix extension. Let N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and let H be a Boolean circuit of size h deciding membership in F. For a prefix p of length t and k=N-t remaining bits, there is a nondeterministic circuit verifier of size h+O(N) that accepts exactly when p has an extension in F: guess u in {0,1}^k, fix the first t inputs of H to p, and evaluate H on pu. Proof: an accepting guess u exists iff H(pu)=1 for some u of length k, which by the correctness of H is equivalent to existence of an accepted completion. Fixing the prefix inputs requires at most linear wiring/input-gate overhead; the circuit H is evaluated once. Thus extension has a compact existential representation from any complete-input decider, while this gives no comparable deterministic circuit bound.

statement: DNF restriction lemma. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF on N Boolean variables with L total literal occurrences. For any prefix p of length t, the extension predicate E_p(u)=H(pu) has a DNF with at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences. Construct it by deleting every term falsified by a fixed prefix literal, then deleting the remaining fixed prefix literals. Proof: each term on input pu is false if one of its fixed literals is false; otherwise it equals the conjunction of its unfixed literals. Disjoining these term identities gives H(pu)=E_p(u). The construction scans the literals once, so takes O(L+h) inspections and has circuit size O(L+h) with binary fan-in gates. Empty terms and an empty disjunction represent true and false, respectively. This proves a linear-cost prefix transition for explicit DNF membership circuits; it gives no such bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

statement: Existential projection lemma for explicit DNF. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF on N Boolean variables, with L total literal occurrences, and split variables into a prefix a and suffix u. Define E(a)=1 iff there exists u with H(a,u)=1. Construct E by deleting each term whose prefix literals conflict with a, and then deleting every suffix literal from each remaining term. The resulting DNF has at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences. Proof: For fixed a and each term T_j, if a falsifies one of its prefix literals then T_j(a,u)=0 for every u. Otherwise its prefix literals are true, and there exists a suffix u satisfying the remaining suffix literals: each variable occurs with a single polarity within a term, so set those variables accordingly and assign all other suffix variables arbitrarily. Thus this term contributes to E(a) exactly when its prefix literals are all true, which is precisely the projected term after suffix literals are removed. Taking the disjunction proves equality. The construction scans the explicit literals in O(L+h) time and yields a binary fan-in circuit of O(L+h) gates. Scope is existential projection of explicit DNF; no implication for arbitrary circuits.

statement: Repaired existential-projection lemma for explicit DNF. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF over N Boolean variables with L literal occurrences; literals may repeat or include both polarities of a variable. Split variables into prefix a and suffix u. The predicate E(a)=1 iff there exists u with H(a,u)=1 has a DNF with at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences: in each term, delete the term if it contains opposite-polarity literals of any variable or if its prefix literals contradict the fixed a; otherwise remove all suffix literals and retain its prefix literals. Proof: A term with contradictory literals is unsatisfiable. A term whose prefix literals conflict with a is false for every suffix. In every other term, all prefix literals are true under a, and the suffix literals are jointly satisfiable because there is at most one required polarity per suffix variable; choose those required bits and assign remaining bits arbitrarily. Thus the existential projection of each term is exactly its retained prefix conjunction, and existential quantification distributes over finite disjunction. No new terms or literal occurrences are introduced. Scanning the explicit DNF takes O(L+h) time, and the resulting binary-fan-in circuit has O(L+h) gates. Scope: explicit DNF only; this gives no transition-cost bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

evidence: Directly substitute the prefix bits into H. Each substitution changes only input wires, not internal gates; extending a prefix is one more such substitution.
proved_step: statement: Cofactor lemma. Let H be a Boolean circuit with h internal gates computing F on N bits. For every prefix p of length t, the residual function f_p(u)=H(pu) has a circuit with at most h internal gates. For b in {0,1}, f_{pb}(v)=f_p(bv), so the next residual is obtained by fixing one input of the current residual circuit to b. Proof: Substituting constants for input wires leaves the internal gate list unchanged and computes the restricted function. The identity follows from H(pbv)=H((pb)v). Repeating this argument from H gives the claimed bound for every prefix. Scope: point-membership residual functions only; this does not compute whether a residual has any accepting suffix or give a compact state encoding for arbitrary H.

statement: Witness-set transition lemma for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite, explicitly indexed family C_{n,s} of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with a fixed output ordering for each truth table. For every length-t prefix p, define W_p={C in C_{n,s}: the first t truth-table bits of C equal p}. Then EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff W_p is nonempty. For t<N and b in {0,1}, W_{pb}={C in W_p: bit_{t+1}(C)=b}; hence W_p is the disjoint union of W_{p0} and W_{p1}. Storing W_p as an explicit bit vector gives an exact deterministic EXT streaming algorithm with at most |C_{n,s}| bits of state; its transition on b scans the indexed circuits and retains exactly those whose (t+1)-st truth-table bit equals b, and final acceptance tests nonemptiness. Proof: By definition, C belongs to W_{pb} exactly when its first t bits equal p and its next bit equals b, which is equivalent to C belonging to W_p and bit_{t+1}(C)=b. Every C in W_p has exactly one next output bit, so the two child sets are disjoint and partition W_p. Nonemptiness of W_p is equivalent to existence of a size-at-most-s circuit with truth-table prefix p, which is the definition of EXT. The explicit transition is correct by the membership equivalence. This is an exact constructive representation, but its state and transition costs are governed by |C_{n,s}|; the lemma makes no polynomial-cost claim and gives no simulation by an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: Finite circuit family with a fixed canonical enumeration and truth-table bit order; exact prefix recognition; no circuit-complexity upper bound beyond explicit witness-set enumeration.

statement: Explicit witness-mask update bound for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite enumerated circuit family C_{n,s} of size M, with each circuit’s truth-table bits in a fixed order. Encode the current prefix residual by an M-bit vector z, where z_j=1 exactly when circuit j agrees with the prefix read so far. For each position i and input bit b, the next-state vector is z'_j=z_j AND [bit_i(C_j)=b]. This is an exact deterministic update using at most M binary AND gates (the bracketed values are constants), and the state uses M bits. Initially z is all ones; after the full truth table, z is nonzero exactly when the input belongs to EXT_{n,s}. Proof: Inductively, after t bits z_j=1 iff circuit j agrees with the first t bits. The displayed update preserves that invariant for t+1 by testing precisely the next bit. At t=N, nonemptiness is equivalent to existence of a size-at-most-s circuit generating the input truth table. This gives an explicit O(M)-gate per-bit upper bound for the witness-set representation; it does not give a bound polynomial in s, nor a construction from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: Finite explicitly enumerated circuit families with fixed truth-table ordering; deterministic exact streaming; gate count is for the update with circuit truth-table bits available as constants, and M=|C_{n,s}|.

statement: Explicit candidate-mask update bound for EXT. Fix N≥1 and a finite, explicitly listed family C={C_1,...,C_M} of Boolean circuits, each producing an N-bit string in a fixed order. At position t, store the M-bit mask A_t whose i-th bit is 1 exactly when C_i agrees with the prefix read so far. On reading b∈{0,1}, update each bit by A_{t+1}[i]=A_t[i] ∧ [C_i(t+1)=b]. This update is realizable with at most M fan-in-two AND gates once the position-t output bits C_i(t+1) are available; if those bits are computed from the circuit descriptions during the update, their evaluation cost must be added. The state is exact: A_t is nonzero iff the read prefix is extendible to a member of C, and induction on t proves the invariant. Thus explicit enumeration gives an exact per-bit transition bound of M plus the cost of obtaining the M predicted bits, but does not yield a polynomial-in-s transition bound when M is the number of size-at-most-s circuits.
scope: Finite explicitly enumerated candidate families with deterministic Boolean circuits and a fixed output-bit order; fan-in-two update gates. No claim that M or the total transition cost is polynomial in s, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
proof: Initially set every mask bit to 1, since the empty prefix agrees with every candidate. Suppose the stored invariant holds after t bits. For candidate i, it agrees with the extended prefix ending in b exactly when it agreed with the length-t prefix and its (t+1)-st output bit equals b. This is precisely the stated AND update, so the invariant holds by induction. A nonzero mask is equivalent to at least one listed candidate agreeing with the prefix, which is exactly extendibility within the listed family. Each updated bit is one binary conjunction, giving M fan-in-two gates after the predicted bits are available. If those bits are not supplied, their computation is a separate cost and cannot be omitted.

gap: G001: Bridge from EXT residual quotient to arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C. The residual automaton gives minimum state count but no bound on transition cost when the transition function is computed from an arbitrary H_C that decides membership in Im(Eval). The candidate-mask S0600 gives an explicit O(M) update for an enumerated family of size M, but M is exponential in s. A lemma is needed that either (a) shows a polynomial-in-s transition bound for EXT transitions using some representation of the residual classes that works for all H_C, or (b) proves a superpolynomial lower bound on the transition cost from arbitrary H_C under a well-defined model. Current open obligation: construct or refute such a bound for a stated subclass (e.g., read-once H_C, or H_C with bounded communication across the prefix cut).

evidence: The set identity is exact and verified: v ∈ R_{t+1}(pb) ⇔ pbv ∈ F ⇔ bv ∈ R_t(p) by definition of R_t. The disjoint union follows because every string u of length N-t has a unique first bit b and suffix v, so u belongs to exactly one of 0R_{t+1}(p0) or 1R_{t+1}(p1). No counterexample exists; the argument is a tautological unfolding of the definition. Scope matches: it proves the abstract transition identity for any F, including EXT, and correctly states it gives no gate-cost bound from H_C.

gap: G002: After the residual-section identity (S0477, SURVIVED_REVIEW), the open obligation is to bound the REAL-GATE cost of implementing the section operation from an arbitrary H_C. The residual automaton gives optimal state count but no transition complexity bound. The candidate-mask lemma (S0600) gives O(M) gates for an explicit family of M circuits, but M is exponential in s. Need a lemma that either (a) constructs a poly(s, log N) real-gate transition for the EXT residual update using some representation derived from H_C, or (b) proves a superpolynomial lower bound on the transition cost under a well-defined model for a stated subclass (e.g., H_C with bounded communication across the prefix-suffix cut).

proved_step:
statement: Lemma: For any fixed layer t, the EXT_{n,s} transition function T_t: R_t(p) × {0,1} → R_{t+1}(pb) can be realized as a projection of the evaluation of H_C on all suffixes of length N-t-1, but no representation of the residual class as a Boolean circuit of size polynomial in s and log N is known that works for every H_C. In particular, if H_C is an arbitrary circuit deciding membership in Im(Eval), then the map from H_C to a circuit computing T_t may require solving circuit equivalence or existential quantification over circuits of size ≤ s, which is not known to be in P. Therefore, the existence of a uniform poly(s, log N) real-gate transition for EXT from arbitrary H_C remains open, and the candidate-mask bound (S0600) is tight for the explicit enumeration approach.
scope: Arbitrary Boolean circuits H_C deciding EXT_{n,s}; real-gate complexity of the transition function T_t as a function of s and N=2^n. No claim that the transition cannot be done in poly(s) gates, only that no such construction is known and the explicit enumeration gives an exponential upper bound.
proof: The transition T_t on input b maps a residual class R = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pu ∈ Im(Eval)} to R_b = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bv ∈ R}. By S0477, R_b = {v : pbv ∈ Im(Eval)}. This set is exactly the set of suffixes v such that H_C(pbv) = 1. A circuit for T_t must therefore compute, from a description of R and b, a description of R_b. The candidate-mask construction (S0600) does this by explicitly tracking agreement with all M = |Im(Eval) ∩ {0,1}^N| candidates, giving M AND gates. Any representation that avoids enumerating all candidates must implicitly perform existential quantification over circuits of size ≤ s to determine which suffixes remain consistent. Since H_C is an arbitrary decision circuit (not necessarily an evaluation circuit), no poly(s) translation from H_C to a transition circuit is known. This is not a lower bound; it is a precise statement of the current knowledge gap.

evidence: The identity R_{t+1}(pb) = {v : bv in R_t(p)} holds by definition of residual sets and string concatenation: v in R_{t+1}(pb) <=> pbv in F <=> bv in {u : pu in F} = R_t(p). This is an exact set-theoretic equivalence valid for every F subset of {0,1}^N, every prefix p, and every bit b. No counterexample exists; the proof is a direct unfolding of definitions.

The argument is a standard Myhill-Nerode style distinguishability proof for streaming automata. If two prefixes p,q have different residual sets R_t(p) != R_t(q), there exists a suffix u in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pu, qu is in F. If the machine reaches the same state after p and q, its deterministic continuation on u yields the same acceptance for both, contradicting that exactly one is in F. Therefore distinct residuals require distinct states. With B state bits there are at most 2^B states, so 2^B >= r_t, giving B >= ceil(log2 r_t). This is exact and unconditional for deterministic exact streaming recognition of any finite language F. No counterexample exists.

The construction is the standard residual (Myhill-Nerode) automaton for finite languages, layered by prefix length. Well-definedness of transitions: if R(p)=R(q) then for any b, R(pb)={u: bv in R(p)} = {u: bv in R(q)} = R(qb) by the residual-section identity (S0477). The automaton accepts exactly F by induction on prefix length. Minimality follows from S0478: any exact deterministic streaming recognizer must distinguish different residuals, so needs at least r_t states at layer t. This construction achieves exactly r_t. The step correctly notes it gives no bound on transition computation cost from an arbitrary H_C. No counterexample exists; the proof is a direct verification of definitions.

This step specializes the general lower bound (S0478) to the specific language L = EXT_{n,s} (prefixes of truth tables of size-s circuits). The reasoning is identical: if R_p != R_q, there exists a suffix z in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pz, qz is a prefix of a size-s circuit truth table. If the machine reaches the same state after p and q, its deterministic continuation on z gives the same answer for both, contradiction. Therefore distinct residuals require distinct states. The count of distinct residual sets over all prefix lengths gives the total state count lower bound. This is a correct instantiation of the general Myhill-Nerode argument to EXT_{n,s}. No counterexample exists; the step correctly notes it does not bound transition gate cost or give a simulation from arbitrary H_C.

Lower bound is S0478 (distinguishability) and upper bound is S0479 (residual quotient automaton). The two directions together give exact minimum r_t states. The statement correctly limits scope to deterministic layered streaming automata and makes no claim about transition cost. No counterexample exists.

This is a standard Myhill-Nerode / residual distinguishability argument applied to the specific language L = EXT_{n,s}. The proof is correct: if two prefixes p,q have different residual sets R_{p,t} ≠ R_{q,t}, there exists a suffix z in their symmetric difference. Since both prefixes have length t, the same suffix z has length N-t and reaches the same subsequent positions. Exactly one of pz, qz is a complete truth table in the target family. A deterministic streaming machine that correctly decides membership must therefore be in different states after reading p and q; otherwise determinism would force the same final output on both pz and qz, a contradiction. The state lower bound |{R_{p,t}}| and bit lower bound ceil(log2 |{R_{p,t}}|) follow directly. No counterexample exists; this is a fundamental property of deterministic automata. The scope limitation (state-width only, no transition-cost or H_C simulation bounds) is explicitly acknowledged and correct.

This is the standard Myhill-Nerode theorem for deterministic streaming automata over finite languages. The proof is correct: (1) Distinct residuals force distinct states - if R_p ≠ R_q, pick u in their symmetric difference; then exactly one of pu, qu is in F, and determinism with the same state after p,q would give the same acceptance, contradiction. (2) The residual sets themselves form a valid deterministic layered automaton - the transition R → {v : bv ∈ R} is exactly the residual update, and induction on prefix length shows exactness. (3) Minimality - any correct automaton must distinguish prefixes with different residuals, so the number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residuals {R_p : |p|=t}. No counterexample exists; this is a classical result. The scope limitation (no transition circuit cost bounds, no H_C simulation) is correctly stated.

This correctly describes the transition function for the explicit candidate-vector representation of the EXT prefix automaton. At stream position t, the state is a K-bit vector z where z_i = 1 iff candidate C_i matches the prefix so far. Given the next input bit b, the new state is z'_i = z_i ∧ [C_i(t) = b]. Since c_i = [C_i(t) = b] is a position-dependent constant (0 or 1) hardwired for that transition, each coordinate is either z_i (when c_i=1) or constant 0 (when c_i=0) - no fan-in-2 gates needed. The acceptance readout at the end is OR_i z_i, which takes K-1 fan-in-2 OR gates in a binary tree (0 for K=1). This is an exact decomposition for this specific representation. The claimed scope is correct: it gives no polynomial-in-s bound when K is exponential, and no simulation through arbitrary H_C circuits. No counterexample exists for the stated representation.

This is a standard DNF construction bound for encoding transitions of a finite automaton. For each of the r output bits, we build a DNF over the m state bits + 1 input bit. There are at most 2D valid (state, input) pairs that map to output 1. Each minterm uses ≤ m AND gates (on m+1 literals including the input bit), OR of t terms costs t-1 gates, and shared input negations cost ≤ m+1. Total per output: ≤ mt + (t-1) + (m+1) ≤ 2Dm + 2D + m (since t ≤ 2D). Multiply by r outputs. This correctly repairs the earlier S0431 inequality. The construction works for any deterministic delta_0, delta_1. The bound is on the encoded transition function on valid codes only (invalid codes can be arbitrary). No counterexample exists for this construction.

This is a direct definitional equivalence. EXT_H(p) is defined as 1 iff ∃z∈{0,1}^{N-t} such that pz ∈ F. Since H decides F, H(pz)=1 exactly when pz∈F. The set of all extensions of p is exactly {pu : u∈{0,1}^{N-t}} by definition of concatenation. Therefore EXT_H(p) = ⋁_{u∈{0,1}^{N-t}} H(pu). The same reasoning with pb gives EXT_H(pb) = ⋁_{u∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}} H(pbu). No counterexample exists because this is a tautology from the definitions. The scope limitation about no bounded-call reduction for arbitrary H is correctly stated as a separate observation, not part of the mathematical claim.

This correctly describes the NP verification procedure for EXT_{n,s}(p). The witness is a circuit description d of length L = O(s log(n+s)). The verifier: (1) checks d is a valid fan-in-2 circuit description with ≤ s gates (O(L) time), (2) for each of t input strings x_i = bin_n(i), evaluates C_d(x_i) in topological order (O(s+n) per evaluation, total O(t(s+n))), (3) compares each output to p[i]. This accepts iff ∃ circuit C of size ≤ s with prefix p. The time bound O(t(s+n)+L) is correct for standard gate-list encoding where input access is O(n) (reading the binary string of length n). No counterexample exists - this is a standard NP verification argument. The scope limitations are correctly stated.

This is a correct definitional identity for EXT over an explicitly listed family. For any prefix p of length t, the set A = {j : E_j[0..t-1] = p} exactly identifies which circuits in the list match p. A circuit C_j extends p0 iff j ∈ A and E_j[t] = 0; similarly for p1. Therefore EXT_F(p0) = ⋁_{j∈A} [E_j[t] = 0] and EXT_F(p1) = ⋁_{j∈A} [E_j[t] = 1]. The circuit size claim O(M(t+1)(s+n)) for fan-in-2 implementation is also correct: for each j, evaluate C_j on the first t+1 inputs (t prefix + 1 next), which takes O((t+1)(s+n)) gates, compare the first t outputs to p, AND with the (t+1)th output's equality to b, then OR over j. No counterexample exists - this is a direct consequence of the definitions. The scope limitation about not bounding M polynomially is correctly stated.

This is a correct inductive description of the streaming update for an explicitly listed family. The invariant: after reading i bits, a_j = 1 iff C_j agrees with the first i bits of the streamed prefix. Base case (i=0): all a_j = 1, which holds since every circuit agrees with the empty prefix. Inductive step: a'_j = a_j ∧ [C_j(i) = b] correctly maintains the invariant because C_j agrees with the extended prefix iff it agreed with the first i bits (a_j=1) AND its output on input i equals b. The circuit implementation evaluates each C_j on the binary encoding of i (cost O(s+n) per circuit), compares to b (O(1)), ANDs with a_j (O(1)), giving O(d(s+n)) total. The finite check cm-69dd62ee713f4a79 corroborates this for all 256 families of 3-input functions and all 130,816 prefix cases. No counterexample exists - this is a direct consequence of the definitions. The scope limitation about d not being polynomially bounded for the full description set is correctly stated.

This is a tautological set identity for any finite family F ⊆ {0,1}^N. For any prefix p of length t ≤ N, R_p = {z ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pz ∈ F} by definition. For b ∈ {0,1}, R_{pb} = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : pbu ∈ F} = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bu ∈ R_p} (since bu ∈ R_p ⇔ p(bu) = pbu ∈ F). This equality holds by direct substitution of definitions. Nonemptiness of R_p is exactly the condition that ∃z : pz ∈ F, i.e., EXT_F(p)=1. The lemma correctly states this is an information-level identity with no computational cost bounds for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary H_C. No counterexample exists - this is a direct consequence of the definitions of concatenation and set membership.

This correctly describes a fan-in-2 circuit that implements the streaming update for an explicit list of M circuits. The construction: (1) uses the n bits of t as the input x_t = bin_n(t), (2) for each j, evaluates the hardwired circuit C_j on x_t using at most s gates (since C_j has at most s fan-in-2 gates), (3) compares the output c_j with b using [c_j = b] = (c_j AND b) OR (NOT c_j AND NOT b) which takes 3 gates (NOT b shared, NOT c_j, AND, OR), (4) ANDs with a_j (1 gate), (5) increments t modulo 2^n with a ripple incrementer using O(n) gates. Total per candidate: s + 4 gates, plus O(n) for the counter. The invariant holds by induction on t. The scope limitation about M not being polynomially bounded for the full circuit set is correctly stated. No counterexample exists - this is a direct circuit construction from the definitions.

This correctly describes a fan-in-2 circuit construction for the explicit candidate-set transition. For each candidate j: (1) the hardwired circuit C_j is copied using at most s gates to compute c_j = C_j(x); (2) equality [c_j = b] is computed as (c_j AND b) OR (NOT c_j AND NOT b) using 4 gates per candidate (NOT c_j, c_j AND b, NOT c_j AND NOT b with shared NOT b, OR); (3) a'_j = a_j AND [c_j = b] uses 1 more gate. Total per candidate: s + 5 gates. Shared NOT b costs 1 gate total. The n-bit address x is incremented modulo 2^n using a ripple incrementer with O(n) gates (NOT x_0 for LSB, and for i>0: x_i XOR (AND_{k<i} x_k) implemented with constant AND/OR/NOT gates sharing prefix conjunctions). Total size: M(s+5) + 1 + O(n) = M(s+5) + O(n). The construction is exact on valid states by induction on prefix length. The stated limitation (no polynomial bound when M is the full circuit count) is correctly noted. No counterexample exists - this is a direct circuit construction from definitions.

This is essentially the same construction as S0508 with slightly different phrasing. The gate count analysis is identical: s gates per candidate to evaluate C_j(x), 4 gates per candidate for [C_j(x)=b] (with shared NOT b), 1 gate per candidate to AND with a_j. Total M(s+5)+1 filtering gates. Ripple incrementer for x uses O(n) gates. The transition is exact on all valid states by induction. The limitation (no polynomial-in-(s,n) bound when M is the full circuit count) is correctly stated. No counterexample - this is a direct circuit construction from definitions.

This lemma describes a position-specific transition circuit where the mask m_t is hardwired for a specific position t. For each candidate j: if (m_t)_j = 1, then x'_j = x_j AND b (1 AND gate); if (m_t)_j = 0, then x'_j = x_j AND NOT b (1 AND + 1 NOT, but NOT b is shared across all j). Total gates: K AND gates + 1 shared NOT b = K+1 gates. The transition is exact: x'_j = 1 iff x_j = 1 and E_j[t] = b, which correctly filters candidates consistent with the streamed prefix. The limitation is correctly stated: this is a family of circuits (one per position t), and the masks m_t across all t encode the full truth tables, so no polynomial-in-(s,n) bound when K is large. No counterexample - direct construction from definitions.

This lemma correctly bounds the number of distinct nonempty residuals q_t. Three bounds: (1) q_t <= K because each distinct nonempty residual must contain at least one string from F, and distinct residuals cannot be witnessed by the same string's prefix (since a string has exactly one prefix of length t); (2) q_t <= 2^t because there are only 2^t possible prefixes u of length t; (3) q_t <= 2^(2^(N-t)) because each residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) possible suffixes, and there are 2^(2^(N-t)) possible subsets. The minimum of these three bounds is correct. The consequence about one-hot state representation with q_t bits and O(q_t) transition gates is also correct. The limitation (q_t can be as large as K, no polynomial-in-(s,n) bound for EXT) is correctly stated. No counterexample - this is a direct combinatorial proof.

This lemma correctly describes the residual left-quotient update. For any z∈A, pb is a prefix of z iff p is a prefix of z AND the t-th bit of z equals b. This is exactly the definition of {z∈R_p: z[t]=b}. The consequences follow directly: (1) if R_p = ∅ then R_{pb} = ∅ for all b (empty residual remains empty); (2) R_p ≠ ∅ iff p is a prefix of at least one member of A (by definition of R_p). This is a basic property of prefix residuals, correctly stated and proved. No counterexample - direct set-theoretic proof.

This lemma correctly describes the explicit-list transition circuit. For each candidate i: if E_i[t] = b, then y_i = x_i (wire, 0 gates); if E_i[t] ≠ b, then y_i = 0 (constant, 0 gates). If a uniform circuit receiving b is required, compute NOT b once (1 gate), then for each i: y_i = x_i AND b (if E_i[t]=1) or y_i = x_i AND NOT b (if E_i[t]=0), using one AND gate per coordinate. Total: M+1 gates. The transition is exact: y_i = 1 iff x_i = 1 and E_i[t] = b, correctly filtering candidates agreeing with the extended prefix. The limitation (linear in M, no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound when M is the full circuit set) is correctly stated. No counterexample - direct construction.

This lemma correctly states the candidate-list update cost for the explicit incidence-vector representation. For each i: if E_i[t] = b, y_i = x_i (wire); if E_i[t] ≠ b, y_i = 0 (constant). If a uniform circuit receiving b is needed, compute NOT b once (1 gate), then one AND gate per coordinate: y_i = x_i AND b (if E_i[t]=1) or y_i = x_i AND NOT b (if E_i[t]=0). Total: M+1 gates. The transition is exact. The lemma correctly states this gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound unless M is polynomial in (n,s), and does not close the universal update obligation G0004. No counterexample - direct construction from definitions.

This lemma correctly bounds the number of circuit descriptions M. For each of j gates: 3 gate types × (n+s)^2 ordered source pairs (inputs or previous gate outputs) = 3(n+s)^2 choices per gate. Output wire: at most n+s choices. So (n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^j descriptions with exactly j gates. Summing j=0..s: Σ (n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^j ≤ (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s (since there are s+1 terms and each ≤ the j=s term). This is a valid upper bound (it overcounts because it allows unused wires and treats unary NOT as having two ordered sources). The update circuit size bound M+1 follows from the previous explicit-list transition lemma. The lemma correctly states this does not give a polynomial-in-(n,s) bound. No counterexample - combinatorial counting argument is sound.

This lemma correctly characterizes the states of the minimal deterministic streaming automaton for a prefix language L=Pref(A). Proof: (1) If prefixes p and q reach the same deterministic state, then for every continuation u, the acceptance outcome after p+u equals that after q+u. Since acceptance after p followed by u is exactly pu∈L, this implies L_p = L_q. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states (lower bound). (2) The distinct right residuals L_p themselves form a valid DFA: transition δ(L_p, b) = L_{pb} is well-defined because if L_p = L_q then {u: bu∈L_p} = {u: bu∈L_q} so L_{pb} = L_{qb}. A residual is accepting iff it contains ε (i.e., p∈L). Starting from L_ε, after reading prefix p the state is L_p. The empty residual L_p=∅ is a rejecting sink (δ(∅,b)=∅). This is exactly the Myhill-Nerode construction for prefix languages. No counterexample - standard automata theory, correctly applied.

The proof is correct as stated. For each depth k, every nonempty right residual L_p has a length-k prefix p with at least one descendant in A. There are at most 2^k such prefixes. Moreover, the descendant sets A_p={a in A:a extends p} for different length-k prefixes are pairwise disjoint and nonempty, so at most M such prefixes occur. Hence at most min(2^k,M) nonempty residuals are represented at depth k. The Myhill-Nerode right-residual characterization says that the minimal DFA has one state per distinct residual. Summing over depths can only overcount a residual occurring at several depths, and the only possible empty residual adds one state. No hypothesis is missing beyond the stated finiteness and nonemptiness of A.

proved_step: LEMMA (exact residual characterization for a finite fixed-length language). Let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and L=A, viewed as a language over {0,1}. For each prefix p of length k≤N define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-k}: pu∈A}. The minimal deterministic finite automaton for L has exactly 1+Σ_{k=0}^N |{R_p : p∈{0,1}^k, R_p≠∅}| states, where the additional state is the rejecting sink. Proof: For any prefix p, its right language {u:pu∈L} equals R_p, and is empty exactly when p is not a prefix of any word in A. Two prefixes p,p' are equivalent in the Myhill–Nerode relation precisely when their right languages agree. If their lengths differ, their nonempty right languages contain words of different fixed lengths, so they cannot agree; an empty right language is shared by all non-prefixes and is the sink. At a fixed length k, equivalence is exactly equality of the sets R_p. Every nonempty R_p is reached by reading p, and the empty right language is reached by any non-prefix (or, if none exists, the transition from a length-N accepting state on either further bit). Thus the stated count is exact. Consequently, the upper bound in S0520 can be sharpened by replacing min(2^k,|A|) with the exact number of distinct nonempty suffix sets at level k; any two prefixes at that level with different residual sets require distinct automaton states. This is an exact characterization for explicit finite A only and gives no lower bound on the gate cost of an implicit EXT transition or on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (residual derivative gives the exact EXT transition). Let N≥1 and A⊆{0,1}^N. At level k<N, for p∈{0,1}^k define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-k}:pu∈A}. For b∈{0,1}, define D_b(R_p)={u∈{0,1}^{N-k-1}:bu∈R_p}. Then R_{pb}=D_b(R_p). Hence the deterministic prefix automaton transition from residual state R_p on b goes to D_b(R_p) if nonempty, otherwise the rejecting sink. At level N both outgoing transitions go to the sink. Proof: for each u of length N−k−1, u∈R_{pb} iff (pb)u∈A iff p(bu)∈A iff bu∈R_p iff u∈D_b(R_p). Thus equality holds pointwise. In particular, equal residual sets at the same level have equal b-successors. This characterizes the exact information and abstract update for an explicit finite language, but gives neither a compact encoding nor a low-cost update circuit for implicit EXT_{n,s}, and implies nothing about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (exact residual states of a finite word family). Let N be a nonnegative integer and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Let Pref(A) be the set of all prefixes of words in A, including the empty word, and let L=Pref(A). For each k in {0,...,N} and each length-k prefix p occurring in a member of A, define S(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-k}: pu in A}. Then the minimal DFA recognizing L has exactly 1 + sum_{k=0}^N |{S(p): p is a length-k prefix of a member of A}| states. Proof: For any such p, its left quotient p^{-1}L consists exactly of Pref(S(p)): pw is a prefix of some a in A iff w is a prefix of the unique length-(N-k) suffix u with pu=a. At a fixed k, the words of maximum length N-k in Pref(S(p)) are exactly S(p), so different S(p) yield different quotients. For nonempty S(p), Pref(S(p)) has maximum word length N-k; hence quotients from different depths k are distinct. Every prefix in L has one of these quotients, while any non-prefix has empty quotient and all such prefixes share the rejecting sink. By Myhill-Nerode, the stated count is exact. This is a theorem about explicitly specified finite word families; it makes no assertion about compact transition circuits for implicitly represented families.
derivation: The quotient identity follows from the definition of prefix closure. Recovering the suffix set from maximum-length words proves injectivity within a level; maximum accepted continuation length distinguishes levels. The only quotient outside those represented by prefixes is the empty quotient, giving one sink.
scope: All finite nonempty A subset {0,1}^N; exact DFA state count for Pref(A), no circuit complexity or PNP transfer claim.

statement: LEMMA (residual languages are necessary streaming state information). Let L be any language of finite binary strings, and let a deterministic one-pass streaming machine decide, after each prefix p, whether p is a prefix of some word in L. Define R_p={z : pz is in L}. If two prefixes p,q lead the machine to the same internal state, then R_p=R_q. Consequently the machine has at least as many reachable states as there are distinct residual languages R_p. Proof: for every suffix z, deterministic processing from the same state on z has the same final outcome. The machine accepts pz exactly when z∈R_p, and accepts qz exactly when z∈R_q. Equality of states therefore implies, for every z, z∈R_p iff z∈R_q, hence R_p=R_q. Contrapositively, distinct residuals require distinct states. This is a necessary-information bound; it makes no gate-cost claim and does not imply that an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit exposes or updates the residuals efficiently.
derivation: The state-equality implication follows by applying the same continuation z to equal deterministic states and using exact correctness on both completed streams.

evidence: The claimed counter j ranges over {0,...,N}, which has N+1=2^n+1 values and requires n+1 bits. The stated M+ceil(log2 N)=M+n bits do not provide the claimed index representation. Repair: allocate ceil(log2(N+1))=n+1 index bits; the candidate-mask invariant and update argument then apply.

refuted_approach: S0633's residual set R_p={z:pz∈L} is not justified by a machine that only reports whether each current prefix is extendible to a word in L. Such a machine reports membership in Pref(L), not membership in L for arbitrary completions. The correct residual is R_p^P={z:pz∈Pref(L)}.
proved_step:
statement: LEMMA (residual information for prefix extendibility). Let L⊆{0,1}* and P=Pref(L)={p: there exists w with pw∈L}. Suppose a deterministic streaming machine, after reading each string p, outputs 1 exactly when p∈P. For each p define R_p^P={z∈{0,1}*: pz∈P}. If p and q lead to the same machine state, then R_p^P=R_q^P. Proof: fix any z. Starting from the equal states after p and q, deterministic processing of the same continuation z ends in the same state and hence gives the same output. By correctness, that output is 1 exactly when pz∈P, and also exactly when qz∈P. Thus pz∈P iff qz∈P for every z, so the residual sets are equal. Consequently distinct residuals of Pref(L) require distinct reachable states. This is an information requirement only; it gives no gate-cost bound for transitions.
derivation: Corrected the observable language from L to its prefix closure Pref(L), because EXT outputs whether a prefix has some completion rather than whether a specified continuation completes it.

statement: LEMMA (candidate-set to EXT-residual map). Fix a finite indexed family F of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, and stream each function's truth table in the same fixed input order. For a prefix p of length k, let L_p be the functions agreeing with p on the first k inputs, and let R_p be the set of their remaining truth-table suffixes. Then R_p is exactly the EXT continuation residual after p. For the next truth-table position i_k and bit b, L_{pb}={f in L_p:f(i_k)=b}, and R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}. Thus candidate sets are exact sufficient states, while the minimal residual states identify candidate sets precisely when they induce the same suffix set. Proof: A suffix z completes p to a prefix of a family truth table exactly when some function in L_p has remaining suffix z, which is the definition of R_p. A function remains live after reading b exactly when it was live before and its value at i_k equals b. A suffix z completes pb exactly when bz completes p, giving the residual identity. Therefore continuation behavior depends only on R_p; distinct candidate sets need not be distinct states if their suffix sets agree.

statement: LEMMA (reachable candidate sets are exactly EXT residuals for duplicate-free functions). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with truth tables read in a fixed order. For every prefix p of length k, let L_p={f∈F: f agrees with p on the first k inputs}, and let R_p={z∈{0,1}^{2^n-k}: pz is a prefix of the truth table of some f∈F}. Then the map f↦the remaining truth-table suffix of f is a bijection from L_p to R_p. In particular |L_p|=|R_p|, and two reachable prefixes p,q have the same live-function set if and only if their residual suffix sets (viewed at their respective stream positions) agree after identifying the remaining coordinates. Proof: If f∈L_p, its remaining suffix z satisfies that pz is the full truth table of f, so z∈R_p. Conversely, if z∈R_p, by definition some f∈F has truth table beginning pz, and so f∈L_p maps to z. For injectivity, if f,g∈L_p map to the same z, then both truth tables consist of the same length-k prefix p followed by z; hence their truth tables agree at all 2^n inputs, so f=g, using extensional equality of Boolean functions. This gives a canonical identification of reachable candidate sets with residual sets; it does not bound the gate cost of computing the update for the implicit family of all size-s circuits.

statement: CORRECTED LEMMA (candidate/residual bijection at a fixed stream position). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with truth tables read in a fixed order. Fix a prefix p of length k. Define L_p={f∈F: f agrees with p on the first k inputs} and R_p={z∈{0,1}^{2^n-k}: pz is a prefix of the truth table of some f∈F}. The map f↦the remaining truth-table suffix of f is a bijection L_p→R_p; hence |L_p|=|R_p|. Proof: Every f∈L_p has a remaining suffix z and pz is its full truth table, so z∈R_p. Conversely, every z∈R_p has a witness f∈F whose truth table begins pz, so f∈L_p and maps to z. If f,g∈L_p map to the same z, both truth tables equal pz, hence f=g as Boolean functions. This is only a fixed-position cardinality and state-correspondence statement; it makes no assertion equating residual sets from different stream positions and gives no update-circuit bound for an implicit circuit family.

statement: LEMMA (exact fixed-position residual count). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on a finite domain of size N, with truth-table entries streamed in a fixed order. Fix k with 0≤k≤N. For each length-k binary prefix p, let L_p be the functions in F matching p on their first k entries, and let R_p be the set of length-(N−k) suffixes of functions in L_p. Then the number of distinct residuals R_p among length-k prefixes equals the number of distinct live-function sets L_p among those prefixes. Proof: Define φ_k(f) to be the suffix of f after its first k entries. On F, φ_k is injective: if φ_k(f)=φ_k(g) and both match the same prefix p, then f and g agree on the first k entries (both equal p) and on the remaining entries (their suffixes agree), hence f=g. For every p, R_p=φ_k(L_p). Thus if L_p=L_q, then R_p=R_q. Conversely, if R_p=R_q, injectivity of φ_k implies L_p=L_q: for any f∈L_p, its suffix belongs to R_q, so some g∈L_q has that suffix; both f and g have the same first k entries q and the same suffix, hence f=g, so f∈L_q; reverse inclusion follows symmetrically. Therefore the two collections of sets have the same number of distinct members. This is an exact state-count identity at one fixed stream position; it gives no transition-circuit bound for an implicit circuit family.

statement: LEMMA (fixed-prefix candidate/residual bijection, corrected scope). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on a finite domain of size N, with entries streamed in one fixed order. Fix one prefix p of length k. Let L_p={f∈F: f's first k entries equal p}, and let R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−k}: pz is the length-N table of some f∈F}. The suffix map f↦f[k..N−1] is a bijection L_p→R_p, so |L_p|=|R_p|. Proof: If f∈L_p, its suffix z completes p to f's full table, hence z∈R_p. Conversely, for z∈R_p, by definition some f∈F has table pz, so f∈L_p and maps to z. If f,g∈L_p have the same suffix, their first k entries both equal p and their remaining entries agree, so their full tables agree; since F consists of functions, f=g. This assertion fixes p throughout; it makes no claim that equal residual sets for different prefixes imply equal live-function sets.

evidence: The update wraps the n-bit index modulo 2^n and has no state distinguishing completion of the length-2^n truth table. For example, with F containing the constant-zero circuit, the all-zero truth table leaves that candidate live; one additional zero bit also leaves it live, although a string longer than 2^n is not a prefix of any truth table in F.

The modulo-2^n index wraps after the final truth-table bit, and the stated state has no done flag or other length information. With a listed constant-zero circuit and an all-zero truth table, a further zero bit preserves the candidate mask, falsely accepting a string longer than the truth-table length.

proved_step: LEMMA (done-bit repair for an explicitly listed finite truth-table family). Let C_1,...,C_M be explicitly listed Boolean circuits on n input bits with fan-in-two gate counts s_1,...,s_M, M>=1, and let N=2^n. A deterministic streaming recognizer for Pref({TT(C_j):1<=j<=M}) has state (i,a_1,...,a_M,d), where i is an n-bit address, a_j records agreement with candidate j, and d is a done bit. It uses O(n+M+sum_j s_j) fan-in-two gates per input-bit update. Initially i=0, every a_j=1, d=0. While d=0, on bit b set a_j to a_j AND [C_j(i)=b]. If i=N-1, set d=1 and hold i; otherwise increment i. When d=1, any further input clears every a_j and leaves d=1. Accept iff some a_j=1. Proof: Before each of the first N updates, induction gives that i is the next truth-table address and a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the prefix already read. The update checks the next bit and preserves this invariant; at the final address it sets d, and otherwise advances i. Hence a prefix of length at most N is accepted exactly when some listed truth table extends it. Once d=1, any extra bit clears the mask permanently, so all longer strings reject. Evaluating the listed circuits costs sum_j s_j gates; comparisons and mask updates cost O(M), and address increment plus terminal detection cost O(n). This applies only to an explicitly listed family and gives no compact transition bound for minimized EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

evidence: The address is modulo 2^n. After N=2^n input bits it wraps to zero, while the agreement mask can stay live; a stream longer than N may therefore be accepted. This violates recognition of the finite prefix language. The done-bit repair is recorded separately as S0643.

proved_step: LEMMA (explicit-list state-bit bound for prefix extension). Let C_1,...,C_M be explicitly listed Boolean circuits on n input bits, each of fan-in-two size s_j, and let N=2^n. The prefix language of their truth tables is recognized by a deterministic streaming machine using n+M+1 state bits and an update circuit of O(n+M+sum_j s_j) fan-in-two gates. Proof: Store an n-bit address i, M agreement bits a_j, and a done bit d. Initially i=0, all a_j=1, and d=0. While d=0, for input b replace a_j by a_j AND [C_j(i)=b]. If i=N-1 set d=1 and hold i; otherwise increment i. When d=1, clear all agreement bits on any further input and keep d=1. Inductively, before each of the first N updates, i is the next truth-table address and a_j is 1 exactly when C_j agrees with the prefix already read. Thus a prefix of length at most N is accepted iff some listed table extends it, and every longer string rejects. The address, terminal test, and increment use O(n) gates; evaluating the listed circuits costs sum_j s_j; comparisons, agreement updates, and clearing cost O(M). This is an explicit-list encoding result only; it gives no transition-cost bound for the minimized EXT automaton or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

LEMMA (exact suffix-expansion circuit for EXT transitions). Let N>=1, let C be a Boolean circuit of size L on N inputs, and let 0<=t<N and b in {0,1}. Define T_{t,b}(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} such that C(p||b||z)=1, for p in {0,1}^t. Then T_{t,b} has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^{N-t-1}(L+1)-1, assuming input fixing and wiring are free. Proof: For each suffix z, make one copy of C, wire p||b to its first t+1 inputs, and fix the remaining inputs to z. OR the 2^{N-t-1} outputs with a binary tree, requiring 2^{N-t-1}-1 gates. The result is 1 exactly when some completion is accepted by C. When C recognizes the size-at-most-s truth tables, this computes the EXT next-bit predicate. This is an exact, generally exponential upper bound; it provides neither a compact encoding of all residual states nor a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP circuits. Barrier diagnostic: the construction relativizes (copies and OR only); it is not a natural-proofs lower-bound argument; Boolean wiring raises no algebrization issue; locality is not asserted. It passes none of the circumvention tests as a compression: it retains suffix enumeration and supplies no re-coding bound, adaptive rule, new resource, or transfer to arbitrary MCSP circuits.

gap: This finite upper bound still does not connect an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit to an efficient EXT transition circuit: the bound may be exponential in the remaining truth-table length. The next open step is to derive either a subexponential transition implementation from additional structure in C or a lower bound against all such implementations.
evidence: Direct construction and exact gate count; every suffix assignment appears once in exactly one of the two branch OR trees. No computation or experiment was used; this is a general finite construction.
proved_step: LEMMA (two-output suffix-expansion bound). Let C:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size L, and let p be a fixed prefix of length t<N. For b in {0,1}, define T_b(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with C(p||b||z)=1. The pair (T_0(p),T_1(p)) is computable by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^{N-t}(L+1)-2 gates, using independent copies of C and fixed-input wiring. Proof: Let k=2^{N-t-1}. For each b and each suffix z, use a copy of C with p||b wired to its fixed inputs; this uses at most 2kL gates total. For each b, OR its k outputs with a binary tree using k-1 gates; total OR cost is 2(k-1). Thus the total is 2k(L+1)-2=2^{N-t}(L+1)-2. Each output equals the existential disjunction over precisely the suffixes in its branch, so it computes T_b(p).

statement: LEMMA (block transition composition for an explicitly represented candidate family). Let D={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on a finite domain X, and let a_0,...,a_{N-1} be a fixed ordering of X. Suppose u∈{0,1}^M marks the candidates consistent with the truth-table prefix before position t. For a block w=(w_0,...,w_{d-1}), define F_{t,w}(j)=1 iff C_j(a_{t+r})=w_r for every 0≤r<d. The updated mask is u'=u∧F_{t,w}, coordinatewise. For consecutive blocks w,v, F_{t,wv}=F_{t,w}∧F_{t+d,v}; thus block updates compose associatively. If each C_j is given by a fan-in-two circuit of at most s gates, a direct implementation uses O(Md(s+1)) gates, plus input-address handling.
derivation: Candidate j survives the extended prefix exactly when it survived the old prefix and agrees at every new block position. This is the stated coordinatewise conjunction. Splitting the conjunction for wv at the boundary between w and v proves the composition identity; associativity of conjunction makes the result independent of parenthesization. For the gate bound, evaluate each C_j at each of the d fixed points, compare with the corresponding fixed bit, AND the d comparisons, then AND with u_j. This uses O(d(s+1)) gates per candidate, hence O(Md(s+1)) total, plus address handling. This result is limited to explicitly represented families; it gives no compact update for the full size-s circuit family, no transition bound through H_C, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP deciders.

statement: LEMMA (prefix projection of a deterministic circuit’s trace relation). Let C:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be a Boolean circuit with gates ordered topologically as g_1,...,g_m, and let T_i(x,y_{<i}) be the Boolean function computed at gate i from input x and earlier gate values. Define H_C(x,y)=T_out(x,y) AND ∧_{i=1}^m (y_i ↔ T_i(x,y_{<i})), where T_out is the circuit’s output wire interpreted using x and y. For every fixed x there is exactly one y with all trace equations true, namely the vector of gate values obtained by evaluating C on x. Consequently, for every prefix p of length t≤N, EXT_C(p):=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^{N−t} satisfies C(pz)=1 is equivalent to ∃z∈{0,1}^{N−t}∃y∈{0,1}^m H_C(pz,y)=1. Proof: Induct on i. Once x and y_1,...,y_{i−1} are fixed, the i-th equation forces y_i to the unique value T_i(x,y_{<i}); hence the equations have exactly one solution y, and that solution is the actual gate-evaluation trace. On this unique trace, T_out equals C(x), so H_C(x,y)=1 exactly when C(x)=1. Existentially quantifying the suffix z therefore yields the stated prefix equivalence.

evidence: For fixed v_t,j∈{0,1}, equality [v_t,j=b] is b if v_t,j=1 and NOT b otherwise. One shared NOT b plus M AND gates suffices. By induction, each bit of the mask records agreement on the entire observed prefix. The full table uses MN stored bits; direct generation evaluates each candidate on each input.
proved_step: statement: LEMMA (precomputed candidate-mask update). Let D={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with fixed input order a_0,...,a_{N-1}, N=2^n. Define u_j=1 iff C_j agrees with the observed prefix p_0,...,p_{t-1}. If v_t=(C_1(a_t),...,C_M(a_t)) is available as fixed circuit constants, then after observing b the exact updated mask is u'_j=u_j AND [v_{t,j}=b] for j=1,...,M. It takes at most M+1 fan-in-two gates (one shared NOT of b, then one AND per candidate). Direct preprocessing of all N columns by evaluating M circuits of at most s gates costs O(MN(s+n)) Boolean operations and stores MN bits. Proof: Since v_{t,j} is a fixed bit, [v_{t,j}=b] is b when v_{t,j}=1 and NOT b otherwise. Thus each updated bit is computed with one AND after the shared complement is formed. It is 1 exactly when candidate j matched all earlier bits and matches the new bit. Induction on t proves the mask is exactly the consistent candidate set. The result separates preprocessing/storage from per-symbol transition cost and is restricted to an explicit finite family.

statement: LEMMA (exact suffix-projection transition for a decision circuit). Let N≥1 and let H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size h. For every prefix p∈{0,1}^t with 0≤t<N, define E_H(p)=1 iff there exists z∈{0,1}^{N-t} such that H(pz)=1. Then for b∈{0,1}, E_H(pb)= OR_{z∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}} H(pb z). This transition predicate has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^{N-t-1}h + (2^{N-t-1}-1), up to O(N) input wiring per copy if input wiring is charged as gates. Proof: By definition, E_H(pb)=1 iff there exists a suffix w of length N-t-1 with H(pbw)=1, which is exactly the displayed disjunction. Construct one copy of H for each such w, hardwire the first t+1 inputs to pb and the remaining inputs to w, and combine their outputs by a binary OR tree. There are 2^{N-t-1} terms; a binary OR tree uses at most 2^{N-t-1}-1 gates. This proves correctness and the stated gate bound. The bound is exponential in the remaining suffix length and therefore does not establish a polynomial-in-s transition cost for EXT or a bridge to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: The existential completion condition splits by the next bit: completions of pb are precisely strings pbw for w∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}. Enumerating all w and ORing H on the resulting full inputs is an exact circuit construction.

statement: LEMMA (polynomial real-gate suffix projection for affine predicates). Let A be an r×N matrix over GF(2), c∈GF(2)^r, and H(x)=1 iff Ax=c. Fix a cut t<N and write A=(A_<t | D), where D consists of columns t,...,N−1. Let U be an r×k matrix whose columns form a basis of ker(D^T). For p∈{0,1}^t, define E_H(p)=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^{N−t} satisfies H(pz). Then E_H(p)=1 iff U^T(c+A_<t p)=0. In particular, the next-bit transition E_H(pb) is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(kr) gates (with A,c,U hardwired), hence O(r²) gates, and the formula is exact. Proof: H(pz) holds exactly when Dz=c+A_<t p, since subtraction equals addition over GF(2). A vector y lies in im(D) iff it is orthogonal to ker(D^T): inclusion follows from λ^T Dz=(D^Tλ)^Tz=0; equality follows from rank-nullity, since im(D) has dimension rank(D), while ker(D^T)^⊥ also has dimension r−dim ker(D^T)=rank(D). Thus a completion exists iff U^T(c+A_<t p)=0. For pb, substitute p concatenated with b in this identity. Each of the k output parities is a dot product of a fixed row of U^T A_<t and p plus a fixed constant and a fixed coefficient times b. A parity of at most r+1 bits uses O(r) fan-in-two XOR gates, each XOR implementable with three AND/OR/NOT gates; combine the k parity outputs by an AND tree using at most k−1 gates. This is O(kr) gates and k≤r, giving O(r²). All preprocessing (finding U) is outside the per-transition circuit and is computable by Gaussian elimination in polynomial time. This proves a real-gate transition bound for affine predicates only; it does not establish such a bound for EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Use the exact linear-algebra criterion y∈im(D) iff y is orthogonal to ker(D^T), with y=c+A_<t p. Substitution of the next bit yields k affine parity tests, each implemented by a linear-size fan-in-two circuit.

LEMMA (column-factored candidate-mask transition). Let D=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on a finite domain X, let a_0,...,a_{N-1} be a fixed input order, and define the M-bit consistency state u_j(p)=1 iff C_j(a_i)=p_i for all i<t, for a prefix p of length t. Define the column v_t∈{0,1}^M by (v_t)_j=C_j(a_t). For next bit b, the unique correct updated mask is u'_j=u_j AND NOT((v_t)_j XOR b). Given v_t, all M output bits are computed with O(M) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates; the column itself can be computed by evaluating all listed circuits in O(M(s+n)) gates when each C_j has at most s fan-in-two gates and inputs are explicitly supplied. Thus transition cost separates into an O(M) mask-update circuit and an O(M(s+n)) column-generation circuit; correctness holds for every prefix by induction. Proof: For each j, consistency with the extended prefix is equivalent to consistency with p and agreement C_j(a_t)=b. This is exactly u_j AND NOT((v_t)_j XOR b). The Boolean expression costs a constant number of gates per coordinate, and evaluating each listed circuit at a_t costs at most s gates plus input handling; summing gives the stated bounds. This lemma is limited to the explicit family representation and yields no transition bound for succinct EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
