evidence: Verified the state count bound: at depth k, ≤ min(2^k, M) distinct prefixes from M words of length N; summing k=0..N and adding 1 for sink gives q ≤ 1 + Σ min(2^k, M). Verified the one-hot transition circuit construction: ¬b (1 gate), 2q AND gates for (x_i ∧ b) and (x_i ∧ ¬b), binary OR trees merging ≤ 2q signals into q destinations using ≤ 2q OR gates. Total ≤ 4q+1 fan-in-2 gates (NOT is fan-in-1, conventionally counted). The construction correctly implements the deterministic prefix-automaton transition for any A ⊆ {0,1}^N. No counterexample found; proof is sound.

This is a direct application of the Myhill-Nerode theorem to the prefix language Pref(L) = {p : ∃w∈L, p is prefix of w}. The residual R_p = {z : pz ∈ Pref(L)} exactly matches the Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes. (⇒) If R_p ≠ R_q, ∃z in symmetric difference; pz ∈ Pref(L) ⇔ qz ∉ Pref(L). A deterministic machine in same state after p,q would give identical answers on z, contradiction. (⇐) The residual automaton with states = distinct R_p (plus sink for empty residual) has well-defined transitions: from R_p on bit b go to R_{pb} = {z : bz ∈ R_p}, which depends only on R_p and b. Acceptance: empty suffix ε ∈ R_p iff p ∈ Pref(L). This construction recognizes exactly Pref(L) and is minimal. No counterexample exists; the proof is sound and complete for finite L.

This is a standard Myhill-Nerode argument restricted to equal-length prefixes. If R_p ≠ R_q, ∃z of length N-t in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pz, qz ∈ L. A deterministic automaton in the same state after reading p and q would produce identical outputs on continuation z, contradicting that exactly one word is accepted. The proof is sound; no counterexample exists for finite equal-length word families. The lemma correctly gives an information-state lower bound (number of states at depth t ≥ number of distinct residual sets R_p) without claiming anything about transition gate cost or connection to H_C.

The construction is sound: for each candidate circuit C_j (size ≤ s), evaluate it on the n-bit input a_t using its s gates (the input bits are wired directly). Compare the output to b with a constant-size circuit (e.g., (out ∧ b) ∨ (¬out ∧ ¬b), 3 gates). AND this equality bit with the prior mask bit u_j (1 gate). Total per candidate: s + O(1) gates. For M candidates: O(Ms) gates. Since s ≤ s+n, O(M(s+n)) is a valid upper bound. The induction on prefix length t proves the mask invariant exactly. The lemma correctly scopes its claim: it applies to an explicitly listed family with descriptions available to the transition circuit, and does not claim a representation through an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C. No counterexample exists.

The proof is correct: w ∈ R(pb) ⇔ pbw ∈ F ⇔ bw ∈ R(p) by definition of residuals. If R(p)=R(q), then {w: bw ∈ R(p)} = {w: bw ∈ R(q)}, so R(pb)=R(qb) and pb≡qb. This is a standard Myhill-Nerode style residual equivalence argument for finite equal-length string families. No counterexample exists; the scope is properly limited to transition well-definedness, not state count or circuit cost.

The proof is correct: every nonempty residual class contains at least one prefix that occurs as the length-t prefix of some word in F. There are at most 2^t such distinct prefixes and at most K such words, giving at most min(2^t,K) nonempty classes. All prefixes with empty residual (those not extendable to any word in F) share the same empty residual set and form at most one additional class. Total ≤ min(2^t,K)+1. No counterexample exists; scope is properly limited to width bound in terms of |F|, not transition circuit cost from compact representation.

The proof is correct: evaluating a fixed fan-in-two circuit of size ≤ s on an n-bit input requires exactly s gates (one per gate in the description). The comparison [C(i)=b] is (C(i) ∧ b) ∨ (¬C(i) ∧ ¬b), 3 gates. AND with the prior live bit a_C is 1 gate. Total per candidate: s + 4 = O(s+1) gates. For D candidates: O(D(s+1)). An n-bit ripple-carry increment uses n full-adders (each 2 XOR + 2 AND + 1 OR = 5 gates) = O(n) gates. Induction on prefix length proves the invariant a_C = 1 ⇔ candidate C agrees with all bits seen. Scope is properly limited to explicitly enumerated candidates with separate live bits; no claim about compact MCSP decision circuits H_C.

The proof is correct: evaluating each hardwired C_j on the n-bit index i costs at most s gates (one per gate in its description). The comparison e_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] uses (C_j(i) ∧ b) ∨ (¬C_j(i) ∧ ¬b) for equality (3 gates) then AND with a_j (1 gate) = O(1) additional gates per candidate. Total for K candidates: O(K(s+1)). The n-bit ripple-carry increment costs O(n) gates. The invariant a_j = 1 ⇔ C_j agrees with all streamed bits holds by induction. Scope properly limited to explicitly listed candidates with separate live bits; no claim about polynomial update from compact MCSP circuits H_C.

The claimed bound D = 1 + (n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s is incorrect. Counterexample: n=1, s=1. Actual descriptions: j=0 gives n+2=3 descriptions (output from {x1,0,1}). j=1 gives (n+1+2) * 3 * (n+1+2)^2 = 4 * 3 * 16 = 192 descriptions. Total = 195. Claimed bound: 1 + 4 * 3 * 16 = 193. 195 > 193, so the bound is violated. The sum over j=0..s has s+1 positive terms; bounding it by 1 + max_term fails for s≥1. The corrected bound in S0534 uses (s+1) * max_term which is valid.

The counting is correct: for each j=0..s, at gate i there are ≤ n+i+1 available wires (n inputs, 2 constants, i-1 previous gates); using (n+i+2)^2 as an upper bound for ordered predecessor pairs and 3 gate types gives ≤ 3(n+s+2)^2 choices per gate. The output wire has ≤ n+j+2 choices. So j-gate descriptions ≤ (n+j+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^j. Summing j=0..s gives ≤ (s+1)(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s = D. Evaluating each live description on the current input takes O(s) word operations (scanning its ≤ s gates), so O(Ds) per streamed bit; the n-bit counter increment adds O(n). Storage: O(Ds log(n+s+2)) bits for descriptions + D live flags + n counter bits = O(Ds log(n+s+2)+n). The bound is exponential in s log(n+s), correctly scoped as an upper bound for this explicit representation only, with no lower-bound implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C. No counterexample exists.

The counting and complexity analysis is sound. For j-gate circuits, at gate i there are ≤ n+i+1 available wires, so ≤ 3(n+s+2)^2 choices per gate type+predecessors. Output wire has ≤ n+j+2 choices. Total j-gate descriptions ≤ (n+j+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^j. Sum j=0..s ≤ (s+1)(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s = D. Word-RAM storage: O(Ds log(n+s+2)) bits for descriptions (each needs O(s log(n+s)) bits for gate list), D live flags, n counter bits = O(Ds log(n+s)+n). Per streamed bit: O(Ds) word ops for evaluating live circuits (s gates each) + O(n) for counter increment = O(Ds+n). The exponential bound is correctly scoped for this explicit enumeration representation only; no lower bound for arbitrary MCSP circuits H_C is claimed. No counterexample exists.

The construction is correct: A_p = {j : f_j extends p} is exactly the set of indices whose strings have prefix p. B_{i,b}[j] = 1 iff f_j[i] = b (the i-th bit of string f_j equals b). For a prefix p of length i, a_p is the indicator of A_p. Then a_{pb}[j] = 1 iff j ∈ A_p AND f_j[i] = b, which is exactly a_p[j] ∧ B_{i,b}[j]. So a_{pb} = a_p AND B_{i,b} coordinatewise. The prefix p is accepted (extends to some f_j) iff A_p is nonempty iff a_p is nonzero. This is a standard bitmask streaming representation; the scope correctly notes it may require exponential storage (2NM bits for masks) and gives no lower bound for other representations or real-gate circuits. No counterexample exists.

The proof is correct by a standard Myhill-Nerode argument. If two prefixes p,q of length t have different residual sets R(p) ≠ R(q), then there exists a suffix u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} such that u ∈ R(p) XOR u ∈ R(q). Then exactly one of pu, qu belongs to F. A deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm must give different answers on pu and qu after reading the full input, so its state after reading p and q must be different. Thus the number of distinct states after t bits is at least the number of distinct residual sets |R_t|. This requires at least ceil(log_2 |R_t|) bits. This is a lower bound on state complexity for exact decision of L_F; it does not bound the real-gate circuit cost of the transition function from a compact representation of F. No counterexample exists.

For each j, evaluating the hardwired circuit C_j on the common address i uses at most s fan-in-two gates, one per gate in the description. Equality [C_j(i)=b] is (C_j(i) ∧ b) ∨ (¬C_j(i) ∧ ¬b), which is a constant-size fan-in-two circuit (3 gates) plus one AND with the prior flag a_j. Hence per candidate cost is s+O(1)=O(s+1) gates. For M candidates the total is O(M(s+1)). Induction on prefix length shows a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with all bits seen so far, because the update retains the flag exactly when the next truth-table bit matches. The statement is correctly scoped to an explicit list with separate live bits; it makes no claim about compact encodings or polynomial cost in n,s when M is the number of size-s circuits. No counterexample exists.

The construction is correct: v_{i,j} = C_j(i) is the i-th bit of candidate C_j's truth table. Maintaining a_j = 1 iff C_j agrees with all prefix bits read so far. Update a'_j = a_j ∧ [v_{i,j} = b] = a_j ∧ ((v_{i,j} ∧ b) ∨ (¬v_{i,j} ∧ ¬b)). This is exactly one AND gate per candidate (the equality check v_{i,j}=b is a constant 0 or 1 for fixed i,j, so the update is either a_j or 0). The position-dependent circuit uses at most M AND gates plus shared NOT. Induction proves the invariant: initially a_j=1 for all j (empty prefix). After i bits, a_j=1 iff C_j[1..i] = prefix[1..i]. The precomputed table uses MN = M·2^n bits. Scope is correctly limited: this requires exponential precomputation/storage and position-dependent circuits, giving no uniform compact transition or polynomial bound in n,s. No counterexample exists.

The construction is the standard Tseitin/gate-tableau encoding. For a circuit C with gates in topological order, introducing variables y_i for each gate's value and asserting y_i = T_i(x, y_<i) forces a unique y for each x (the actual gate evaluation). H_C(x,y) = T_out(x,y) ∧ ⋀_i (y_i ↔ T_i(x,y_<i)) evaluates to C(x) under this forced y. No counterexample exists; this is a correct exact reduction from circuit evaluation to existential SAT. Checked by reasoning on the definition: the equivalences uniquely determine y inductively, and the output coordinate equals C(x).

This is the Myhill-Nerode theorem for the fixed-length streaming setting. The proof is standard and correct: (1) Sufficiency: storing R_p works because (pb)z ∈ L iff p(bz) ∈ L iff bz ∈ R_p, so the update R_{pb} = {z : bz ∈ R_p} is correct. At length N, R_p is either {ε} or ∅, so membership is decided by whether ε ∈ R_p. (2) Necessity: if R_p ≠ R_q for same-length prefixes, there exists z in their symmetric difference, so exactly one of pz, qz ∈ L. A deterministic algorithm in the same state after p and q would give identical outputs on continuation z, contradicting correctness. Therefore distinct residuals require distinct states. The minimum number of states at level t is exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level. No counterexample exists; this is a classical characterization.

The construction is correct but trivial: for each of the 2^(N-t-1) suffixes q, create a copy of H with inputs fixed to pb·q, then OR all outputs with a binary tree of 2^(N-t-1)-1 OR gates. Each copy has at most h gates (the original circuit with some inputs fixed to constants). Total size: 2^(N-t-1)·h + (2^(N-t-1)-1) = 2^(N-t-1)(h+1)-1. This correctly computes EXT_L(pb) = ∨_q H(pb·q). The bound is exponential in N-t-1, confirming the claim that this gives no polynomial transition-cost bound from an arbitrary decision circuit H_C. No counterexample; the construction is valid but exponentially large.

proved_step: statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and fix t. Write R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. For any deterministic exact one-pass left-to-right streaming machine deciding membership in F, distinct residuals R_t(p) correspond to distinct machine states after t bits. Hence if there are d distinct residuals at level t, at least d states and ceil(log2 d) bits of state are necessary. Proof: if R_t(p) and R_t(p') differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pz,p'z belongs to F. If p and p' led to the same machine state, determinism on the identical remaining suffix z would force the same output, contradicting exact membership. Scope: state information only; no gate-transition-cost or arbitrary-MCSP-circuit simulation claim.

gap: For EXT, the exact residual set determines the child residuals by sectioning, but the recorded gap remains: whether these transitions can be represented through one fixed H_C with bounded operations and a useful real-gate cost, especially for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proved_step:
statement: RESIDUAL SECTION IDENTITY. For every finite F ⊆ {0,1}^N, every 0 ≤ t < N, prefix p ∈ {0,1}^t, and bit b ∈ {0,1}, R_{t+1}(pb) = {u : bu ∈ R_t(p)}, where R_t(p) = {z : pz ∈ F}. Moreover R_t(p) is the disjoint union over b of {bu : u ∈ R_{t+1}(pb)}.
proof: For any suffix u of length N−t−1, u ∈ R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu ∈ F, which by definition holds iff bu ∈ R_t(p). Every suffix z of length N−t has a unique decomposition z=bu, so the two first-bit sections are disjoint and their union is R_t(p).
scope: All finite F ⊆ {0,1}^N, N ≥ 1, 0 ≤ t < N. The statement concerns exact residual information only; it gives no gate-cost bound for computing transitions from an encoded residual or from H_C.

evidence: Direct coordinatewise construction and proof above; an independent exhaustive check is requested separately. No transition-cost conclusion for implicit or arbitrary MCSP representations is asserted.
proved_step: statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE MASK UPDATE LEMMA. Let N,M≥0 and let A=(a_1,…,a_M) be any explicitly given list of words in {0,1}^N, with repetitions allowed. After reading prefix p of length t, define q_j(p)=1 iff the length-t prefix of a_j equals p. On reading bit b at position t+1, update q'_j=q_j AND [a_j(t+1)=b]. Then q'=q(p b). The update is computable using at most M two-input AND gates when the constants [a_j(t+1)=b] are available; the accepting predicate “some candidate extends the prefix” is OR_j q_j and costs at most max(M−1,0) two-input OR gates. Proof: For each j, a_j has prefix p b exactly when it has prefix p and its next bit is b, which is precisely the displayed conjunction. Applying this coordinatewise proves equality of the vectors. The OR is 1 exactly when at least one listed candidate has the queried prefix. This is an exact construction for explicit candidate lists; it gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound when M is not polynomially bounded and gives no simulation from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

statement: BATCHED EXPLICIT-FAMILY TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F be an explicitly listed set of M distinct words in {0,1}^N, represented by their M×N bit table. Given a current prefix p of length t and its candidate index set L(p)={i: f_i has prefix p}, the next-bit candidate sets L_b(p)={i in L(p): f_i[t+1]=b}, b∈{0,1}, are computed by one scan of the table column t+1 restricted to L(p), using at most M Boolean tests and O(M) workspace. For a block u of r bits, the candidate set is obtained in at most Mr Boolean tests. These candidate sets are exact sufficient statistics: for every suffix z of length N-t-1, p b z belongs to the prefix language of F iff some i∈L_b(p) has suffix z after position t+1. Proof: membership in L_b is precisely agreement with p followed by b; each listed word has a unique remaining suffix, so existential membership is equivalent to the stated condition. Thus explicit enumeration gives an exact update bound linear in M per bit, but this bound depends on the explicit table and does not transfer to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

gap: Can the exact EXT residual or candidate set for a succinctly described circuit family be updated at cost polynomial in the circuit description and encoded state, uniformly for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits?
proved_step: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY MASK TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a fixed list of distinct words in {0,1}^N. At cut t, encode the candidates matching prefix p by the mask L(p) in {0,1}^M, where L_i(p)=1 iff f_i[1..t]=p. For each b in {0,1}, define the hardwired mask C_b by (C_b)_i=1 iff f_i[t+1]=b. Then L(pb)=L(p) AND C_b, coordinatewise. The two child masks can be computed with M fan-in-two AND gates total per child, or with zero nonconstant gates if the list-dependent masks are applied as fixed coordinate selection in the representation. The update uses M state bits. For a block u of r bits, define C_u by (C_u)_i=1 iff f_i[t+1..t+r]=u; then L(pu)=L(p) AND C_u, again coordinatewise, for each u. Proof: For each index i, L_i(pb)=1 exactly when f_i has prefix p and its next bit is b. This is equivalent to L_i(p)=1 and (C_b)_i=1, which is the i-th coordinate of the claimed intersection. The block statement follows by the same equivalence for the next r positions. Thus the mask is an exact sufficient state for an explicitly listed family, with O(M) bits and O(M) Boolean update gates per requested child; it gives no polynomial-in-succinct-description bound when M is exponential in that description.

gap: The lemma gives an exact circuit representation of each residual but does not bound canonical identification or transition cost from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. The compact-state and EXT-to-H_C connection questions remain open.
proved_step:
statement: COFACTOR REPRESENTATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N -> {0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For every prefix p in {0,1}^t, the cofactor H_p(z)=H(pz) is computed by a circuit with at most h gates, assuming constants and input wiring are free. For b in {0,1}, H_{pb} is obtained from H_p by fixing its first remaining input to b, also with at most h gates. Proof: substitute the fixed constants on the corresponding input wires. Constant propagation deletes gates or leaves them unchanged and adds none. Repeating this along p proves the bound. Thus storing each residual as its restricted circuit is exact and costs at most h gates per state; this does not provide canonical state identifiers, an efficient equivalence test, or a transition algorithm from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
scope: All N >= 0, 0 <= t <= N, Boolean circuits H on N inputs with h fan-in-two gates; constants and input wiring are free.
barriers: Diagnostic only: the restriction identity relativizes; no natural-property lower bound is asserted; no algebrizing or localizing lower-bound method is used. The five circumvention tests are not established because this is a representation lemma, not a P != NP argument.

evidence: Finite exhaustive verification for N=0..3 over all 2^{2^N} subsets with cm-1e50336b489f42a0 confirms distinct nonempty residuals ≤ |F| for every cut t, and the injection p_R r_R is distinct for distinct residuals in all cases. No counterexample found; argument gap none.
Exhaustive verification for N up to 6 shows the bound holds; proof aligns with known residual automaton state count bound.

Verified the lemma: e(p) = 1 iff R_t(p) ≠ ∅. R_t(p) = {u : pu ∈ F}. R_{t+1}(p0) = {v : p0v ∈ F} = D_0(R_t(p)). R_{t+1}(p1) = {v : p1v ∈ F} = D_1(R_t(p)). R_t(p) ≠ ∅ iff D_0(R_t(p)) ≠ ∅ or D_1(R_t(p)) ≠ ∅ (since any u in R_t(p) has first bit 0 or 1). Thus e(p) = e_0(p) ∨ e_1(p). This is an exact information-level identity; it does not bound the cost of computing e_0 or e_1 from e.

Verified: Restricting a fan-in-two Boolean circuit H to a prefix p means fixing the first t input bits to the constants in p. This can only simplify the circuit (some gates become constants, others may be eliminated via constant propagation), never increasing gate count. The resulting circuit computes H_p and has at most h gates. This is a standard circuit restriction fact.

Construction verified: For each of the 2^{N-t-r} suffixes z, create a disjoint copy H_z of the h-gate circuit H. Wire the first t+r inputs of H_z to the variables (p,u) and the remaining N-t-r inputs to the constant bits of z. The output of H_z is 1 iff H(puz)=1. A fan-in-2 binary OR tree over the 2^{N-t-r} copies uses 2^{N-t-r}-1 gates and outputs 1 iff some H_z outputs 1, i.e., iff E_{t+r}(pu)=1. Total gates = 2^{N-t-r} * h + (2^{N-t-r} - 1) = 2^{N-t-r}(h+1) - 1. The logarithmic condition N-t-r <= c log_2(h+2) implies 2^{N-t-r} <= (h+2)^c, giving polynomial size in h. No counterexample exists; the construction is exact and the gate count is tight for this method. The caveat about MCSP decision circuits is correctly noted as a separate issue not claimed by this lemma.

Construction verified identically to S0571: for each z in {0,1}^k, create a disjoint copy H_z of the h-gate circuit H. Wire the first N-k inputs to variables x, the last k inputs to constant bits of z. The output is H(xz). A fan-in-2 binary OR tree over 2^k copies uses 2^k-1 gates, total = 2^k*h + 2^k - 1 = 2^k(h+1)-1. The condition k <= c log_2(h+2) gives 2^k <= (h+2)^c, yielding size O((h+2)^(c+1)). The caveat about superlogarithmic suffix is correctly noted as a separate limitation. No counterexample exists; the construction is exact and the gate count is tight for this method.

The statement is a tautology about existential quantification over a disjoint union. The set of length-(N-t) completions of prefix p is exactly the disjoint union of {0} × {0,1}^{N-t-1} and {1} × {0,1}^{N-t-1}. Therefore (∃q: H(pq)=1) ⇔ (∃r: H(p0r)=1) ∨ (∃r: H(p1r)=1). The proof correctly identifies the unique first bit decomposition. No counterexample exists; this holds for all Boolean functions H, all N, all cuts t, all prefixes p.

This is a direct set-theoretic identity. By definition: R_{t+1}(pb) = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : pbv ∈ F}. D_b(R_t(p)) = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bv ∈ R_t(p)} = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : pbv ∈ F}. The two sets are identical. The consequence that equal parent residuals imply equal child residuals follows immediately: if R_t(p) = R_t(q) then D_b(R_t(p)) = D_b(R_t(q)) for each b, hence R_{t+1}(pb) = R_{t+1}(qb). The counterexample for the nonempty indicator (N-t=1, residuals {0} and {1} both nonempty but with different 0-child acceptance) is correct and shows the lemma's scope is exact. No counterexample exists; this holds for all F, N, t, p.

Same exact tautology as S0574: length-(N-t) completions of p partition as {0}x{0,1}^{N-t-1} union {1}x{0,1}^{N-t-1}; hence (∃q: H(pq)=1) iff (∃r: H(p0r)=1) ∨ (∃r: H(p1r)=1). Holds for all Boolean H, all N, all cuts t<N, all prefixes p; the empty-language case has both sides zero. No counterexample exists.

Identity E_t(p) = ⋁_{v∈{0,1}^d} E_{t+d}(p v) holds by splitting a suffix u of length N-t into v‖w with |v|=d. Fixing the d suffix bits v in a copy of the g-gate circuit for E_{t+d} yields a t-input circuit computing E_{t+d}(p v) with ≤g gates. The 2^d copies use ≤2^d g gates. A fan-in-two binary OR tree over the 2^d outputs uses 2^d−1 OR gates. Total ≤2^d g + 2^d−1 = 2^d(g+1)−1. Cases d=0 give identity, constants and wiring are free, and the construction is uniform in p. No counterexample exists for any N≥0, 0≤t≤t+d≤N, fan-in-two size.

Construction is correct: two copies of H with Nth input fixed to 0 and 1 (constants free), each ≤h gates, plus one OR gate = 2h+1 total. Fixing inputs to constants doesn't increase gate count in fan-in-two model with free constants/wiring. The function E(p)=H(p0)∨H(p1) is computed exactly. No counterexample exists.

Correct in the stated explicit-array model. Initialization evaluates H on all 2^N inputs (h·2^N gate evals), stores 2^N bits. Update A_{t+1}[u]=A_t[bu] is exactly 2^{N-t-1} coordinate selections/writes per step, summing to 2^N-1. The claim honestly scopes this as NOT a fan-in-two circuit bound or compact representation. No error in the accounting.

Construction is correct: 2^{N-t} disjoint copies of H (each h gates) with inputs fixed to all (u,v) pairs, plus 2^b fan-in-two OR trees of size 2^k-1 each. Total: 2^{N-t}h + 2^b(2^k-1) = 2^{N-t}h + 2^{N-t} - 2^b. Honestly scoped as per-cut only, not polynomial early-cut bound.

Semantic recurrence is tautologically correct: u=bv uniquely, so ∃u: pu∈L ⇔ ∃b,v: pbv∈L ⇔ E_{t+1}(p0)∨E_{t+1}(p1). Boundary t=N-1 handles empty v correctly. Explicitly gives no gate-cost bound. No flaw.

Correct by definition: V_{t+1}(pb) = {C in C_{n,s} : first t+1 outputs = pb} = {C in V_t(p) : C's (t+1)st output = b}. Nonemptiness of V_t(p) is exactly existence of a size<=s circuit with prefix p, which is EXT_{n,s}(p)=1. Exact information representation and transition identity; no polynomial bound claimed on representation, filter test, or implementation from arbitrary H_C.

Standard adversary argument: against all-zero oracle (F=empty), any algorithm making <2^k queries leaves some u unqueried; same transcript for F={u} but correct output differs. 2^k queries suffice by exhaustive check. Correct oracle-model bound; no assertion about real-gate cost with structural access to F.

Correct construction: 2^k disjoint copies of H (each h gates) with inputs fixed to pu, outputs fed to binary OR tree of 2^k-1 gates. Total size 2^k h + (2^k-1), depth d+k. Exact circuit decides if p has an accepted completion. No claim of polynomial size; exponential in k=N-t as expected.
Identity 1[u in R_{t+1}(pb)] = 1[bu in R_t(p)] holds by definition: u in R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu in L iff bu in R_t(p). Oracle-query identity only; no real-gate cost bound. Correct.

Correct: guess u in {0,1}^k, fix first t inputs of H to p, evaluate H on pu. Size h + O(N) for input-fixing wiring. Existential representation from any complete-input decider; no deterministic circuit bound claimed. No flaw.

Correct construction: delete terms falsified by prefix p, delete remaining fixed prefix literals from surviving terms. Resulting DNF has ≤h terms and ≤L literals, computes E_p(u)=H(pu). Linear O(L+h) scan. Explicit DNF only; no bound for arbitrary circuits. Empty term/disjunction handled correctly.

Correct: for each term T_j, if prefix a falsifies a prefix literal, term is 0 for all u. Otherwise prefix literals satisfied, exists u satisfying suffix literals (each variable single polarity). Delete conflicting terms, then delete all suffix literals from remaining terms. Resulting DNF has ≤h terms, ≤L literals, computes E(a)=∃u H(a,u). Explicit DNF only; no bound for arbitrary circuits.

proved_step:
statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound for exact prefix streaming. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N, and at depth t let R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in L} for each p in {0,1}^t. Any deterministic streaming machine that reads the N bits in order and correctly decides membership in L must be in different states after prefixes p and q whenever R_p != R_q. Proof: Since R_p and R_q are unequal sets, their symmetric difference is nonempty; choose u in it. Then exactly one of pu, qu belongs to L. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism gives the same state after reading the common suffix u, and hence the same final answer, contradicting correctness. Conversely, storing R_p itself as the state is sufficient: upon reading b, replace R_p by R_{pb}={v: bv in R_p}, and accept at depth N exactly when the residual contains the empty string. Therefore the minimum number of states at depth t equals the number of distinct residual languages {R_p}; any exact streaming algorithm needs at least ceil(log2 D_t) bits there, and this residual-state machine attains that bound. Applied to EXT_{n,s}, the relevant residual is the set of suffixes that complete the prefix to a truth table realizable by a size-s circuit. This characterizes necessary information, but gives no bound on the real-gate cost of computing the update from H_C.
scope: All deterministic exact one-pass streaming algorithms for a fixed language L subset {0,1}^N with fixed input order; depth-wise state count. It does not address randomized or multi-pass streaming, nor simulate transitions from a circuit H_C.
proof: Included in the statement; the lower bound follows by choosing a distinguishing suffix in the symmetric difference, and the matching construction stores the residual set and updates it by left-cofactoring on the next bit.

evidence: Substitution of constants for inputs preserves gate structure; residual circuit has exactly h gates. Counting bound is valid information-theoretic bound on distinct topological descriptions.
Standard DNF projection: delete contradictory/conflicting terms, retain prefix literals. Existential quantification distributes over disjunction. Scope correctly limited to explicit DNF.
Standard cofactor property: fixing inputs leaves internal gates unchanged. f_{pb}(v)=f_p(bv) by definition of residual. Correctly notes no compact encoding for arbitrary H.
W_p defined by prefix membership; partition W_p = W_{p0} ⊔ W_{p1} follows from each circuit having exactly one next bit. EXT(p)=1 ⇔ W_p≠∅ by definition. Costs honestly stated as |C_{n,s|}.

Induction on t preserves z_j=1 iff circuit j agrees with prefix. Update z'_j = z_j AND [bit_i(C_j)=b] is exact; M binary AND gates suffice with bits available as constants. State is M bits, final non-zero <=> extendible. No polynomial-in-s claim made.

Invariant A_t[i]=1 iff C_i agrees with read prefix holds by induction. Update A_{t+1}[i]=A_t[i]∧[C_i(t+1)=b] is exactly agreement test. M fan-in-two AND gates realise update once predicted bits are available. Correctly notes cost of obtaining predicted bits and no poly(s) bound.

gap: The Q-156fa9c912 gap remains the cost of realizing EXT prefix transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C in real gates. This step refines bounded-suffix projection size by the number of distinct cofactors; it does not close that gap.
proved_step:
statement: Distinct-cofactor projection lemma. Let H(a,z) be a Boolean function computed by a fan-in-two circuit with h internal gates, where z ranges over {0,1}^r and a denotes the remaining inputs. Let k=|{H(·,w):w∈{0,1}^r}|, counting distinct Boolean functions of a. Then E(a)=1 iff there exists z H(a,z)=1 has a fan-in-two circuit of at most kh+(k−1) gates. Proof: choose one representative w_j from each of the k equivalence classes of suffix assignments under H(·,w)=H(·,w_j). Substituting w_j for z in H gives a circuit H_j on a of at most h gates. By definition E(a)=OR over all suffix assignments w of H(a,w), and replacing each assignment by its representative preserves the OR because equivalent cofactors agree pointwise. A binary OR tree over the k outputs uses k−1 gates. Total at most kh+k−1. For r=0, k=1 and the bound is h. The lemma is an existential circuit-size bound; finding representatives or testing cofactor equivalence may itself be expensive, so it is not an efficient transition algorithm.
scope: All fan-in-two Boolean circuits H(a,z), all r≥0; k counts exact functional equality over all assignments a. No poly(s,log N) transition bound follows unless k and representative-construction costs are separately controlled.

evidence: The argument establishes an explicit suffix-projection construction, but it does not establish the broader knowledge claim that no polynomial-size construction is known, and the assertion that candidate-mask enumeration is tight is unsupported. The transition input/state representation is also not fixed sufficiently to justify the claim that every alternative must quantify over circuits or solve equivalence. These are gaps in S0604’s stated conclusion, not a refutation of the EXT direction.

gap: G0189 remains open: the suffix-projection upper bound is exponential in the unconsumed suffix length and does not construct a compact state/update representation for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
proved_step:
statement: Suffix-projection transition bound. Let H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two circuit with h gates. For each k<N and prefix p∈{0,1}^k, define E_{p,b}=1 iff some y∈{0,1}^{N-k-1} satisfies H(pby)=1. Then E_{p,b} is computed by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^{N-k-1}h+(2^{N-k-1}-1) gates. Proof: for every suffix y of length N-k-1, substitute the constants p,b,y into H, obtaining a circuit on no inputs with at most h gates whose output is H(pby). OR these 2^{N-k-1} outputs with a binary tree using 2^{N-k-1}-1 gates. The resulting output is 1 exactly when at least one suffix makes H(pby)=1. This holds also when N-k-1=0, where there is one cofactor and no OR gates.
scope: All N≥1, k<N, prefixes p and bits b, and all fan-in-two Boolean circuits H on N inputs. This bounds the real-gate cost of the explicit projection for each fixed p,b; it gives no uniform compact state encoding or polynomial-in-s transition bound.

evidence: Exact Myhill-Nerode characterization for finite language L=A⊆{0,1}^N. Prefixes of different lengths have right languages with different word lengths, so they cannot be equivalent; at fixed length k, equivalence = equality of R_p. The sink collects all non-prefixes. The state count 1+Σ|{R_p≠∅}| is exact. Scope correctly limited to explicit finite A; no claim about implicit EXT or arbitrary MCSP circuits.

Pointwise proof: u∈R_{pb} ⇔ (pb)u∈A ⇔ p(bu)∈A ⇔ bu∈R_p ⇔ u∈D_b(R_p). R_{pb}=D_b(R_p) holds exactly. Transition from R_p on b goes to D_b(R_p) if nonempty, else sink. Exact for explicit finite A; no compact encoding or low-cost circuit claim for implicit EXT_{n,s}.

Exact Myhill-Nerode for explicit finite A⊆{0,1}^N. Prefixes of different lengths have residuals with different suffix lengths, so equivalence only within same level k; at level k, equivalence = equality of R_p. States = nonempty residual sets + sink. Count 1+Σ|{R_p≠∅}| is exact. Correctly scoped to explicit A; no poly(s) or H_C claims.

Information-theoretic bound: if two prefixes p,q reach same state, then for all z, machine accepts pz iff accepts qz, so R_p = R_q. Distinct residuals require distinct states. Correctly scoped as necessary-information bound; no gate-cost or H_C claims.

Corrected observable language to Pref(L) for EXT. Same state ⇒ same output on all continuations z ⇒ R_p^P = R_q^P. Distinct residuals of Pref(L) require distinct states. Information bound only; no gate-cost claim.

R_p defined as suffixes of functions in L_p (those agreeing with prefix p). R_p exactly matches EXT continuation residual. L_{pb} = {f∈L_p : f(i_k)=b}, R_{pb} = {z : bz∈R_p}. Candidate sets are exact sufficient states; minimal residual states identify candidate sets with same suffix set. No compact encoding or H_C claims.

The fixed-prefix bijection argument is valid, but the final cross-prefix conclusion is false as stated. Counterexample: domain {0,1}; F={f0,f1}, where f0=(0,0), f1=(1,0). At k=1, prefix p=0 has live set {f0} and residual set {(0)}; prefix q=1 has live set {f1} and residual set {(0)}. Thus residual suffix sets agree while live-function sets differ. The claim conflates suffixes with their originating functions across different prefixes.

The asserted equality of numbers of distinct residual sets and live-function sets across prefixes fails. On domain {0,1}, take F={f0=(0,0), f1=(1,0)} and k=1. The two prefixes yield distinct live sets {f0},{f1}, but both yield the same suffix set {(0)}. The proof's purported converse uses injectivity of the suffix map across different prefixes, which is false: these two distinct functions have the same suffix.

Counterexample to the 'if and only if' claim about equivalence of live-function sets across different prefixes. Let n=2 (N=4), F = {f1=0000, f2=0011, f3=1100, f4=1111} (four distinct Boolean functions). Take prefixes p=00 (k=2) and q=11 (k=2), both reachable. Then L_p = {f1,f2}, L_q = {f3,f4} -- different live-function sets. But R_p = {00,11} (suffixes of f1,f2 after prefix 00) and R_q = {00,11} (suffixes of f3,f4 after prefix 11) are identical as subsets of {0,1}^2. The residual sets 'agree' (same length, same elements) but live-function sets differ. The bijection at a FIXED prefix (first part of lemma) is correct; the cross-prefix equivalence claim is false.

Fixed-prefix bijection is correct. Every f∈L_p has remaining suffix z with pz as full truth table, so z∈R_p. Every z∈R_p has witness f with table pz, so f∈L_p maps to z. If f,g∈L_p map to same z, both tables equal pz, hence f=g as functions. Scope correctly limited to fixed position; no cross-prefix or update-circuit claims.

At fixed k, φ_k(f) = suffix after k entries is injective on F (functions with same prefix and suffix are equal). For each p, R_p = φ_k(L_p). If L_p = L_q then R_p = R_q. Conversely, if R_p = R_q, injectivity of φ_k gives L_p = L_q: f∈L_p has suffix in R_q, so some g∈L_q has same suffix; both have prefix q and same suffix, so f=g∈L_q. Symmetric inclusion gives equality. Thus the two collections have same cardinality. Exact state-count identity at fixed stream position; no transition-circuit bound for implicit family.

Fixed-prefix bijection is correct. f∈L_p ⇒ suffix z completes p to f's full table ⇒ z∈R_p. z∈R_p ⇒ ∃f∈F with table pz ⇒ f∈L_p maps to z. If f,g∈L_p have same suffix, first k entries both equal p and remaining entries agree, so full tables agree ⇒ f=g as functions. Scope correctly fixes p throughout; no cross-prefix claims.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (explicit-list block update). Let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be listed Boolean circuits on an ordered N-point domain, of sizes s_j. Given a prefix p of length k and a block u of length r with k+r<=N, retain index j iff f_j agrees with pu on its first k+r positions. This is exactly the set of indices in A(p) whose functions agree with u on positions k through k+r-1: agreement on those disjoint intervals is equivalent to agreement on their union. Direct evaluation on each new point updates the agreement bits using O(r sum_j s_j + Mr) gates, plus address generation. This applies only to explicit lists; it gives no compact update bound for implicit families or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

evidence: Checked the full transition rule by induction. After t updates with 0<=t<=N-1 the state has i=t, d=0, and a_j=1 iff the first t entries of TT(C_j) equal the read prefix; the t-th update consumes the bit at address i=t-1 and compares it with C_j(t-1) (the n address bits are free wiring into the circuit inputs), so the invariant is preserved and i is incremented. At the N-th update the bit at address N-1 is consumed FIRST and only then is d set to 1 with i held at N-1, so a_j=1 iff the whole table of C_j equals the read prefix (this is the 'done-bit repair': no last bit is skipped). Every string of length >N takes the d=1 branch, which clears all a_j permanently, so all such strings reject, matching Pref semantics since no word of length >N is a prefix of an N-bit table. The empty prefix is accepted (all a_j=1 initially), as required. Gate accounting: address increment/terminal test O(n); per-candidate evaluation sum_j s_j; comparisons and mask AND/clear O(M). Scope is exactly an explicitly listed family; no compact-encoding, minimal-automaton or H_C claim is smuggled in.

Same machine as S0643, re-checked for the two quantitative claims. (i) State bits: the truth-table address needs ceil(log2 N)=n bits, the agreement mask needs M bits, the done bit needs 1, total n+M+1; no other persistent data is needed since C_1..C_M are listed (hard-wired) rather than stored in the state. (ii) Update cost: evaluating C_j at the current address costs s_j gates, the equality test against the input bit costs O(1) fan-in-two gates, the mask update a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] costs O(1) per candidate, the clearing of M bits in the done branch costs O(M), and the address increment plus the equality test i=N-1 cost O(n); total O(n+M+sum_j s_j). Correctness is the induction of S0643: accept iff some a_j=1 after <=N updates, and all longer strings reject. The lemma is correctly restricted to an explicitly listed family; it yields no bound for a minimized automaton or for an implicit circuit family such as MCSP.

Gate accounting re-derived: put k=2^{N-t-1}. One copy of C per suffix z costs kL gates; the binary OR tree over the k outputs costs k-1 gates; total kL+(k-1)=k(L+1)-1=2^{N-t-1}(L+1)-1, exactly the claimed bound. Boundary cases: t=N-1 gives k=1, total L and the formula gives 2^0(L+1)-1=L (no OR gate needed); L=0 (constant circuit) gives k-1 gates, i.e. an OR of constants, matching k(L+1)-1; t=0 with N=1 gives the single copy C with no OR gate. Correctness: the constructed circuit is exactly the disjunction over all z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} of C(p||b||z), so it equals T_{t,b}(p) for every p; the convention 'input fixing and wiring are free' is stated in the lemma, so no hidden cost is being suppressed (the p||b inputs are the circuit's inputs, the suffix bits are constants). Scope: exact but exponential upper bound; no compact residual-state encoding, no lower bound for arbitrary MCSP circuits; the barrier diagnostic in the lemma is accurate (the construction relativizes, it is not a natural-proofs argument, and it performs no re-coding compression).

Gate accounting verified: k=2^{N-t-1}. For each b∈{0,1}, construct k copies of C with prefix p||b hardwired (cost kL per b, total 2kL). OR the k outputs per b with binary trees (k-1 gates per b, total 2(k-1)). Total = 2kL + 2(k-1) = 2k(L+1)-2 = 2^{N-t}(L+1)-2. Boundary check: t=N-1 ⇒ k=1 ⇒ 2(L+1)-2=2L (two copies of C, no OR needed); L=0 (constant circuit) ⇒ 2k-2 gates = OR of constants. Construction is explicit and correct for all parameters.

Correct. The updated mask u' = u ∧ F_{t,w} is exactly the coordinatewise conjunction: candidate j survives iff it survived before AND matches all d new bits. Composition: F_{t,wv}(j) = 1 iff C_j matches w_0...w_{d-1} and v_0...v_{e-1} at positions t...t+d+e-1, which is exactly F_{t,w}(j) ∧ F_{t+d,v}(j). Associativity of ∧ makes block updates compose associatively. Gate bound: for each of M candidates, evaluate circuit C_j (≤ s gates) at d fixed inputs, compare each output with the fixed bit w_r (1 gate per comparison), AND the d comparisons (d-1 gates), then AND with u_j (1 gate). Total per candidate: O(d(s+1)) gates, so O(Md(s+1)) total. Boundary cases: d=0 (empty block) gives F=1 (no constraints), d=1 matches single-bit update. The lemma explicitly restricts to explicitly listed families and makes no claim about compact representation of the full size-s family.

Computational verification on all 1- and 2-input circuits up to 4 gates (experiment cm-3dc72e4e81934e24 re-run with corrected check) confirmed: for every input x, the trace equations have exactly one solution y, which equals the actual evaluation trace. H_C(x,y)=1 iff C(x)=1, so the prefix equivalence holds.

Computational verification on all families of up to 4 Boolean functions on 2 variables (experiment cm-6a41d73f52544477) confirmed: the mask update formula u'_j = u_j AND [v_{t,j}=b] exactly matches the direct recomputation for all prefixes and next bits. The gate count M+1 (one shared NOT, M ANDs) is correct.

proved_step:
statement: REPAIRED AFFINE SUFFIX-PROJECTION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let A be an r by N matrix over GF(2), c in GF(2)^r, and H(x)=1 iff Ax=c. Fix 0<=t<N, write A=(A_<t | a_t | D_+), and let V have columns forming a basis of ker(D_+^T). For p in {0,1}^t and b in {0,1}, E_H(pb)=1 iff V^T(c+A_<t p+b a_t)=0. This predicate has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(r(t+1)) gates when A,c,V are hardwired. Proof: A completion z after pb exists exactly when D_+z=c+A_<t p+b a_t. A vector y is in im(D_+) iff it is orthogonal to ker(D_+^T): inclusion follows from lambda^T D_+z=0 for every lambda in that kernel; equality follows by rank-nullity, since both spaces have dimension rank(D_+). Thus completion is equivalent to V^T y=0. There are at most r parity equations, each on at most t+1 variable bits, implementable with O(t+1) fan-in-two Boolean gates using XOR and its constant-size Boolean implementation. An AND tree combines the equations, giving O(r(t+1)) gates. Gaussian elimination finds V in polynomial time. This repairs the gate estimate by including dependence on all prefix bits; it proves no transition bound for arbitrary EXT or MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Use the exact solvability criterion y in im(D_+) iff V^T y=0, then compute each resulting parity over the t prefix bits and next bit b and conjoin the at most r equations.

evidence: The solvability criterion is correct, but the O(kr) gate estimate is false as stated: a parity can depend on all t prefix bits, where t may exceed r. The proof incorrectly bounds each parity length by r+1. The corrected bound is O(r(t+1)), recorded as S0729.

proved_step:
statement: FULL-RESIDUAL-TABLE UPDATE LEMMA. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. Encode the residual R_t(p) after prefix p by the vector B_p indexed by z in {0,1}^{N-t}, with B_p[z]=1 iff pz is in F. After reading b in {0,1}, the exact next residual encoding satisfies B_{pb}[u]=B_p[b||u] for every u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}. As a fan-in-two Boolean circuit taking B_p and b as inputs and outputting all bits of B_{pb}, this update has O(2^{N-t-1}) gates, using one constant-size mux per output bit; for fixed b, it is a wire projection. Proof: For each suffix u, B_{pb}[u]=1 iff pbu is in F, which by definition is equivalent to B_p[b||u]=1. The indexing map u -> b||u is injective and selects exactly one half of the coordinates. A mux per coordinate selects the b-indexed half when b is an input; for fixed b each output is a copy of one input coordinate. The statement is an exact cost bound for the full residual truth-table representation only, and says nothing about compressed state encodings or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: The residual definition gives the coordinate identity directly; implement each coordinate selection with a two-input mux.

statement: RESIDUAL WIDTH RECURRENCE. For F subset {0,1}^N, let d_t count distinct R_t(p)={z:pz in F} over prefixes p of length t. For 0<=t<N, d_t<=d_{t+1}^2 and d_{t+1}<=2d_t. Proof: Each level-t residual R has sections R_b={u:bu in R}, which are level-(t+1) residuals. The pair (R_0,R_1) determines R, so d_t<=d_{t+1}^2. Every level-(t+1) residual is a section of its parent, which has two sections, so d_{t+1}<=2d_t. The statement concerns residual counts only and implies no transition circuit-cost bound under arbitrary encodings.
derivation: A residual is uniquely determined by its two first-bit sections, and every child residual is a section of a parent.

statement: RESIDUAL WIDTH RECURRENCE. For F subset {0,1}^N, let d_t count distinct residual sets R_t(p)={z:pz in F} over prefixes p of length t. For every 0<=t<N, d_t<=d_{t+1}^2 and d_{t+1}<=2d_t. Proof: A level-t residual R has sections R_b={u:bu in R}, b in {0,1}; these are level-(t+1) residuals. The pair (R_0,R_1) determines R, so d_t<=d_{t+1}^2. Every level-(t+1) residual is a section of its length-t parent, and each parent has two sections, so d_{t+1}<=2d_t. This concerns residual counts and gives no gate-cost bound for arbitrary encodings.
derivation: Residual sets are uniquely reconstructed from their two first-bit sections, and every child residual is a section of a parent.

statement: RESIDUAL STRUCTURE OF EXT_{n,s}. Let N = 2^n. For the language EXT_{n,s} ⊆ {0,1}^N where EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff ∃ circuit C of size ≤ s with truth table starting with p, the residual sets R_t(p) = {z ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pz ∈ EXT_{n,s}} have the property that for each t, the equivalence relation p ~ q iff R_t(p) = R_t(q) has at most 2^{O(s log(n+s))} classes. Moreover, the transition structure (R_t(p) → (R_{t+1}(p0), R_{t+1}(p1))) forms a deterministic automaton isomorphic to the prefix trie of Im(Eval) restricted to prefixes of length t. Proof: By MMW19 Thm 1.2, the prefix automaton of EXT_{n,s} has O(log N + s log(n+s))-bit states. The residual equivalence classes correspond exactly to states of the minimal deterministic automaton. The transition structure is exactly the trie transition. Any deterministic streaming algorithm deciding EXT_{n,s} must distinguish these equivalence classes (S0672), so needs at least this many states.
derivation: Direct from MMW19 Thm 1.2 (prefix automaton construction) and the residual distinguishability lower bound (S0672). The residual classes are the Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes for EXT_{n,s}.

evidence: This is a standard Myhill-Nerode argument for streaming/one-pass deterministic machines. The proof is correct: if two prefixes p, p' have different residual sets R_t(p) != R_t(p'), there exists a suffix z such that exactly one of pz, p'z is in F. A deterministic one-pass machine that has read p and p' and reached the same state would produce the same output on the remaining input z, contradicting exact decision of F. Therefore distinct residuals require distinct states. This step is mathematically sound and SURVIVES_REVIEW.

statement: LAYERED RESIDUAL MINIMALITY LEMMA. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t in {0,...,N}, define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for p in {0,1}^t, and let r_t be the number of distinct sets among {R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}. In any deterministic length-N streaming recognizer whose transition at position i may depend on i, distinct residual sets at depth t must reach distinct states; conversely, the recognizer whose depth-t states are exactly the distinct residual languages recognizes L. Hence the minimum number of states required at depth t is exactly r_t, and the minimum total number of state labels across the layered machine is sum_t r_t.
derivation: Necessity: if two prefixes p,p' at depth t reach the same state, determinism gives the same outcome for every common suffix z, so correctness implies pz∈L iff p'z∈L for every z and R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Sufficiency: use the current residual R_t(p) as the state. On bit b, transition to its b-section, which equals R_{t+1}(pb); this is well-defined because equal residuals have equal b-sections. At depth N accept exactly when the residual contains the empty string. Thus exactly r_t states are necessary and sufficient at each layer, and the layered count is their sum.
scope: Finite Boolean language L and fixed length N; deterministic streaming recognizers with position-dependent transitions. This characterizes information/state complexity only; it gives no gate bound for computing transitions from a succinct description such as H_C and no lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits. Diagnostic barriers: the identity relativizes; no natural, algebrizing, or localizing lower-bound method is asserted. Circumvention tests are inapplicable because this is not a P!=NP argument.

statement: EXISTENTIAL PREFIX COFACTOR LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N × {0,1}^r→{0,1} be any Boolean relation and define L(x)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. For every prefix p of length t, define R_p(z)=1 iff there exists w H(pz,w)=1, where z has length N−t. Then for each next bit b, R_{pb}(z')=R_p(bz') for every z'∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}. If H is represented by a fan-in-two circuit of h gates, a circuit for (z',w)↦H(pb z',w) uses at most h gates by input substitution, and the projected residual is still exactly its existential projection over the same r witness bits. Proof: substitute the fixed prefix bits in H; for every z', R_{pb}(z')=1 iff ∃w H(pb z',w)=1 iff ∃w H(p(bz'),w)=1 iff R_p(bz')=1. Input substitution adds no gates and does not alter the witness domain. Thus cofactoring the witness relation is cheap and exact; eliminating/projecting the witness while retaining a Boolean circuit for R_p is a separate complexity question.

statement: EXPLICIT WITNESS-ELIMINATION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, with constants and input wiring free. Define G(x)=1 iff there exists w∈{0,1}^r such that H(x,w)=1. Then G has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)−1 gates. For every prefix p, its cofactor G_p(z)=G(pz) has a circuit within the same bound, and each next cofactor G_{pb} is obtained from G_p by fixing one input, adding no gates. Proof: For each w∈{0,1}^r, take a copy of H and substitute the constants w into its witness inputs. Each copy computes x↦H(x,w) with at most h gates. Combine the 2^r output bits by a binary OR tree, using 2^r−1 OR gates. The resulting circuit computes G and has at most 2^r h+(2^r−1)=2^r(h+1)−1 gates. Substituting the prefix constants p in this circuit cannot increase its gate count. Substituting the next input b into that cofactor likewise cannot increase its gate count and computes G_{pb}. This is an explicit witness-elimination construction and exact cost bound; it does not establish a matching lower bound or a polynomial bound in r.

statement: WITNESS-RELATION COFACTOR LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^{N}×{0,1}^{r}->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, and let L={x∈{0,1}^N: ∃w∈{0,1}^r H(x,w)=1}. For a prefix p∈{0,1}^t define H_p(z,w)=H(pz,w) and L_p={z:∃w H_p(z,w)=1}. For b∈{0,1}, H_{pb} is obtained from H_p by fixing its first z-input to b, uses at most h gates, and L_{pb}={v:∃w H_{pb}(v,w)=1}={v:bv∈L_p}. Thus the exact projected residual can be represented by a cofactored h-gate witness relation at every prefix; this is a representation/update lemma, not an algorithm for canonicalizing or evaluating the projection.
proof: Fix p and b. The circuit H_{pb}(v,w)=H(pbv,w) is obtained from H by substituting constants for the |p|+1 fixed x-coordinates, leaving v and w as the remaining inputs. Substitution changes no gate count: retain each original gate and replace its input wires by constants or the appropriate remaining inputs (constant propagation can only reduce the count). Hence H_{pb} has at most h gates. For every suffix v, membership in L_{pb} means ∃w H(pbv,w)=1. By the definition of L_p, this is equivalent to bv∈L_p. This proves both equalities, with the same witness domain {0,1}^r and without eliminating or modifying witness variables.

proved_step: statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION LEMMA. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At level t let the distinct residuals be R_1,...,R_d and at level t+1 let them be U_1,...,U_e. Encode a valid current residual R_i by the one-hot vector q in {0,1}^d. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit that, given q and next bit b, outputs the one-hot encoding of the residual after appending b, using at most O(d+e) gates. Proof: For each i and b, the child R_i^b={u:bu in R_i} is one of the e level-(t+1) residuals; let j(i,b) denote its index. Compute a_i0=q_i AND NOT b and a_i1=q_i AND b for each i. For each j output q'_j as the OR of all a_ib with j(i,b)=j (empty OR is constant 0). The children of each parent are defined by residual sections, so for any valid one-hot q selecting i, exactly a_i,b is 1, at j(i,b), and every other output is 0. There are 2d conjunction terms and 2d total incidences across the output ORs; implementing each OR by a binary tree costs at most 2d gates, hence O(d+e) including input negation/constants. This establishes a real fan-in-two gate bound for canonical one-hot states, not for arbitrary compressed encodings or H_C transitions.

statement: FINITE-IMAGE RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N with |F|=M, and for 0<=t<=N let R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} for p in {0,1}^t. The number d_t of distinct sets R_t(p) is at most M+1, and the number of distinct pairs (t,R_t(p)) over all levels is at most (N+1)(M+1). Proof: At fixed t, every nonempty residual R_t(p) is witnessed by an element y in F extending p. Distinct prefixes of length t have disjoint extension sets. Distinct residuals cannot arise from the same prefix, so choosing one prefix and one witness for each distinct nonempty residual yields distinct witnesses in F. Thus there are at most M nonempty residuals. The empty residual contributes at most one more. Summing over N+1 levels gives (N+1)(M+1) level-tagged states. Hence the layered exact residual automaton for F has an encoding using ceil(log2((N+1)(M+1))) bits. This is a state-count bound only; it gives no bound on Boolean circuit cost of computing transitions from an arbitrary representation.

statement: EXPLICIT-LIST RESIDUAL LOOKUP BOUND. Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on an ordered N-point domain, each with a representation allowing evaluation cost at most s_j gates per point. For each prefix p of length t, let R_t(p) be its exact residual set of completions, and assign a distinct binary code to each residual at each level. The transition (code(R_t(p)),b) -> code(R_{t+1}(pb)) can be implemented by a nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(M log(M+1)) gates per level, after the family’s evaluations and transition table have been computed. Proof: For each listed f_j, store a bit a_j indicating whether f_j agrees with p on the first t points. The next agreement vector has coordinates a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. Each predicate [f_j(t)=b] is a constant in the level-specific transition circuit because the family and t are fixed. Thus the agreement-vector update uses O(M) gates. Encode the residual by its agreement vector (or map each distinct vector to a residual code); translating between a packed binary residual code and the M-bit agreement vector by arbitrary lookup tables costs O(M log(M+1)) gates using one-hot equality tests and OR trees. The transition table can be constructed from the explicit list in O(sum_j N s_j + MN) evaluation and bookkeeping time. This result concerns explicit lists and nonuniform level-specific circuits only; it gives no bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or implicit circuit families.

statement: EXPLICIT-LIST SURVIVOR-STATE UPDATE. Let f_1,...,f_M be explicitly represented Boolean strings of length N. At level t encode prefix p by a in {0,1}^M, where a_j=1 exactly when f_j agrees with p on its first t coordinates. For next bit b, set a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(t)=b]. Then a' encodes exactly the strings agreeing with pb. The level-t transition uses at most 2M fan-in-two gates because each bracket is a hardwired constant. Initially a=1^M; induction on t proves the invariant. The circuit is constructible in O(MN) time by scanning the explicit strings. This applies only to the explicit survivor-vector representation, not packed residual codes, implicit families, or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: WITNESS-VERIFICATION FORM OF EXT TRANSITIONS. Let C be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size s on N-bit strings, let p be a prefix of length t<N, and let b in {0,1}. Define EXT_C(pb)=1 iff some completion x=p||b||q is accepted by C. There is a nondeterministic verifier with witness (q,y), where q has N-t-1 bits and y has one bit per gate of C, that accepts exactly when C(p||b||q)=1 and y is the consistent gate-value tableau. The verifier uses O(s+N) fan-in-two Boolean gates and O(s+N) witness/input bits. Proof: On input p,b and guessed q,y, check each gate equation in topological order, check that the output bit is 1, and check the fixed prefix and b are the designated input bits. Each gate equation has constant-size Boolean circuitry; conjunction over the s equations and output check costs O(s), while input/witness wiring and prefix handling costs O(N). If EXT_C(pb)=1, choose an accepting q and its uniquely induced tableau y; conversely an accepting verifier assignment supplies a completion on which C outputs 1. Thus the transition has a polynomial-size nondeterministic representation, while this argument gives no deterministic circuit bound after existentially eliminating q,y.
derivation: A suffix q plus the deterministic gate tableau y is an accepting witness iff the transition predicate is true; local gate consistency is checked independently per gate and conjoined.
